issues.title: Vestigial sequenceStart in MissionRuntime computes colliding ids (trap for a plausible refactor)
issues.description:
> ⚠️ **This issue was rewritten 2026-07-24.** The original description said the bug was latent *"because the golden fixture uses ticks 0 and 1 — different ticks."* **That reasoning was wrong.** Two fixtures with real goldens DO schedule same-tick events. The bug is latent for a different reason, and the original text could have led a fixer to *activate* it. See the correction comment.

## Current state: computed, then discarded twice. Nothing is broken today.

`MissionRuntime` computes collision-prone sequence ids, but they never reach the code that would collide:

| Step | Evidence |
| -- | -- |
| Harness hardcodes `sequenceStart: 0` | `BalticReplayHarness.cs:347` |
| Emission id = `sequenceStart + emissions.Count` → 0, 1, 2, 3… | `MissionRuntime.cs:32` |
| Harness passes the **record only** — factory's `sequenceId` param defaults to 0 | `BalticReplayHarness.cs:352-370` → `OrderLogEntryFactories.cs:36,39` — `FromMissionTransition(record, ulong sequenceId = 0)` |
| `OrderLogEntry.SequenceId` is therefore always 0 → auto-assign | `DecisionLog.cs:72` |
| The record's buggy value is **overwritten** | `DecisionLog.cs:112,117` — `mission with { SequenceId = sequenceId }` |

**Empirically confirmed** in `tests/regression/replay-golden-baltic-v3-mission-band-b-2026-06-25.txt`:

```
EventFired|4|1|1|recon-passive|recon_passive_start
MissionTransition|5|1|1|start-exec|Execution
```

Sequential ids 4 and 5 — correctly assigned, not the colliding 0/1.

## ⛔ The actual risk: an inviting refactor activates it

Fixtures **do** exercise the same-tick path — verified:

| Fixture | Event ticks | Has golden |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `baltic-v3-mission-band-b.policy.json` | **{0: 2 events, 1: 2 events}** | ✅ |
| `baltic-v3-mission-roe-band-c.policy.json` | **{0: 2 events, 1: 2 events}** | ✅ |
| `baltic-v2-contact-window-arc.policy.json` | same-tick dups | no |
| `baltic-v2-narrative-arc.policy.json` | same-tick dups | no |

So if anyone "tidies the plumbing" by wiring `emission.SequenceId` into the factory's `sequenceId` parameter — which looks like an obvious unused-value fix — the collision goes **live immediately against two golden-backed fixtures**, silently corrupting the replay fingerprint.

**Do not wire** `emission.SequenceId` **through to** `OrderLogEntryFactories`**.**

## Recommended fix

The `sequenceStart` parameter on `MissionRuntime.Tick` is **vestigial** — its output is discarded on every path. Prefer deleting it (and the `SequenceId` field on the emission) over plumbing it through, so the trap cannot be sprung. `DecisionLog` is already the single authority for sequence assignment.

Add a guard test regardless: append 2+ same-tick mission events **through the production factory calls** into a real `DecisionLog`, and assert no duplicate `SequenceId` and correct chronological placement. The existing `MissionRuntimeTests.Fire_order_same_tick_respects_locked_order` only checks `MissionRuntime.Tick`'s in-memory return value and never touches `DecisionLog`.

Also worth adding: `design/gdd/order-log-replay.md` specifies *"Duplicate* `sequenceId` *… Assert fail in debug; reject in release"* — **no such assertion exists** in `DecisionLog.Append`. That missing guard is why this class of bug would fail silently rather than loudly.

## Surface

`src/ProjectAegis.Delegation/Mission/MissionRuntime.cs` · `src/ProjectAegis.Delegation.UnityAdapter/Baltic/BalticReplayHarness.cs` · `src/ProjectAegis.Delegation/Decision/OrderLogEntryFactories.cs` · `src/ProjectAegis.Delegation/Decision/DecisionLog.cs`

⚠️ `DecisionLog` is CRITICAL (341 impacted). Run `impact()` before editing; keep this separate from <issue id="bd271fba-768c-4132-97ca-442e01b02875" label="DRG-48" href="https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-48/req-02-mission-runtime-system-9-no-gdd-no-adr" />'s documentation work.

*Verified by direct source and golden-fixture inspection, 2026-07-24.*

issues.title: [ADR-022] Target OS and CPU architectures (v1) — Accepted
issues.description:
## ADR-022 — Target Operating Systems and CPU Architectures (v1)

* **Status:** Accepted (2026-07-25)
* **Renumbered 2026-07-26:** issued as ADR-018; that number was already taken by `adr-018-sensor-side-picture-datalink.md`. See §Renumbering.
* **Git source of truth:** `docs/architecture/adr-022-target-os-and-cpu-architectures.md` — ⚠️ not yet committed to any branch
* **Product NFR:** `Game-Requirements/requirements/01-Project-Overview.md` (platforms decided 2026-06-09)

### Summary

Project Aegis v1 ships an **interactive client on Windows 10/11 x64** (Steam primary) and runs **headless sim / batch / CI on Linux x64**. The managed core (`ProjectAegis.Data`, `.Sim`, `.Delegation`) is **host-agnostic**. **x64 only** for v1. **macOS, ARM64, console, Steam Deck, and Linux interactive player** are out of scope.

### Supported host matrix

| Role | OS | Arch |
| -- | -- | -- |
| Interactive player (Steam) | Windows 10/11 | x64 |
| Headless farm / AvA / CI | Linux | x64 |
| Local dev (optional) | Windows or Linux | x64 |

### Explicit non-goals (v1)

* macOS player or headless gate
* Windows/Linux/Apple ARM64 as ship or required CI
* Steam Deck, consoles
* Linux interactive Steam player
* Multi-arch fat binaries

### Architecture rules

1. **No OS-conditioned sim rules** in Data / Sim / Delegation.
2. Presentation and packaging may be OS-specific (Unity StandaloneWindows64 player).
3. **Cross-OS determinism:** InvariantCulture; BCL path APIs; ordered filesystem iteration; no wall-clock in sim; quantized floats in fingerprints; ADR-008 validation parity; Baltic hash host-independent.
4. Authoritative CI host: **Linux x64** (Buildkite).
5. Reopening non-goals requires **ADR amendment + product re-decision**.

### Renumbering (2026-07-26)

Originally ADR-018. Collided with `docs/architecture/adr-018-sensor-side-picture-datalink.md` (<issue id="5dff175d-4399-4ee1-9610-91f6db842583" label="DRG-43" href="https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-43/req-15-sensor-side-picture-datalink-tr-sensor-004-gap" />), committed `2abea6f` on 2026-07-25 and carried in PR #339.

Resolved per this ADR's own stated rule — *"Git remains source of truth; Linear/Notion are mirrors"* — so the ADR that exists in git kept **018** and this one moved to **022**.

Numbers now claimed: **018** sensor side picture / datalink · **019** agentic AAR read-only order log · **020** logistics fuel model · **021** mission timeline runtime · **022** this ADR. ADR-012 remains a known numbering gap.

### ⚠️ Open action

**This ADR does not exist as a file in any branch.** It is currently Linear + Notion only — the same shape as the stranded-artifact problem tracked in <issue id="0142ebcc-cd8d-4c8f-b1b5-c185d1f58c3e" label="DRG-42" href="https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-42/restore-or-retire-2-never-committed-governance-artifacts-2026-07-14" />. To become a real decision of record it must be committed as `docs/architecture/adr-022-target-os-and-cpu-architectures.md` and linked from `architecture-traceability-index.md`.

### Related

* ADR-001, ADR-006, ADR-008, ADR-010, ADR-011
* `docs/engineering/buildkite-ci.md`

Docs-only codification of existing practice. Git remains source of truth; Linear/Notion are mirrors for navigation and delivery tracking.

issues.title: [ADR-022] Target OS and CPU architectures (v1) — Accepted (duplicate of DRG-51)
issues.description:
## Summary

**ADR-018: Target Operating Systems and CPU Architectures (v1)** is **Accepted** (2026-07-25). Architecture enforcement of the product NFR decided 2026-06-09 in `Game-Requirements/requirements/01-Project-Overview.md`.

Project Aegis v1 ships an **interactive client on Windows 10/11 x64** (Steam primary) and runs **headless sim / batch / CI on Linux x64**. The managed core (`ProjectAegis.Data`, `.Sim`, `.Delegation`) is **host-agnostic**. **x64 only** for v1 ship and gate hosts.

> **Git is the source of truth.** This Linear issue is a tracking mirror only. Do not treat Linear as authoritative over the repo ADR.

## Decision matrix (v1)

| Role | OS | Arch |
| -- | -- | -- |
| Interactive player (Steam) | Windows 10/11 | x64 |
| Headless farm / AvA / CI | Linux | x64 |
| Local dev (optional) | Windows or Linux | x64 |

CI authoritative host: **Linux x64** (Buildkite). Player packaging target: **StandaloneWindows64** only for v1 commercial path.

## Non-goals (out of v1)

* macOS (player or headless gate)
* ARM64 (Windows / Linux / Apple Silicon) as ship or required CI
* Console
* Steam Deck
* Linux interactive player (Linux is headless/batch only)
* Multi-arch fat binaries / universal builds

Reopening any non-goal requires a **new ADR or amendment** plus product re-decision in req 01.

## Host-agnostic core rule

```
Ship: Windows x64 player          Farm/CI: Linux x64 headless
Unity presentation + C2           dotnet CLI / batch / tests
              \                         /
               v                       v
        Host-agnostic managed core
        ProjectAegis.Data · Sim · Delegation
        (no UnityEngine; no OS-dependent sim rules)
```

1. **No OS-conditioned sim rules.** `#if WINDOWS` / `#if LINUX` (or runtime OS checks) must not change engagement, policy, sensors, logistics, RNG, or order-log semantics.
2. Presentation and packaging may be OS-specific.
3. Adapter layer (`UnityAdapter`) may use Unity APIs; it must not redefine world truth.

## Cross-OS determinism (architecture law)

* **Culture:** InvariantCulture for goldens, fingerprints, Excel, scenario JSON (see ADR-011).
* **Paths:** BCL path APIs only (`Path.Combine`, etc.); no hardcoded `\` or `/` in core logic.
* **Filesystem:** Ordered, deterministic enumeration — never rely on directory order.
* **Time:** No wall-clock in sim paths; injectable clocks only.
* **No OS-conditioned sim rules** in Data / Sim / Delegation.
* **Validation parity** (ADR-008): same fixture → same `ValidationReport` semantics across Linux and Windows when both are exercised.
* **Replay hash:** Production Baltic hash invariant unchanged; host OS must not diverge hash without a golden ADR.

## Source of truth

* **Repo path:** `docs/architecture/adr-018-target-os-and-cpu-architectures.md`
* **Status:** Accepted (2026-07-25)
* **Product NFR:** `Game-Requirements/requirements/01-Project-Overview.md` (2026-06-09)

## Related ADRs

* **ADR-001** — Sim assembly boundary (engine-free Sim)
* **ADR-006** — Data layer boundary (engine-free Data)
* **ADR-008** — Mission editor validation (cross-host determinism)
* **ADR-010** — Headless-first command-driven UI
* **ADR-011** — Platform Editor Excel round-trip (InvariantCulture)

## Work type

Docs-only architecture decision already accepted in git. No implementation work remaining for this ADR record itself. Remaining validation items (packaging checklist cite, spot-check core for OS gates) are ongoing review gates — see ADR Validation Criteria in the repo file.

issues.title: Buildkite fails at 0s on every build — main and all PRs blocked
issues.description:
**Every Buildkite build fails in \~0 seconds with no step logs.** `buildkite/cmano-clone` is the sole required status check on `main` — enforced by **both** classic branch protection *and* the "Protect main branch" ruleset — so **nothing can merge**. 18 open PRs and `main` itself are blocked.

## Evidence it is infrastructure, not content

| Build | Commit | Date | Result |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| **#880** | `a73f722` | 2026-07-17 | **passed, 1m39s** |
| **#929** | `03e91df` | 2026-07-25 | **failed, \~0s** |

The **entire delta between those two commits is 4 markdown files, +292 lines, zero code** (PR #340). Build #929 was created and failed in the same second — 11:38:29Z, 4s after the merge.

On that same commit, GitHub Actions `oracle` **passed in 57s**. Actions is healthy; the fault is isolated to Buildkite.

## What this rules out

* **Not PR-specific** — `main` fails too, so the `gitnexus-pr` step's `if: build.pull_request.id != null` condition cannot be the cause; that step never runs on `main`
* **Not repository content** — `main` was green at `a73f722` with an identical pipeline
* **Not GitHub Actions** — `oracle` passes on the same commit

Something **outside the repository** changed after **2026-07-17 18:48 UTC**.

## Remaining hypotheses (need Buildkite org access)

1. **Hosted-agent quota exhausted or billing lapsed** — the most common cause of instant, universal failure
2. **Cluster removed or reconfigured** — `.buildkite/pipeline.yml` sets no `agents:` queue targeting, so it depends on a default queue; a renamed or deleted cluster fails every build to schedule
3. **Pipeline "read steps from repo" changed** — `docs/engineering/buildkite-ci.md` attributes a \~3s no-log failure to *pipeline upload rejection*

## Next step

Open [**build #929**](<https://buildkite.com/drgaciw/cmano-clone/builds/929>) — the cleanest possible case: known-good pipeline, four markdown files, instant failure on `main`. The error text should name the cause outright.

API triage (`/builds/929`, `/builds/929/jobs`, `/pipelines/cmano-clone`, `/organizations/drgaciw/agents`) covers hypotheses 1–3. **Billing is org-admin UI only** and is not exposed on the REST API.

## Impact / workaround

PR #340 merged on 2026-07-25 only by temporarily removing the required check from **both** protection mechanisms, then restoring them immediately (verified byte-identical to backup). That is a workaround, not a fix — every future merge needs the same manual intervention until this is resolved.

## Local gate is green

Release build 0 errors/0 warnings, **1792 tests pass**, ReplayGolden 6/6, PlayModeSmoke 21/21. Nothing in the repository is broken.

issues.title: Scenario policy loaders enumerate unordered and silently overwrite duplicate ids
issues.description:
Found by the **ADR-022 OS-gated sim spot-check** (2026-07-26). Two defects in the same two call sites — one latent and cross-OS, one platform-independent.

## Sites

* `src/ProjectAegis.Data/Scenario/Policy/ScenarioPolicyJsonIndex.cs:26`
* `src/ProjectAegis.Sim/Scenario/ScenarioPolicyJsonLoader.cs:32`

Both:

```csharp
foreach (var file in Directory.EnumerateFiles(directoryPath, "*.policy.json"))
{
    // ...
    map[dto.Id] = dto;   // silent last-writer-wins
}
```

## Defect 1 — unordered enumeration (violates ADR-022 Decision 3)

`Directory.EnumerateFiles` returns filesystem-dependent order: roughly alphabetical on NTFS, inode/hash order on ext4. <pull-request id="181a547e-6e88-43a4-9d07-981437c7f22b" label="drgaciw/cmano-clone#339" href="https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/review/docsfeat-linear-as-delivery-tracker-4-adrs-mission-runtime-gdd-a131283fd28e" /> Decision 3 requires *"ordered, deterministic enumeration; never rely on directory order."*

Order only reaches the output through `map[dto.Id] = dto`, so it is inert **while all ids are unique** — but when two files share an `Id`, **the surviving profile differs between Windows and Linux**. That is exactly the cross-OS divergence ADR-022 exists to prevent, and the authoritative CI host is Linux while the shipped player is Windows.

**Status: latent.** Verified 2026-07-26 — 76 files in `data/scenarios`, **zero duplicate ids**; `assets/data/scenarios` has no policy files.

## Defect 2 — silent overwrite on duplicate id (platform-independent)

Neither loop has `ContainsKey`, `TryAdd`, or a duplicate throw — confirmed, zero matches in both files. A duplicate `Id` is **silently swallowed on every platform**.

Realistic trigger: someone copies a scenario file to make a variant and forgets to change `id`. One profile vanishes with no error, and *which* one vanishes varies by OS. The failure presents as "my scenario edits do nothing", which is expensive to diagnose.

This is the more likely defect of the two, and it is live today in the sense that nothing prevents it.

## Fix

Two small changes per site:

1. Sort the enumeration — `.OrderBy(f => f, StringComparer.Ordinal)` — so iteration order is stable across hosts
2. Reject duplicates loudly rather than overwriting — throw `InvalidDataException` naming both files, consistent with the existing `"Invalid scenario policy JSON: {file}"` throw already in `ScenarioPolicyJsonIndex`

## Surface

`src/ProjectAegis.Data/Scenario/Policy/ScenarioPolicyJsonIndex.cs` · `src/ProjectAegis.Sim/Scenario/ScenarioPolicyJsonLoader.cs`

Outside the ZERO-hotpath files (`DelegationBridge`) and outside the CRITICAL hubs (`DecisionLog`, `IOrderLog`), so this does not need the heavier gate — but run `impact()` before editing per CLAUDE.md.

## Test

Regression test: a fixture directory containing two `*.policy.json` files with the same `id` must **fail loudly** rather than silently keeping one. A second test asserting stable ordering across a shuffled directory would also pin Defect 1.

## Note on ADR-022

This closes the ADR's open validation item *"spot-check no OS-gated sim outcomes in core assemblies"* with a result. The headline finding is positive: **Decision 2 is clean** — zero `#if WINDOWS`, zero `RuntimeInformation.IsOSPlatform`, zero `OperatingSystem.Is*` across all 489 files in `Data`, `Sim`, and `Delegation`. Wall-clock reads and unseeded RNG are also zero. This issue is the only exception found, and it is a Decision 3 (determinism) matter rather than a Decision 2 (OS-gating) one.

issues.title: Editor findings list sorts by code, not severity — contradicts ADR-008
issues.description:
**LIVE defect**, verified by direct source inspection 2026-07-26. Found by UX review of the ME-W1 mock against shipped HEAD.

## Site

`src/ProjectAegis.Delegation.UnityAdapter/Authoring/LiveFindingsPresenter.cs:52-55`

```csharp
.Select(f => f.Code)
.OrderBy(c => c, StringComparer.Ordinal)
```

## The contradiction

ADR-008 pins the deterministic findings order as:

`(Severity DESC, Code ASC, MissionId, UnitId, TargetId, Message)`

The presenter implements only the second term. Severity is dropped entirely — it survives as a single boolean `HasErrorSeverity` (`:42-43`).

## Effect

The one finding that blocks export is sorted among the ones that block nothing, by alphabetical accident. Observed in the ME-W1 mock rendering the Baltic Patrol fixture:

| Order | Severity | Code |
| -- | -- | -- |
| 1 | WARN | `MISSION_NO_UNITS` |
| 2 | WARN | `MISSION_NO_UNITS` |
| 3 | **ERROR** | `STRIKE_UNREACHABLE` |
| 4 | WARN | `MISSION_NO_UNITS` |

The blocking error is third of four, at the same visual weight as the rest.

This is a presenter defect, not a determinism defect — `ReportHash` is unaffected, and the current order is stable run-to-run. It is deterministically wrong.

**Surface:** `src/ProjectAegis.Delegation.UnityAdapter/Authoring/`

## Done when

- [ ] `LiveFindingsPresenter` orders by the full ADR-008 tuple, severity first
- [ ] Sort lives in the presenter, not any view layer
- [ ] Test asserts error-before-warning on a mixed-severity fixture
- [ ] Test asserts byte-identical ordering across two runs (existing determinism assertions extended, not replaced)
- [ ] `dotnet test ProjectAegis.sln` suite floor held

## Design

Notion: [Mission Editor — UX/UI Review (2026-07-26)](<https://app.notion.com/p/3a9f7cb4e4df8151ae42d2b0a065683e>) → finding **UX-02**

issues.title: Scenario editor validation gate is unreachable from the UI — TryEnterPlay is dead code
issues.description:
**LIVE defect**, verified by direct source inspection 2026-07-26. Found by UX review of the ME-W1 mock against shipped HEAD.

The validation gate is enforced in the core and in the CLI, and is reachable from neither the Unity panel nor the ME-W1 mock. The safety presenter written for the UI layer has no caller.

## The chain

| \# | Link | Evidence |
| -- | -- | -- |
| 1 | An error-severity gate exists for the UI layer | `EditModeController.cs:51-63` — `TryEnterPlay` returns false when `_findings.HasErrorSeverity && !forceConfirmInvalid` |
| 2 | Nothing references it | Window holds only `_session`, `_surface`, `_findings` — `ScenarioMapAuthoringWindow.cs:33-36`. Zero callers of `TryEnterPlay` in the Unity layer |
| 3 | Export gate likewise has no UI caller | `ScenarioExportCommand.Prepare` at `src/ProjectAegis.Data/Scenario/Authoring/ScenarioExportCommand.cs:23` — zero hits for `export`/`publish` across `src/ProjectAegis.Delegation.UnityAdapter/Authoring/` |
| 4 | No action exists to gate | Shipped button set (`ScenarioMapAuthoringWindow.cs:307-338`): Browse, Open, Load UI Dev Baltic, Save, Rebuild, Refresh Findings, 4 domain buttons, place/RP form. **No Export, Publish, Validate, or Play** |
| 5 | The presenter cannot express the gate anyway | `LiveFindingsPresenter` exposes `HasErrorSeverity` only (`:42-43`) — no per-severity counts, no `CanExport` flag |

## Why this is a defect and not a missing feature

The constraint is real and enforced — `scenario_publish` refuses with `VALIDATION_BLOCKED`, and save-is-never-gated-but-export-is is the correct, deliberate policy. The editor simply has no way to say so. A designer sees a red finding count and learns nothing about what it costs them.

Per the GDD, the differentiator is that the tool never lets you ship something broken silently. Today the editor is silent about the one thing it exists to say.

**Surface:** `unity/ProjectAegis/Assets/Editor/`, `unity/ProjectAegis/Assets/UI/ScenarioEditor/`, `src/ProjectAegis.Delegation.UnityAdapter/Authoring/`

## Done when

- [ ] `LiveFindingsPresenter` exposes per-severity counts and a `CanExport` flag sourced from `ScenarioExportCommand.Prepare(...).Allowed` — the view never recomputes the gate
- [ ] Session bar carries a persistent gate state: `EXPORT BLOCKED · N errors` / `READY TO EXPORT`
- [ ] Export / Publish / Sample rendered **disabled with the blocking reason** in tooltip and accessible name — not absent

issues.title: [H4 trigger] Open/no-go decision — UX review supplies the evidence pack H4 is waiting on
issues.description:
H4 currently reads **"Currently out of scope"**, trigger to open: *"product prioritization decision + a new scope boundary document."* Neither existed. This issue supplies the input for the first and scopes the second.

Not a work item — a decision item. Nothing here should be built until H4 opens.

## What prompted it

A UX review of the ME-W1 mock against shipped HEAD produced 23 findings, 8 blocking. Two turned out to be defects in already-delivered work rather than Phase 2 scope, and were filed separately against no milestone, following the <issue id="34e49285-daea-49fa-a85f-3078962dcd89" label="DRG-50" href="https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-50/fuel-drains-60-too-fast-in-play-mode-hardcoded-deltaseconds-vs-160" />/<issue id="81fa9202-c620-4b8c-9544-d7306e89a968" label="DRG-54" href="https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-54/scenario-policy-loaders-enumerate-unordered-and-silently-overwrite" /> precedent:

* [DRG-55](<https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-55>) — findings sort contradicts ADR-008
* [DRG-56](<https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-56>) — validation gate unreachable; `TryEnterPlay` is dead code

**Both are fixable without opening H4.** They are presenter-layer, headless-testable, and do not require a GUI scope decision. Recommend taking them regardless of the outcome here.

The remaining 21 findings are genuine Phase 2 GUI scope and are parked in Notion, not duplicated into Linear.

## The decision

M6 reads **100%**. The review's finding is that the milestone completed against its stated acceptance criteria while the product's stated differentiator — *the tool never lets you ship something broken silently* — is not expressible in any shipped UI. The ACs are CLI-level and genuinely pass; the gap is that no AC covered the panel surfacing the gate.

So the question is not "is the editor done." It is: **was M6's AC set the right one, and does closing that gap belong to H4 or to a corrective slice against M6?**

## What the scope boundary doc must settle

- [ ] Is ME-W1 intended to become the Unity panel, ship as a separate front-end, or remain a design study? *(Changes the estimate materially — the mock's finding-row design is ahead of the shipped panel and either gets ported once or built twice.)*
- [ ] Does the export gate UI land as a corrective slice against M6, or as H4 scope?
- [ ] Is undo/redo in the panel a Phase 2 feature or a data-loss defect? Backend is complete and cross-process (`ScenarioUndoStackStore`, `scenario_undo`); only the panel wiring is missing, and the nearest-looking controls are named "Rebuild" and "Refresh"
- [ ] Accessibility floor for editor tooling — no `:focus` rule exists in either USS file today, against a project standard requiring keyboard-only navigation on PC targets. Does that standard bind internal tools?
- [ ] Does H4 subsume the WYSIWYG platform editor, or split?

## Waves, if H4 opens

Sized in the Notion review; summarized here as pointers only.

| Wave | Theme | Findings |
| -- | -- | -- |
| 1 | Make the gate real | UX-01…04 — *mostly [DRG-56](<https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-56>); presenter-layer, headless-testable* |
| 2 | Safety and input | UX-05, 06, 09, 10, 18 — undo, keyboard model, dirty state, conflict dialog |
| 3 | Legibility and craft | UX-07, 08, 11–17, 19 — layout, contrast, tokens, timeline density, inspector |
| — | Backlog | UX-20…23 — seed/determinism, catalog binding, TL branch, provenance. UX-23 gates on ADR-015 (Proposed, due 2026-09-01) |

## Done when

- [ ] Product prioritization decision recorded (open H4 / defer / corrective slice against M6)
- [ ] If opening: scope boundary doc written and the five questions above answered
- [ ] If deferring: this issue carries the deferral reason and a re-look trigger, so the review does not silently rot

issues.title: Manual autonomy is non-functional — GateResult.QueueForApproval has no product consumer
issues.description:
**LIVE defect**, verified by direct source inspection 2026-07-28. Found by requirements review of agent-management UI (req 04) against shipped HEAD.

## The contradiction

Req 04 defines autonomy level **Manual** as:

> **Manual** — Agent suggests actions only; player must approve (`HUMAN_IN_LOOP`)

There is no approval path. The suggestion is computed, logged, and discarded.

## The chain

| \# | Link | Evidence |
| -- | -- | -- |
| 1 | The gate models an approval outcome | `Orchestration/AutonomyGate.cs:7` — `GateResult(bool ExecuteNow, bool QueueForApproval, bool Rejected, FireAbortReason PolicyDenialReason)` |
| 2 | Manual autonomy sets it | `AutonomyGate.cs:29` — `AutonomyLevel.Manual => new GateResult(playerApproved, !playerApproved, false)` |
| 3 | The caller hardcodes no approval | `Controllers/AgentController.cs:141` — `gate.Evaluate(Autonomy, order, playerApproved: false)` |
| 4 | Only two branches are handled | `AgentController.cs:142-158` — `if (gateResult.Rejected && ...)` logs a denial; `if (gateResult.ExecuteNow)` issues. `QueueForApproval` **is never read** |
| 5 | Nothing else consumes it | Repo-wide grep for `QueueForApproval` outside its declaration returns only `AutonomyGateTests.cs` (3 assertions) |

## Effect

At **Manual** autonomy — and at **Assisted** with a high-risk order — the agent runs its full decision pipeline, appends a `DecisionRecord` (chosen action, candidate set, rationale, attention load/budget, RNG draw), and the resulting order is then **silently dropped**. The player is never asked. The unit does nothing.

The decision *record* survives in the order log, so a replay shows the agent deciding and no order following — which reads as an engine bug rather than a missing feature.

## Why it matters beyond the one level

`HUMAN_IN_LOOP` is the autonomy tier that makes lethal delegation defensible (req 13: full-auto lethal engagement requires explicit opt-in per mission phase). The tier below full-auto currently does nothing at all.

## To close

- [ ] Retain approval-gated orders as durable pending items bound to unit + agent + originating `DecisionRecord` (req 04 **AGD-07**)
- [ ] Approve/reject path, both logged, so an AAR distinguishes *proposed and refused* from *never proposed* (**AGD-08**)
- [ ] Tick-based expiry, identical at 1× and 60× compression — must not vary with frame rate, to preserve replay determinism (**AGD-09**)
- [ ] Surface the backlog with alert priority (**AGD-10**, doc 20 **ALR-01**)
- [ ] Determinism: `ReplayGolden` held; Baltic v2 hash `17144800277401907079` unchanged or golden-updated with an ADR

## Related

Requirements written up in `Game-Requirements/requirements/04-Agent-Delegation.md` (AGD-07 – AGD-10, acceptance criteria 1–2). The UI half depends on the command result channel tracked separately in doc 20 **CMD-16**.

issues.title: Agent attention is a designated core mechanic that no UI surface exposes
issues.description:
**Verified by direct source inspection 2026-07-28.** Found by requirements review of agent-management UI (req 04) against shipped HEAD. Unlike <issue id="addfc33f-54c0-4cbb-94ed-b66aec9bce5b" label="DRG-66" href="https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-66/manual-autonomy-is-non-functional-gateresultqueueforapproval-has-no" /> this is not a broken mechanic — the sim half works correctly. The gap is that it is invisible.

## The design intent

Req 04 \[Resolved Design Decision §1\] designates attention/bandwidth a **core mechanic, not optional**:

> Strategic intent: delegation is a trade-off — one super-agent cannot perfectly command an entire theater.

## It genuinely works

| Link | Evidence |
| -- | -- |
| Load is computed per agent | `Attention/AttentionCalculator.cs` — `Evaluate(budget, memberCount, state)` → `AttentionEvaluation(budget, load, degradation)` |
| Three **graded** degradation tiers | `SlowerReactions` (load > budget), `NarrowedFocus` (> 1.25×), `SimplerDecisions` (> 1.5×) |
| It measurably changes behaviour | `Controllers/AgentController.cs:108-112` — overload multiplies `Traits.ReactionDelay` by 5 |
| It feeds decisions | `AttentionEvaluation` passed into `Decision/DecisionPipeline.cs:13` |
| It is recorded | `attention.Load` / `attention.Budget` written into every `DecisionRecord` |

## The gap

**No C2 projection exposes any of it.** There is no `AttentionProjection`; nothing under `ProjectAegis.Delegation/Projection/` surfaces load, budget, or degradation tier.

So the operator cannot see that an agent is overloaded, cannot see *how* it is degrading, and cannot make the trade-off the mechanic exists to pose. The player experiences a sluggish agent with no available explanation — the data to explain it is already logged.

## To close

- [ ] Project per-agent load vs budget, sourced from the same `AttentionEvaluation` that gated the decision (do not re-derive in UI — it would diverge from the value that actually applied) — req 04 **AGD-11**
- [ ] Surface the three tiers distinctly, named (**AGD-12**)
- [ ] Raise an alert on tier crossing, attributable to the agent (**AGD-13**, doc 20 **ALR-01/05**)
- [ ] Show projected post-assignment load before committing more units to an agent, so overload is a choice not a discovery (**AGD-14**)
- [ ] Include decision-time attention in the agent explain surface (**AGD-20**) — "the agent was overloaded" is frequently the true answer to "why did it do that"

## Related

Requirements in `Game-Requirements/requirements/04-Agent-Delegation.md` (AGD-11 – AGD-14, acceptance criteria 3–4). Projection-only work; no sim change, so no determinism risk.

issues.title: [S109-01] Define decision-time attention projection contract
issues.description:
## Objective

Expose the exact attention state that governed an agent decision as a stable projection contract.

## Acceptance criteria

* Projection carries agent identity, decision-time load, budget, and named degradation tier.
* Values originate from the `AttentionEvaluation` applied by the decision pipeline; Unity performs no duplicate calculation.
* Contract is null-safe for agents with no recorded attention state and preserves deterministic ordering.
* Focused tests cover normal, overloaded, narrowed-focus, and simpler-decisions tiers.
* No change to attention rules, replay hash, or `DelegationBridge` hotpath.

## Dependencies

issues.title: [S109-02] Surface attention state in agent roster and directive UI
issues.description:
## Objective

Make each agent's attention load, budget, and named degradation tier legible in the existing agent roster and directive flow.

## Acceptance criteria

* Roster displays load / budget and one named tier per agent, including normal state.
* Tier presentation is distinct, accessible, and does not rely on color alone.
* Detail and directive views use the S109-01 projection, with consistent empty/loading states.
* Tests cover ordering, tier rendering, and keyboard/screen-reader labels.
* Does not alter command execution or `DelegationBridge` hotpath.

issues.title: [S109-05] Add decision-time attention to the agent explain surface
issues.description:
## Objective

Explain degraded agent behavior with the attention state that was present when the decision occurred.

## Acceptance criteria

* Explain records show decision-time load, budget, and degradation tier.
* Attention appears as an attributable explanation when it affected behavior.
* Historic explain data remains readable when no attention record is available.
* Focused tests prove the explain text matches the decision-time projection, not current UI state.
* No modification of simulation attention rules.

issues.title: [S109-03] Alert on attributable attention-tier crossings
issues.description:
## Objective

Notify the operator when a specific agent enters or changes a degradation tier without creating alert spam.

## Acceptance criteria

* Alert includes agent identity, prior tier, new tier, and the observed load / budget.
* It emits on tier transition only; unchanged tiers do not repeat alerts.
* Alert is observable from the C2 surface and accessible without color-only meaning.
* Tests cover upward, downward, and no-change transitions.
* The mechanism consumes the attention projection; it does not recompute attention.

## Depends on

<issue id="937d3a11-398d-4a8d-b134-d6236fd0bee5" label="DRG-78" href="https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-78/s109-02-surface-attention-state-in-agent-roster-and-directive-ui" />.

issues.title: [S109-04] Preview post-assignment attention before command commit
issues.description:
## Objective

Let the operator understand an assignment's likely attention consequence before committing it through the established command boundary.

## Acceptance criteria

* Assignment/directive flow presents projected load, budget, and resulting tier for the affected agent.
* Preview clearly distinguishes advisory projection from committed state.
* Commit remains routed through the existing pending-approval/command path.
* Invalid or unavailable forecasts fail safely with clear UI feedback.
* Tests cover normal, tier-crossing, cancellation, and no-agent cases.

issues.title: Combat event projection contract
issues.description:
## Goal

Define the deterministic, presentation-facing event contract for player-visible engagements.

## Acceptance criteria

* Emits intent accepted, authorization/refusal, firing/launch, sustained or in-flight state where applicable, and terminal outcome.
* Includes shooter, target, weapon family, outcome, correlation ID, simulation time, and explanation reference.
* Remains replay-stable and is the only combat-fact source for presentation.
* Consumes the authoritative Slice A targetability state and does not rebuild existing sensor, weapon-envelope, or datalink overlays.

## Dependency

Follows the Slice A kill-chain foundation and targetability scenario.

## Design

Notion: Combat Interaction UX — Proposed Requirements and Vertical Slice.

issues.title: Battle graphics: weapons firing, shooter–target tracks, telemetry, effects (presentation)
issues.description:
## Goal

Render the combat-event contract as a readable **battle graphic** between units: weapons firing, shooter–target tracking, weapon telemetry, and bounded weapon effects. **Presentation-only** (ADR-010 / presentation wall). Bind existing combat-event projection ([DRG-165](<https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-165>)); do not invent a second combat-fact source.

## User story

As a player, I want to see engagements between units on the combat picture so I can tell who is shooting whom, with what family, and where the weapon is in its lifecycle — without leaving the map for a separate 3D tool.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Missile, gun, and laser (or energy) engagements are distinguishable without color alone
- [ ] Each engagement shows shooter, target, weapon family, and lifecycle state at tactical zoom
- [ ] Shooter→target track / allocation geometry is visible when facts exist (Command analog: targeting / illumination vectors; salvo allocation between attacker and contact)
- [ ] In-flight / in-progress weapons show track or trail telemetry from projection (heading/path enough for BVR readability; not cinematic-only)
- [ ] Fire / launch and terminal effects are short-lived and budgeted; salvos/bursts aggregate at operational zoom (declutter)
- [ ] Tooltip or detail chrome supplies the readable text equivalent (accessibility)
- [ ] Replay-stable: presentation consumes projection only; no silent ReplayGolden re-bless
- [ ] Hard-no: MapPlaceholderPanelHost / GlobeMapProductHost overlay nits, DelegationBridge Tick/hotpath, CatalogWriteGate writes, SimulationSession, CMD-31/32/34

## Command / CMO reference notes (research 2026-09-22)

Use as *reference vocabulary*, not pixel-copy:

1. **Native map** — Zoomable globe with units, contacts, courses, range rings, weapon allocation UI (Engage Auto F1 / Manual Shift+F1). Manual: [https://ftp.matrixgames.com/pub/CommandModernOperations/CMO%20manual%20EBOOK.pdf](<https://ftp.matrixgames.com/pub/CommandModernOperations/CMO%20manual%20EBOOK.pdf>)
2. **Salvo allocation facts** — Lua `ScenEdit_WeaponAllocation(attacker, contact, side)` returns salvos between attacker↔contact. Aegis exposes equivalent via <issue id="bc6294e8-2fc0-4927-8c32-2a1516bb64df" label="DRG-165" href="https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-165/combat-event-projection-contract" /> projection, not Lua.
3. **Map vectors** — Community/docs cite green targeting / red illumination vectors in Map Settings as 2D engagement geometry cues.
4. **3D / Tacview** — CMO streams real-time 3D via Tacview Advanced for missile trails / corkscrew BVR geometry ambiguous top-down. Matrix UI+Tacview article + Tacview↔CMO setup (attachments).
5. **Altitude / pin-cushion** — Optional true-altitude poles for aerospace — nice-to-have, not MVP.

**Product stance:** Strong **2D combat-picture** graphic first (Command-native map readability). Optional later 3D/Tacview-like view is out of MVP unless Play Mode proves 2D insufficient for BVR.

## Surface (GitNexus stamp — CMANO 2026-09-22)

Index: laptop `cmano-clone` @ `4190fb1` (GitNexus impact on `CombatEvent` / `CombatEventProjection` / `CombatPresentationFrame`).

### Consume (<issue id="bc6294e8-2fc0-4927-8c32-2a1516bb64df" label="DRG-165" href="https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-165/combat-event-projection-contract" /> contract — read-only)

* `src/ProjectAegis.Delegation/CombatEvents/CombatEventTypes.cs`
* `src/ProjectAegis.Delegation/CombatEvents/CombatEventProjection.cs`
* `src/ProjectAegis.Delegation/CombatEvents/CombatEventLogProjection.cs`
* `docs/engineering/combat-event-log-projection.md` (docs only)

### Presentation bind (expected edit / new — ADR-010 wall)

* `src/ProjectAegis.Delegation.UnityAdapter/Bridge/CombatPresentationFrame.cs` (frame assembly; presentation path)
* **NEW** headless binder under `src/ProjectAegis.Delegation.UnityAdapter/Presentation/` (pattern: `DlzLiveSurfaceBinder` / `WraSalvoRemainingBinder`) + matching `*.Tests`
* **NEW** Unity host + UXML/USS for engagement battle-graphic chrome (map-layer presenters owned by this story — **not** MapPlaceholderPanelHost / GlobeMapProductHost)
* Optional thin read helpers on `unity/ProjectAegis/Assets/Scripts/Runtime/DelegationBridgeHost.cs` (**projection read only** — no Tick/hotpath)
* Optional tooltip/detail only: `…/Presentation/CommandReviewTimeline.cs` (keep disjoint from MessageLog focus-ring / C2 chrome)

### Hard exclusions (do not touch)

* MapPlaceholderPanelHost, GlobeMapProductHost
* DelegationBridge Tick / hotpath
* CatalogWriteGate writes, SimulationSession
* CMD-31 / 32 / 34
* Silent ReplayGolden re-bless
* In-flight land Surfaces: RightUnit WRA (<pull-request id="dbb89eb8-1fb9-4cd1-a79c-496c409bae33" label="drgaciw/cmano-clone#672" href="https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/review/featui-drg-259-wra-salvo-remaining-on-weapon-chrome-slice-b-81cb5e1c34a9" />), Oob/MessageLog focus (<pull-request id="4ad51233-da17-4e5a-9b29-6104e3f642fd" label="drgaciw/cmano-clone#673" href="https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/review/featui-drg-270-focus-ring-token-and-keyboard-discovery-baseline-f4790361bbee" />), PendingApproval confirm (<pull-request id="da8d3318-8d8e-4e20-9c66-7e1d8a8f0537" label="drgaciw/cmano-clone#675" href="https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/review/featui-drg-260-assisted-withdrawredeploy-confirm-chrome-0c34401ae4f6" />), AirOps ready (landed <pull-request id="22ff8cb4-945e-46e5-a3e4-eeeefc868763" label="drgaciw/cmano-clone#674" href="https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/review/featui-drg-267-air-ops-ready-aggregate-on-existing-panel-838481cafbdf" />)

### Parallelism note

Implement **after** land stack `#673 → #675 → #672` clears. File-disjoint from C2 residual trio; no 4th slice until then.

## Out of scope (MVP)

* New Air Ops FSM / LOG-08
* Photoreal VFX pipeline
* Full Tacview AAR export
* Unity MCP authoring pass (deferred until connector exists)

## Design

Notion: Combat Interaction UX — Proposed Requirements and Vertical Slice.

## Status

**REQ draft ready** for Notion claim. Implementation queued post land `#673→#675→#672`. Play Mode <issue id="066c5b74-3cec-4f52-9eba-4ef15653abab" label="DRG-208" href="https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-208/play-human-play-mode-re-signoff-at-2316cbf5" /> remains human gate.

issues.title: EPIC: Slice A — Find, Fix, Track, Target
issues.description:
## Outcome

A player can follow a contact from detection to targetability, with visibility into provenance, confidence, freshness, communications state, classification, authority, and rules of engagement.

## Framework

## Goal

Notion is requirements/design source; Linear is delivery source; GitHub is code, review, and CI source; Graphite manages stacked branches and pull requests.

* Correlates a scenario run with replay, oracle outcome, Buildkite evidence, and defect follow-up.
* Retains existing fingerprint checks during migration; no silent loss of fail-closed coverage.
* Keeps simulation facts authoritative and observable without duplicating tactical logic.

## Dependency

Requires the capability manifest.

## Revision-bound evidence extension — 2026-09-30

Owner: drg amtd. Requirement VER-07.3–6 (proposed). Every evidence row records requirement/AC ID, inspected and executed revision (and dirty-tree identity), scenario/seed/policy/catalog identity, command or harness, timestamp, artifact link, result and evidence kind (static inspection/headless/Editor capture/human acceptance). Keep declared floor separate from observed counts; historical results cannot satisfy a different revision. Missing, skipped or blocked evidence remains explicit. Owner signoff is a separate row with person/date/revision; technical success never infers acceptance.

## Outcome

Establish an evidence-backed Unity UX/UI baseline for C2, Mission Editor and Platform Editor, then close confirmed presentation gaps through the existing delivery owners.

## Scope

G1 reconciles requirements and evidence; G2 validates integrated C2 workflows; G3 validates Mission/Platform Editor workflows. Existing A-C implementation, traceability, performance and accessibility stories retain ownership.

## Sources

[Slice G requirements and acceptance](<https://app.notion.com/p/3d5f7cb4e4df812186c2db1a397b17d1>)
Local plan: `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-08-slice-g-unity-ux-ui.md` (uncommitted at creation).
Baseline: `docs/superpowers/reviews/2026-09-08-slice-c-playmode-acceptance.md`, HEAD 37e6ba6d plus existing local changes.

## Exit gate

* Requirement/surface/command/test/scenario/evidence links are reconciled, with proposed requirements distinguished from approved ones.
* C2 and editor success/recovery flows have reproducible evidence.
* Headless, Editor, performance and owner acceptance are reported separately.
* Relevant <issue id="23fe78fc-ddbf-4aeb-a8fd-8826afb06205" label="DRG-187" href="https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-187/maintain-kill-chain-traceability-and-slice-acceptance-matrix" />/188, <issue id="c8b79a30-0b7e-4f3f-a4b0-0b22320a67b1" label="DRG-176" href="https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-176/set-combat-picture-performance-and-declutter-budgets" />/26, <issue id="7565c7a4-b3ff-4d35-aaea-4ff7f56452bd" label="DRG-170" href="https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-170/validate-combat-declutter-accessibility-and-replay" />/177/205 and Slice C gates are linked rather than duplicated.
* Required technical checks pass; no high-severity usability defect lacks owner-approved disposition.
* Owner explicitly accepts the scoped UX/UI package.

## Boundaries

ADR-010 sections 2-3, ADR-007 and ADR-001; ADR-011/017 for authoring. DelegationBridge zero-touch, existing CatalogWriteGate paths unchanged, Excel-primary PE, v2 golden hash preserved. Planning approval is not visual signoff. D/E/F are audit categories, not confirmed delivery slices.

## Sequencing

G1 and traceability can proceed now. <issue id="72627172-94af-41de-b160-61e0febb7890" label="DRG-197" href="https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-197/reindex-gitnexus-and-verify-the-post-implementation-knowledge-graph" /> must restore usable current graph impact before symbol edits. G2/G3 follow G1 with one local Editor coordinator. Slice C owner acceptance and positive live group/coverage gaps remain explicit.

issues.title: GitNexus MCP servers return corrupted results after the 2026-09-27 14:23 CT rebuild
issues.description:
## Problem

After the `cmano-clone` GitNexus index was rebuilt at 2026-09-27 14:23 CT (main `7a097f93`), the running `user-gitnexus` MCP servers started returning corrupted results: empty or garbled symbol ids, NUL bytes in strings, UIDs that are not found, and unrelated symbols merged together.

Example: `impact` upstream on `C2AuthorityProjector` through MCP returns CRITICAL with 140 direct callers, 157 impacted, 51 processes and 20 modules (mostly MissionEditor CLI commands). The correct result from a fresh `npx gitnexus` CLI read is HIGH with 4 direct callers (`SliceAContactFrame`, `EscalationGate` x2, `TargetabilityAccept`), 6 impacted, 2 processes and 3 modules, which matches a text search. SliceA saw the same fake 140-caller CRITICAL on `AfterActionLedgerProjection`.

Restarting the MCP connection from one agent at about 14:35 CT did not fix it. The `npx gitnexus` CLI against `/workspace/cmano-clone` was also corrupted between about 14:25 and 14:28 CT, and has been clean since about 14:31 CT. Every MCP server process that was checked had started before the rebuild (the newest at 14:08 CT).

## Current workaround

Per CMANO on 2026-09-27: use the `npx gitnexus` CLI or a plain text search for blast-radius checks, not the MCP tools.

## Acceptance criteria

* Find out why MCP servers keep serving corrupted reads after an index rebuild (for example, stale database handles or WAL state held by long-running servers).
* Document a recovery step (such as a full server restart) that makes MCP results match the CLI again, and verify it with the `C2AuthorityProjector` example.
* Add a note to the GitNexus runbook to restart MCP servers after any reindex.

## Context

Evidence: <issue id="72627172-94af-41de-b160-61e0febb7890" label="DRG-197" href="https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-197/reindex-gitnexus-and-verify-the-post-implementation-knowledge-graph" />, draft PR <pull-request id="6557634e-7317-47ec-9c33-b2e9d8669d2a" label="drgaciw/cmano-clone#681" href="https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/review/drg-197-gitnexus-reindex-verify-evidence-at-7a097f93-737a691527e4" /> (`production/qa/drg-197-gitnexus-reindex-evidence.md`, gap G1).

issues.title: GitNexus misses calls to overloaded static Project(...) methods (impact reads 0 but says exact)
issues.description:
## Problem

The GitNexus analyzer on `cmano-clone` (index at main `7a097f93`) does not create CALLS edges for calls to overloaded static `Project(...)` methods. As a result, `impact` reports UNKNOWN with 0 callers for those methods but still labels the result `epistemic: exact`, which reads as "nobody calls this" when it isn't true.

* `ContactProvenanceProjection.Project` has 4 production callers by text search (confirmed by SliceA with GitHub code search): `IdentityClassProjection`, `TrackCustodyProjection`, `TargetabilityAcceptProjection`, and `SliceAContactFrame` in UnityAdapter/Bridge. GitNexus shows 0.
* `KillChainContactStateProjection.Project` has 3 production callers: `KillChainContactStateBridge`, `TrackCustodyProjection` and `SensorToShooterProjection`. GitNexus shows 0.
* By contrast, the single-overload `C2AuthorityProjector.Project` resolves correctly (4 direct callers, HIGH).

## Risk

Any blast-radius check on these projections, or on similar overloaded static methods, undercounts callers and can clear a Surface that isn't actually disjoint.

## Acceptance criteria

* Reproduce with the two methods above, then determine whether it is an analyzer limitation (overload resolution for static calls in C#) or a configuration issue.
* Report upstream or fix it if possible. Otherwise, add a runbook note that impact on overloaded static methods is a lower bound and must be backed up with a text search.
* Re-verify the 4 and 3 caller counts after any change.

## Context

Evidence: <issue id="72627172-94af-41de-b160-61e0febb7890" label="DRG-197" href="https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-197/reindex-gitnexus-and-verify-the-post-implementation-knowledge-graph" />, draft PR <pull-request id="6557634e-7317-47ec-9c33-b2e9d8669d2a" label="drgaciw/cmano-clone#681" href="https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/review/drg-197-gitnexus-reindex-verify-evidence-at-7a097f93-737a691527e4" /> (`production/qa/drg-197-gitnexus-reindex-evidence.md`, gap G2).

* `ReplayCheckpointStore` (`src/ProjectAegis.Delegation/Replay/ReplayCheckpointStore.cs`) records only `(simTick, worldHash, logFingerprint, lastSequenceId)`. Those are hashes, not restorable state.

* The GDD already specifies it: `design/gdd/simulation-core-time.md` edge case "Save/load restores simTick, scenarioSeed, RNG stream counters (checkpoint + log tail)".
* Scenario *authoring* save/load exists (`ScenarioAuthoringSession`, ME-023, `SaveVsExportGateTests`). That is file authoring, not game state.

**Multiplayer is excluded from v1 in the repo:**

* `design/gdd/game-concept.md`: "Out (v1): … full multiplayer"
* `production/stage.txt`: "No E7/E9/multiplayer"
* `production/release/launch/faq-draft.md`: "Out of current E7 prep scope (ZERO DelegationBridge edits)"

Product confirmation + an **ADR for the DelegationBridge ZERO-touch constraint** (roadmap §14). Roadmap 2026-08-09 also notes "out of single-player deploy model".

## Hard-no exposure (ADR required before touching)

* **DelegationBridge Tick/hotpath**: `Tick(ISimWorldSnapshot, IOrderSink)`, `TryEnqueueHumanOrder`, `TryIssuePlayerCommand`
* **SimulationSession**: clock, watch queue, orchestrator state

* **CMD-31/32/34**: issued player commands must be persisted (save) or networked (multiplayer)

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Product decision recorded: save-load only, or save-load + multiplayer (child story)
- [ ] ADR merged and Accepted. It must name either an explicit product waiver of ZERO-touch or a design that needs no bridge or session change.
- [ ] First slice defined with non-`TBD` Surfaces, and a replay-hash plan (preserve, or re-bless via ADR)

issues.title: [H6] Product decision: save-load only vs multiplayer for H6
issues.description:
## Context

H6 bundles two things of very different size:

* **Save/load** is single-player and fits the deterministic core. The GDD already specifies it (`design/gdd/simulation-core-time.md`: "Save/load restores simTick, scenarioSeed, RNG stream counters (checkpoint + log tail)").
* **Multiplayer** is excluded from v1 in `design/gdd/game-concept.md` ("Out (v1): full multiplayer") and in `production/stage.txt`. The roadmap calls it "out of single-player deploy model". It would change the deploy model, store copy (`production/release/store/store-page-draft.md`: "Singleplayer focus"), and the `DelegationBridge` order-injection path.

This is an **owner decision**. It is not engineering work.

## Decision options

1. Save/load only, and multiplayer stays out of v1. This is the smallest ADR and the least bridge exposure.
2. Save/load now, with multiplayer as a separate later horizon (for example H9) behind its own ADR.
3. Save/load + multiplayer together. That needs a netcode model (deterministic lockstep vs server-authoritative), a v1 scope change, and store/FAQ changes.

## Questions the owner must answer

- [ ] Save/load: manual save slots, autosave, or both? Mid-engagement saves allowed?
- [ ] Must saves survive a build or catalog update, or only the same build and same catalog snapshot?
- [ ] Is multiplayer in or out of H6? If in: co-op or adversarial, LAN or online, turn/lockstep or real time?
- [ ] Is a `DelegationBridge` / `SimulationSession` **product waiver** acceptable, or must the design be zero-touch?

## Entry gate

This story **is** the "product confirmation" half of the H6 gate.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The decision is recorded as a comment here and in the Notion H4–H6 intake page
- [ ] The H6 ADR story is updated with the chosen option
- [ ] If multiplayer is out, the H6 epic is renamed or scoped to save/load and the `cmano-clone` H6 milestone note is updated after GO

Surface: none (decision only)

## Start condition

**Nothing is started until the owner gives GO.** This issue stays in Backlog and no agent is dispatched.

2026-09-30 user authorized all review recommendations: use **save first / multiplayer separate and later** as the roadmap planning direction. Keep manual/autosave, retention, cross-build compatibility and architecture constraints as explicit decision questions. Record owner approval of the eventual product/ADR package separately; this planning update does not claim implementation or close the issue.

6. **Presentation**: how Play Mode rebinds after a load without editing `MapPlaceholderPanelHost` / `GlobeMapProductHost` (ADR-010 / 007 / 001 presentation wall).

issues.title: [H6] Read-only spike: replay-to-tick resume feasibility + mutable session-state inventory
issues.description:
## Context

A save model that keeps `DelegationBridge` and `SimulationSession` untouched depends on one thing: whether a session can be rebuilt by deterministically re-simulating `(scenario, seed, catalog snapshot, order log)` up to a tick through existing public APIs. The facts this rests on:

* `docs/engineering/determinism-and-replay.md`: `(scenario, seed)` gives an identical order log. `SeededRng` is a pure function of `(seed, domain, entityId, simTick, drawIndex)`.

* `src/ProjectAegis.Delegation.UnityAdapter/Baltic/BalticReplayHarness.cs`: an existing headless re-simulation driver.

issues.description:
## Context

The H5 entry gate is "Content pipeline ADR accepted". No such ADR exists (`docs/architecture/` holds ADR-001…026; ADR-027 is in open PR <pull-request id="540d1213-7de1-4ff7-a462-c2a405c9d241" label="drgaciw/cmano-clone#679" href="https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/review/docsunity-record-unity-mcp-stack-choice-adr-027-and-fix-0860-version-176dd2257933" />).

Addressables use today is a single atlas key, `Map/App6FrameAtlas`:

* `unity/ProjectAegis/Assets/Addressables/Map/App6AtlasAddressablesManifest.json`
* `unity/ProjectAegis/Assets/Editor/App6AddressablesGroupSetup.cs`
* `src/ProjectAegis.Delegation/Projection/App6AddressablesCatalog.cs`
* Consumed by `MapPlaceholderPanelHost` with a Unicode fallback (S27-07)

The package is `com.unity.addressables` 2.9.1. The roadmap (`docs/reports/future-sprint-roadmap-07142026.md`) lists "Addressables / remote content design undesigned".

## Scope of the ADR

Write a new ADR under `docs/architecture/` using the next free number.

1. **Content classes** in and out of Addressables:
   * Presentation art/USS/audio (`production/assets/*`, `design/assets/asset-manifest.md`)
   * APP-6 atlases
   * Globe/basemap tiles
   * Scenario packages (`AegisScenarioPackage`)
   * Catalog snapshots (`src/ProjectAegis.Data/Snapshots/`)

   Core sim DLLs are **out** (`.claude/agents/unity-addressables-specialist.md`).
2. **Presentation wall** (ADR-010 / 007 / 001): Addressables APIs only in Unity presentation assemblies. `ProjectAegis.Sim`, `ProjectAegis.Data` and `ProjectAegis.Delegation` keep headless resolvers like `App6AddressablesCatalog` and never reference `UnityEngine.AddressableAssets`.
3. **Determinism**: sim-relevant data (catalog, scenario policy) must reach the sim through existing Data loaders and hashes (`CatalogSnapshotHasher`, `UnifiedReleaseTrainManifest`), not through Addressables. State how the Baltic hash `17144800277401907079` stays preserved. **No silent ReplayGolden re-bless.**
4. **CatalogWriteGate**: Addressables never becomes a write path into the catalog.
5. **Host impact**: bulk loading must go through a new loader seam, not by growing `MapPlaceholderPanelHost` or `GlobeMapProductHost`. If it cannot, name the waiver.
6. **Local vs remote**: local-only for Release, or remote/CDN (Launch-adjacent, and H3 is not open).
7. Build and CI: headless CI cannot build Addressables content, so say what is verified headless and what needs a local Editor.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] ADR file merged with Status Proposed, then Accepted by the owner (this closes the H5 gate)
- [ ] Content-class table with owner and loader for each class
- [ ] Hard-no impact stated per host, gate and golden
- [ ] First slice named, with a non-`TBD` Surface

issues.title: DRG-169 follow-up: reject cross-snapshot target mismatches on contact combat card
issues.description:
## Context

Deferred from Codex P2 on [PR #684](<https://github.com/drgaciw/cmano-clone/pull/684#discussion_r4162526546>) (<issue id="56453500-7b38-4684-afaa-376904a68c1c" label="DRG-169" href="https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-169/add-contact-combat-card-and-bda-state" /> headless contact combat card).

## Suggestion

When snapshots associate the same contact ID with different targets (e.g. provenance maps `c1` to `target-1` while targetability or BDA maps it to `target-2`), `ResolveEngagementTargetId` suppresses only the engagement, but targetability and BDA for `target-2` can still render on `c1`'s card. Fail those fields closed to `UNKNOWN` unless their target agrees with the selected contact's other identity facts.

## Scope

`ContactCombatCardProjection.cs` (+ tests). Non-blocking for the <pull-request id="bf3faee0-81f0-4709-99fc-8c1ad2cfdf8f" label="drgaciw/cmano-clone#684" href="https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/review/drg-169-headless-contact-combat-card-projection-and-bda-state-a5b527a2c57b" /> land; mixed-frame / contact-ID reuse edge case.

issues.title: DRG-169 follow-up: wrap ContactCombatCardSnapshot.Cards with Array.AsReadOnly
issues.description:
## Context

Deferred from Codex P2 on [PR #684](<https://github.com/drgaciw/cmano-clone/pull/684#discussion_r4162526559>) (<issue id="56453500-7b38-4684-afaa-376904a68c1c" label="DRG-169" href="https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-169/add-contact-combat-card-and-bda-state" /> headless contact combat card).

## Suggestion

For every non-empty snapshot, `Cards` exposes the copied array behind `IReadOnlyList`; a consumer can cast it back to `ContactCombatCard[]` and replace entries, leaving `Cards` inconsistent with the stored replay fingerprint. Wrap the copy with `Array.AsReadOnly(copy)` so the advertised immutable snapshot cannot be mutated through its public surface.

AGENTS.md reference: immutable snapshot guidance.

## Scope

`ContactCombatCardProjection.cs` (+ a regression test if cheap). Non-blocking for the <pull-request id="bf3faee0-81f0-4709-99fc-8c1ad2cfdf8f" label="drgaciw/cmano-clone#684" href="https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/review/drg-169-headless-contact-combat-card-projection-and-bda-state-a5b527a2c57b" /> land.

issues.title: DRG-231 follow-up: [SYM-MIL] preserve naval type icon + MIL SIDC through map/Cesium symbology projection; immutable SymbolKeyRegistry.All
issues.description:
## Context

Deferred code-review findings on [PR #694](<https://github.com/drgaciw/cmano-clone/pull/694>) (S126 MIL-only symbology subset — canonical keys, profile switch, disclaimer; <issue id="a657c027-6658-4623-97d1-eba4b527acb2" label="DRG-231" href="https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-231/sym-mil-01-military-tactical-symbology-ntds-app-6-mil-std-2525" /> SYM-MIL-01).

## Findings

1. `SymbologyProjection.cs:63` **— combatant vs unknown look identical in projected map rows.** The naval type icon is not preserved when rows are projected, so a classified combatant and an unknown contact render the same glyph.
2. **Cesium path re-parses MIL SIDC into the legacy ground glyph.** `CesiumBillboardProjection` takes the military SIDC produced by the MIL profile and re-parses it into the legacy ground glyph, losing domain/type on the globe.
3. `SymbolKeyRegistry.All` **exposes a castable array.** Callers can cast the exposed collection back to an array and mutate the registry. Expose `Array.AsReadOnly(...)` / an immutable collection instead.

## Why deferred (non-blocking for #694)

`SymbologyProjection.Apply` has no non-test caller yet, so none of these affect a shipped surface today. **Must be done before the map consumes the MIL profile.**

## Acceptance (when picked up)

* Projected map rows preserve the naval/domain type icon; a combatant and an unknown contact of the same platform type produce distinguishable symbols (test covers both).
* `CesiumBillboardProjection` consumes the MIL SIDC / canonical key directly (no re-parse into the legacy ground glyph); test proves a naval MIL SIDC stays naval on the Cesium path.
* `SymbolKeyRegistry.All` returns a read-only/immutable collection; a test proves it cannot be cast to a mutable array and mutated.
* Observer-safe unknown fallback (MIL-AC) unchanged; ReplayGolden / Baltic v2 hashes untouched; projection stays presentation-only.

issues.title: DRG-165 follow-up: wire Slice A targetability into production CombatPresentationFrame.Build; match targetability on shooter + target
issues.description:
## Context

Deferred code-review findings on [PR #696](<https://github.com/drgaciw/cmano-clone/pull/696>) (<issue id="bc6294e8-2fc0-4927-8c32-2a1516bb64df" label="DRG-165" href="https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-165/combat-event-projection-contract" /> combat event contract consumes Slice A targetability + execution facts), plus a matching finding on [PR #702](<https://github.com/drgaciw/cmano-clone/pull/702>) (<issue id="28e8db3d-4595-4bbb-ba4d-c38283aa6261" label="DRG-166" href="https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-166/combat-vertical-slice-scenario-and-acceptance-harness" /> vertical-slice harness).

## Findings

1. `CombatPresentationFrame.cs:79` **— Slice A link exists only in tests.** The bridge and `SliceBCombatScenario` call `Build` without Slice A targetability, so the targetability → combat-event link DRG-165 advertises is only exercised by unit tests, never on the production/scenario path.
2. `CombatEventProjection.cs:240` **— targetability lookup matches target only.** It should also match the requested shooter; otherwise a targetability fact for a different shooter on the same target can be attached to the event.
3. **Same pattern in PR #702:** `EngagementExplanationProjection.cs:90` uses a target-only lookup, so an earlier refusal can show later (or other-shooter) facts.

## Why deferred (non-blocking for #696 / #702)

The PRs land the headless contract and harness; changing the bridge/scenario composition widens Surface beyond the stamped presentation files. The lookup fixes are correctness hardening with no current production consumer depending on multi-shooter disambiguation.

## Acceptance (when picked up)

* Bridge and `SliceBCombatScenario` pass the authoritative Slice A targetability state into `CombatPresentationFrame.Build`; a scenario-level test (not a hand-built frame) proves the link appears.
* `CombatEventProjection` targetability lookup keys on (shooter, target) \[and correlation/time where applicable\]; test with two shooters on one target proves the correct fact is attached.
* `EngagementExplanationProjection` lookup keys on shooter + target and respects ledger/sim-time order so an earlier refusal never shows later facts; regression test included.
* Replay-stable; ReplayGolden / Baltic v2 hash untouched; `DelegationBridge` hotpath unchanged unless a separate single-owner story owns it.

Surface (CMANO re-stamp 2026-10-29, main 3bcfbb7b): `src/ProjectAegis.Delegation.UnityAdapter/Baltic/CombatVerticalSliceHarness.cs`, `src/ProjectAegis.Delegation.UnityAdapter/Baltic/SliceBCombatScenario.cs` (only if the scenario `Result` must carry the targetability frame), `src/ProjectAegis.Delegation.UnityAdapter.Tests/Baltic/CombatVerticalSliceHarnessTests.cs`. All three exist on main 3bcfbb7b; none is hard-no.

Dependency cleared: PR <pull-request id="7cb3625f-5a34-475a-99d8-8786ce00096d" label="drgaciw/cmano-clone#710" href="https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/review/fixcombat-preserve-shooter-scoped-slice-a-facts-65e19ccd2f6f" /> (`fix(combat): preserve shooter-scoped Slice A facts`) merged into `main` 2026-10-15 (merge commit 7674649f, an ancestor of 3bcfbb7b). It covered findings 1, 2 and 3 (runtime bridge plus shooter + target lookups). This story is the residual scenario path: on 3bcfbb7b `CombatVerticalSliceHarness.cs:97` still passes `SliceAContactFrame.Empty` into `CombatPresentationFrameBridge.Build`; pass a frame carrying the authoritative targetability built at line 95, plus a scenario-level test (not a hand-built frame) proving the link appears in `slice.Frame.Events.Targetability`.

Read-only, do not edit (landed via <pull-request id="7cb3625f-5a34-475a-99d8-8786ce00096d" label="drgaciw/cmano-clone#710" href="https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/review/fixcombat-preserve-shooter-scoped-slice-a-facts-65e19ccd2f6f" />, now on main): `CombatPresentationFrame.cs`, `SliceAContactFrame.cs`, `CombatEventProjection.cs`, `CombatEventLogProjection.cs`, `CombatEventFingerprint.cs`, `CombatEventTypes.cs`, `EngagementExplanationProjection.cs`, `TargetabilityAcceptProjection.cs` and their tests. Not touched: `DelegationBridgeHost.cs`, `SimulationSession.cs` (used, not edited), ReplayGolden / Baltic v2 hash. Open gap outside this Surface: on 3bcfbb7b `EngagementExplanationProjection.FindTargetability` is shooter + target scoped but has no sim-time ordering, so <pull-request id="7cb3625f-5a34-475a-99d8-8786ce00096d" label="drgaciw/cmano-clone#710" href="https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/review/fixcombat-preserve-shooter-scoped-slice-a-facts-65e19ccd2f6f" /> did not cover the sim-time acceptance bullet. Track that in a separate follow-up; do not widen this Surface.

Owner lane: SliceA. Not reserved.

issues.title: DRG-358 follow-up: [S124] wire commit strip/bark binders to live commit UI; coalesce double DROPPED bark; log fallback abort code
issues.description:
## Context

Deferred code-review findings on [PR #699](<https://github.com/drgaciw/cmano-clone/pull/699>) (S124 pre-commit constraint/cost strip + refuse bark with ADR-010 fence; <issue id="c7df88ed-b9f5-41af-bb45-8d7c04e606f1" label="DRG-356" href="https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-356/s124-01-w2-c2-01-pre-commit-constraint-cost-strip" /> S124-01, <issue id="0041b3f7-208a-4861-93f9-30d7fbe4ac0a" label="DRG-358" href="https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-358/s124-03-w2-c2-04-refusedrop-bark-log-reason" /> S124-03).

## Findings

1. `CommitConstraintStripBinder` **/** `CommitRefusalBarkBinder` **are not wired to the live commit UI.** Both binders are headless/static; no Unity host binds them (suggested UXML names in the PR: `commit-strip-constraints`, `commit-strip-cost`, `commit-bark-line`).
2. `CommitRefusalBarkBinder.cs:170` **— two DROPPED barks for one refusal.** `SimulationSession` emits a `PolicyDenialRecord` *plus* a synthetic not-launched `EngagementRecord` for the same denied order, so the binder produces two DROPPED barks. Coalesce them into one.
3. `CommitRefusalBarkBinder.cs:125` **— bark shows** `UNSPECIFIED` **but the log line is blank.** When the abort code falls back, put the same fallback code in the `MessageLogLine` so bark and log agree.

## Why deferred (non-blocking for #699)

(1) is deferred by design — #699 is a headless PR; Unity host wiring and Editor screenshots are explicitly out of scope. (2)/(3) only surface once a host renders barks; no live consumer yet.

## Acceptance (when picked up)

* Strip and bark render in the live commit UI via the existing presentation host; projection-only fence (`CommitStripProjectionFenceTests`) stays green; plugin DLL refreshed; Editor capture recorded.
* One denied order yields exactly one DROPPED bark (correlated `PolicyDenialRecord` + synthetic not-launched `EngagementRecord` coalesced); regression test.
* Fallback abort code (e.g. `UNSPECIFIED`) appears in both bark and log line; regression test.
* Façade remains authoritative; no `SimulationSession` / order-sink / `DelegationBridge` edits from presentation.

issues.title: DRG-345 follow-up: [H4-CAPABILITY] add 'generic-only' Warning tier for Patrol/Strike on CLI simulate path
issues.description:
## Context

Deferred code-review finding on [PR #698](<https://github.com/drgaciw/cmano-clone/pull/698>) (<issue id="044990c3-0fab-4227-988a-c3ca7af56e6f" label="DRG-345" href="https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-345/h4-capability-expose-unsupported-mission-roles-before-export-and-play" /> disclose unexecuted mission roles before Export and Play). Related: <issue id="5f3fde68-82d5-4309-8b80-1254f1308065" label="DRG-346" href="https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-346/h4-first-slice-map-edit-validate-save-export-play-using-existing" /> H4 first slice.

## Finding

`MissionRoleCapabilityManifest.cs:103` **labels Patrol/Strike as executed**, but `ScenarioSimulateSampleCommand` never passes missions to `BalticReplayHarness.Run`. On the CLI simulate path, Patrol/Strike missions are therefore effectively generic (units behave without mission-specific execution), so the manifest overstates execution.

## Why deferred (non-blocking for #698)

The obvious fix — marking Patrol/Strike unexecuted at **Error** severity — would block Export of every Patrol/Strike scenario, which is worse than the current overstatement. The right fix needs a new intermediate tier, which is a contract change beyond #698's scope.

## Acceptance (when picked up)

* Manifest gains a **generic-only** tier evaluated per execution backend (CLI simulate vs session/Play), surfaced as a **Warning** finding with a stable code.
* Patrol/Strike on the CLI simulate path produce the generic-only Warning; Export and Play are **not** blocked; Tanker/AEW/EW unexecuted Errors unchanged.
* Disclosure text in validation UI/briefing states the role runs as generic behavior on that backend; UI does not invent sim authority.
* Deterministic role-policy fixtures + UI projection tests cover executed / generic-only / unexecuted; saving incomplete drafts still allowed.
* If `ScenarioSimulateSampleCommand` is later changed to pass missions, the tier flips to executed via the manifest (no hard-coded role lists in UI). ReplayGolden hash untouched.

issues.title: DRG-236 follow-up: [S125 editor] validate saved drafts against their bound catalog, not the Baltic fixture fallback
issues.description:
## Context

Deferred code-review finding on [PR #701](<https://github.com/drgaciw/cmano-clone/pull/701>) (S125 editor honesty (headless) — save≠export, verb table, workbook contract, binding; <issue id="4e65f999-c537-4646-bdd7-9d3e69dc3f19" label="DRG-236" href="https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-236/slice-g3-validate-mission-and-platform-editor-ux-workflows" /> Slice G3).

## Finding

`ScenarioSaveExportGate.cs:54` **—** `LiveValidate()` **falls back to the Baltic fixture catalog when no catalog is bound.** A saved draft authored against a different catalog would be validated against Baltic data, producing false passes/failures.

## Why deferred (non-blocking for #701)

`SaveDraft` has no production caller yet, so the fallback cannot affect a real save today. Binding the draft's catalog requires the editor composition path, which is outside the headless PR's Surface.

## Acceptance (when picked up)

* `LiveValidate()` / `SaveDraft` validate against the draft's bound catalog (resolved from the document's `dbRef`/binding).
* With no bound catalog, the gate reports a stable, actionable finding (e.g. catalog unbound) instead of silently using the Baltic fixture; saving an incomplete draft remains allowed, Export stays gated.
* Tests: draft bound to non-Baltic catalog validates against that catalog; unbound draft yields the finding; Baltic fixture only used in explicit test setup.
* No `CatalogWriteGate` path changes; Excel-primary authoring unchanged.

issues.title: DRG-361 follow-up: [S124 rebrief] refresh Hindsight personality routing after TryRebriefAgent
issues.description:
## Context

Deferred code-review finding on [PR #704](<https://github.com/drgaciw/cmano-clone/pull/704>) (S124 headless Assign Agent + Rebrief success path; <issue id="890865f3-14ca-41b0-aedb-f527fc1daf93" label="DRG-361" href="https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-361/s124-06-w2-del-02-rebrief-success-path" /> S124-06).

## Finding

`DelegationOrchestrator.cs:479` **— Hindsight personality routing is not refreshed after rebrief.** `TryRebriefAgent` swaps the personality preset (traits + slug) and logs `personality.rebrief`, but does not re-call `RegisterAgent`, so Hindsight memory/routing keeps using the old personality slug.

## Why deferred (non-blocking for #704)

Hindsight is off in CI and replay, so the stale routing cannot affect tests, goldens, or deterministic replay. Low risk; only matters when Hindsight is enabled in a live session.

## Acceptance (when picked up)

* After a successful rebrief, Hindsight routing reflects the new personality (re-call `RegisterAgent` or an equivalent refresh), only when Hindsight is enabled.
* Test with a fake/stub Hindsight client proves the post-rebrief registration uses the new slug; refused rebriefs do not re-register.
* No change to DecisionLog contents or replay hash with Hindsight off; `DelegationBridge` hotpath untouched.
