A modal titled "Air Ops — Multiple host units" with tabs Aircraft Status / Air Facilities; a table of Aircraft · Status · Mission · Loadout · Time to ready · Quick; a stores panel showing magazine availability; and an action bar of Launch Individually · Launch as group(s) · Ready/Arm · Abort Launch · Doctrine · Assign to mission · Unload Cargo. Why it is missing. REQ-20 has zero mentions of aircraft, launch, sortie, hangar or deck. The CMO toolbar surfaces Aircraft Operations and Boat Operations as first-class order groups; REQ-20's parity table has no row for either. ### ⚠️ This requirement is gated by REQ-16, and must be phased accordingly This is the crux. Game-Requirements/requirements/16-Logistics-And-Magazines.md is unusually honest about what exists: > "Not shipped: full air-ops FSM, UNREP, live magazines C2 panel, product MCP logistics tools." > > "Air-ops FSM (taxi/takeoff/land/maint) — Phase N — Boolean readiness only on main." | Model | REQ-16 status | Can the UI show it? | | --- | --- | --- | | Magazine ledger consume (MagazineLedger) | Shipped | Yes | | Fuel burn / bands, per-domain fuel types (aviation JP) | Shipped / P0 | Yes | | Boolean ReadyForLaunch → AIR_NOT_READY (UnitReadinessMap) | Shipped | Yes — binary only | | Ferry missions moving aircraft between bases | Shipped (CLI + validation) | Yes | | Air-ops FSM — taxi / takeoff / land / maintenance | Phase N | No | | Deck cycle, sortie generation rate | Phase N | No | | Composite readinessScore | Phase N | No — boolean only | | UNREP / underway rearm | Phase N | No | A "Time to ready" column cannot be populated, because no state machine produces a time. Rendering it empty, or with a fabricated value, repeats the exact failure documented in the [Scenario Editor W2 review](https://app.notion.com/p/3aaf7cb4e4df81d58626cdda26db28eb) (W2-02), where a mock advertised a 300 ms validation debounce that LiveFindingsPresenter stores and never honours. An absent column is honest; an empty one is a bug report; a fabricated one is a lie. ### Phase A — buildable today against the shipped spine - CMD-24.1 — Cross-host aggregation. List air assets across all units in the current selection, grouped by type and host with counts (12x F/A-18A Hornet (CVN 70 Carl Vinson)). The reference aggregates a carrier, a cruiser, a frigate and a supply ship into one list — the player commands the group's air assets, not each deck separately. This is the window's single most important structural idea and it costs nothing extra to adopt. - CMD-24.2 — Binary readiness with an explicit cause. Show ReadyForLaunch, and where false, name the reason using the same AIR_NOT_READY vocabulary the engage gate already emits — so the window and the engage refusal agree word-for-word. - CMD-24.3 — Magazine-constrained loadout feasibility. For a selected loadout, show how many airframes can be armed from current stock. The reference does this well: # Available Magazines alongside # Available Mags + A/C answers "how many sorties can I actually arm?" rather than "how much do I have?" This is directly implementable on the shipped MagazineLedger. - CMD-24.4 — Aviation fuel shown distinctly from platform fuel (REQ-16 P0: per-domain fuel types). The reference states it as its own line: 0.0 fuel units remaining (Aviation Fuel). - CMD-24.5 — Assign to mission, bridging air assets to the mission system (doc 11). - CMD-24.6 — Aggregate ready count in group status (Aircraft: 35/71). One line, high value, no new model needed. ### Phase N — gated on the REQ-16 air-ops FSM Do not build these ahead of the model: time-to-ready timers; Launch Individually vs Launch as group(s); Abort Launch (requires an in-progress launch state); the Air Facilities tab (deck / hangar / runway capacity and deck cycle); and per-airframe drill-down beyond type aggregation. When the FSM lands, these should arrive together — a launch button without an abort is worse than neither. ### Do not inherit this defect In the reference, the entire action bar is disabled with only Loadout Details: None Selected as explanation. Which action needs what is left to inference. Per the disabled-with-reason pattern established in the editor reviews, each disabled action should carry its own reason — "select a loadout" differs from "no ready airframes" differs from "magazine stock insufficient." ### Projection dependency REQ-16 lists logistics_get_readiness and logistics_project_sorties as MCP Gap — not shipped. The same data has to reach this panel, so CMD-24 likely implies a new read-only projection under ADR-010 rather than view work alone. Worth confirming before estimating. ## CMD-25 — Boat Operations window \[P2 — blocked on domain model\] Requirement. The C2 client shall provide a Boat Operations window, opened from the unit-order toolbar (CMD-16), presenting embarked small craft across the current selection, their readiness, and their tasking. ### ⚠️ Epistemic note — what this is and is not based on I have not seen this window. No screenshot of CMO's Boat Operations dialog was reviewed. What is actually grounded: - A Boat Operations toolbar button sits beside Aircraft Operations in the reference product's order bar (visible in two screenshots) - Group status pairs Boats: 2/2 with Aircraft: 35/71 — the same ready-over-total treatment - REQ-16 maps boat ops to CMO manual §3.3.8 and scopes it P1 The existence and rough role of the window are grounded. Its contents are not. Any detailed layout below the requirement statement would be invention, so there isn't one — deliberately. ### The actual finding — the domain is unspecified, not just unbuilt CMD-24 was gated on a Phase-N state machine, but at least stood on a shipped spine (MagazineLedger, boolean ReadyForLaunch, fuel bands, ferry hooks). Boat operations has no such floor. REQ-16 contains a section literally titled "Boat and Naval Operations". Its entire content is three bullets: > P1 UNREP for fuel and limited rearm → Phase N\* > P0 Docked / underway replenishment affects readiness flags → Partial / Phase N\* > P0 Submarine battery/charge model (simplified) → Phase N\* That is replenishment and submarine power. None of it is about launching, recovering, or tasking boats. The section heading promises a domain the section does not specify. Corroborating checks: | Source | Boat operations coverage | | --- | --- | | REQ-16 §Boat and Naval Operations | UNREP / replenishment / sub battery only — no launch, recovery, or tasking | | REQ-18 Combat Domains | Zero hits for boat, small craft, amphibious, littoral | | REQ-20 C2 UI | No mention | | src/ sim model | No boat / craft / amphibious / boarding type exists | | Sea state / weather model | Not modelled — "sea state" appears only in REQ-15 sensor/EW context | Recommendation: specify the domain before the UI. A window spec written now would be interface over vapour at two levels — no model and no domain requirements. The productive next step is amending REQ-16 §Boat and Naval Operations to actually cover boat operations, then deriving this window from it. ### Why cloning CMD-24 would be wrong The symmetry of the toolbar buttons is misleading. Boats differ from aircraft in ways that change the interface, and a copied spec would encode the wrong model: - Recovery is the hard operation, not launch. Aircraft recovery is gated by deck cycle; boat recovery is gated by sea state and mothership manoeuvring, and a boat that cannot be recovered is a stranded crew, not a diverted airframe. The window's centre of gravity is different. - Sea state gates the operation — and Aegis has no weather or sea-state model at all. This is a hard dependency air ops does not have. - Cargo and personnel, not weapon loadouts. CMD-24.3's magazine-feasibility idea has no boat analogue; the equivalent question is who and what is embarked. - Counts are small. Boats: 2/2 versus Aircraft: 35/71 — type-aggregated rows (12x F/A-18A Hornet) are the right unit for air and the wrong one for boats, where each hull is individually tracked and named. - Boarding / VBSS is a mission type, not a launch action — it needs mission-system integration (doc 11) rather than an ops-window button. ### Scoping note worth raising The reference scenario is anti-piracy — the map carries a "Suspected Pirate Staging Area" label and hostile small craft. In that scenario class, boarding operations are the primary tactical activity, not a supporting one. If Aegis intends to support littoral or counter-piracy scenarios, P1/P2 understates boat operations and the priority deserves revisiting on scenario grounds rather than parity grounds. ### Phase A — what is genuinely buildable today Almost nothing, honestly: - CMD-25.1 — Embarked-craft ready count in group status (Boats: 2/2), mirroring CMD-24.6. This is a readout, needs no FSM, and is the only piece not blocked. Everything else waits on a domain model that does not exist yet. ## CMD-26 — Ground Operations window \[P2 — scoped to brigade+; battalion depth is out of charter\] Requirement. The C2 client shall provide a Ground Operations window presenting friendly and known-hostile ground formations at brigade echelon and above, their aggregate strength and readiness, their air-defence contribution, and their tasking — within the charter scope defined by doc 01. ### ⚠️ Scope finding — read before designing anything The requested echelon list runs division → brigade → regiment → battalion. The project charter already draws a line inside that list, and it is not a "not yet" — it is an explicit exclusion. Game-Requirements/requirements/01-Project-Overview.md: > In scope (line 82): "Air, naval, and aggregate-level ground (brigade+) for air/naval interaction" > > Out of scope (line 90): "Land warfare at battalion scale or below" Echoed normatively in REQ-18 §Land Combat (Limited): "Per doc 01 scope: strategic facilities and IADS, not battalion tactics." | Echelon | Charter status | Notes | | --- | --- | --- | | Division | In scope | Aggregate formation | | Brigade | In scope | The boundary, inclusive — "brigade+" | | Regiment | Needs a decision | Brigade-equivalent in US/NATO and Soviet-pattern usage, so probably in scope — but the charter says "brigade+", not "brigade-equivalent+". Worth resolving explicitly rather than by assumption. | | Battalion | Out of charter | doc 01 line 90 excludes battalion scale and below by name | ### The structural consequence — the TO&E tree is shallow, by design This is the finding that actually shapes the interface, and it is easy to miss. A TO&E window is usually a deep tree: division contains brigades, which contain battalions, which contain companies. But if the charter caps modelling at brigade+, then a brigade is a leaf, not a container. The hierarchy the request implies only has depth if battalions exist as modelled entities — and they explicitly do not. So the in-scope window is two or three levels deep at most: ```javascript Division └─ Brigade / Regiment ← leaf: aggregate strength, readiness, ADA contribution └─ (battalions: out of charter) ``` Designing a deep expandable TO&E tree would build interface for a hierarchy the sim will never populate — the same class of error as CMD-24's Time to ready column and the W2-02 debounce chip. Aggregate rows with no expander are the honest shape under current charter. ### What exists today | Capability | Status | | --- | --- | | CombatDomain.Land enum + LandAspectDomainValidator | Shipped spine / Partial aspect gate | | Ground platform presets in the scenario editor | Shipped — but they are IADS and facilities: Patriot PAC-3, M901 launcher, S-400, RBS-15 coastal battery, air base, port | | Tactical Group model (GroupTarget, DetachRejoinService, detach/rejoin records) | Shipped | | Echelon / TO&E / organisational hierarchy type | Does not exist — no Echelon, Formation, Brigade, Battalion type in src/ | | Full land IADS / battalion-scale combat | Phase N (REQ-18) | Note what the shipped ground presets are: every one is an air-defence system, a coastal battery, or a facility. That is precisely the charter's "strategic facilities and IADS" — the ground domain today is things that shoot at aircraft and things aircraft shoot at, not manoeuvre forces. ### TO&E is not the tactical Group model — do not conflate them Aegis has a Group concept with detach and rejoin. That is a transient tactical association — units operating together now, formed and dissolved at will, mirroring CMO's naval groups. TO&E is permanent organisational subordination — a battalion belongs to its brigade whether or not they are co-located, and that relationship survives detachment. The two answer different questions ("who is manoeuvring together" vs "who does this belong to") and a ground window needs the second, which does not exist. Reusing GroupTarget for echelon structure would silently make organisational hierarchy dissolvable, which is wrong. ### Phase A — buildable within the current charter - CMD-26.1 — Aggregate ground formation list at brigade+ with side, type, and location. Flat or two-level; no battalion expander. - CMD-26.2 — Air-defence contribution per formation — which IADS assets it fields, their state, and their coverage. This is the charter's stated purpose for modelling ground at all ("for air/naval interaction"), so it is the window's centre of gravity rather than a side panel. - CMD-26.3 — Facility status — airbase, port, runway damage, and sortie-capacity linkage into REQ-16 (doc 16 already wires runway/sortie capacity where present). - CMD-26.4 — Aggregate strength / readiness as a single band per formation, not a rolled-up sum of subordinate units — there are no subordinate units to roll up. ### Charter-change path — if battalion depth is genuinely wanted This cannot be filed as a UI requirement. It would require, in order: 1. Amend doc 01 line 90 — the exclusion is charter-level, and everything downstream inherits it 2. Amend REQ-18 §Land Combat (Limited), which cites doc 01 as its authority 3. Introduce an echelon / TO&E model in src/ distinct from the tactical Group model 4. Decide the regiment question above 5. Only then derive this window's deep-tree form That is a significant sim expansion — land manoeuvre warfare is a different game from the air/naval simulation the charter describes. Worth a deliberate product decision, not a requirements edit. ## CMD-27 — Scenario library and load operations \[P0\] Requirement. The client shall provide a scenario library surface for browsing, previewing, and loading scenarios and saved games, which states before load whether a scenario will actually run. ### Why P0 — this is the first screen of the game and it is specified nowhere | Source | What it says | | --- | --- | | doc 02 §Core Gameplay Loop | "Phase 1: Scenario Selection & Force Composition" — the loop begins here | | design/ux/c2-command-post.md:45 | Main Menu → **Scenario Select** → Mission Planning → C2 Command Post → AAR — named in the navigation flow | | REQ-20 | Zero mentions of load, main menu, front-end, or scenario select | | design/ux/ | No main-menu or scenario-select spec (c2-command-post, c2-map-placeholder, interaction-patterns, onboarding-baltic, scenario-editor) | | src/ • CLI | No scenario list/browse verb or projection — scenario_* has create / validate / export / publish / simulate / undo / diff / trace, but no list | Every player's first interaction with the product is a screen that is named twice and designed nowhere. ### The part that is not CMO parity — pre-load feasibility CMO's Load Scenario dialog lists files. Aegis scenarios are not just files — they are validated, catalog-bound, deterministic artifacts that can fail to load for reasons knowable in advance: - Catalog binding — dbRef / dbSnapshotId may not resolve against the installed catalog (DB_MISMATCH), and ref:-prefixed ids may dangle (BROKEN_REF). These are among the most common failure modes in the system. - Validation state — ADR-008 findings with severity; a scenario can carry blocking errors. - Schema / version — scenario-document.schema.json compatibility and editVersion. CMD-27.1 — Pre-load feasibility. The library shall state, per entry, whether the scenario resolves against the installed catalog and passes validation, before the user commits to loading it. This is the load-time analogue of the export gate (UX-01 / DRG-56 in the editor reviews). Same principle, different surface: a constraint the system already enforces should be visible before the user hits it, not as a failure afterwards. Listing an unloadable scenario with no indication is the browser equivalent of an unreachable gate. ### Phase A sub-requirements - CMD-27.2 — Provenance and trust. Distinguish authored / AI-scaffolded / imported (ManifestBuilder.ProvenanceTag, Source ∈ {user, ai, import}) and bundled / user-saved / third-party. ADR-015 (Proposed, decision due 2026-09-01) would derive an agent-authored label from provenance — this library is where that label becomes visible to a player, and is the natural forcing function for that decision. - CMD-27.3 — Determinism metadata. Show metadata.seed, TL branch (metadata.tlBranch), bound policy, and whether a published manifest with ReportHash exists. In a project where replay parity is a release gate, "will this reproduce" is a property worth seeing before opening. - CMD-27.4 — Separate artifact lifecycles. Autosaves, manual saves, and authored scenarios are different classes with different retention and trust; they shall not share one flat list. The reference mixes Autosave_20sec.scen through Autosave_100sec.scen directly among authored scenarios like Georgia2008.scen. - CMD-27.5 — Search and filter, not only sort. The reference offers a single Order scenarios by dropdown. Filter by side, region, duration, validation state, and TL branch. - CMD-27.6 — Preview pane with a real zero-state. Two further views of this dialog show what actually populates it, in one scrolling region: licence prefix + title, Difficulty and Complexity meters, Location — Year, a long briefing, and a rendered map preview. On open, with nothing selected, roughly 40% of the dialog is blank — the zero-state needs instruction, not void. - CMD-27.7 — Unavailable entries state their reason on the row. ⚠️ Corrected after further views. The padlocked entries are explained — selecting one shows [NOT LICENSED] Don of a new Era in red at the top of the preview. So the reason exists; it is just only reachable by selecting each locked item one at a time. The requirement is therefore narrower and cheaper than first written: carry the reason on the list row, so a player sees what they own by scanning rather than by clicking. (Still the third instance of disabled-without-reason in this series — after the editor's greyed actions and the Air Ops action bar — and worth a house rule.) - CMD-27.8 — Difficulty and Complexity as separate, rated axes. The reference rates both independently, as meters, colour-coded by level (green at low, orange higher). This is a better model than one star rating and worth adopting deliberately: difficulty is how hard the scenario is to win; complexity is how much there is to manage. They are orthogonal — a submarine duel can be hard and simple, a multi-domain operation forgiving and overwhelming.

For Aegis this matters more than for the reference product: agent delegation is the mitigation for complexity, not for difficulty. The library is where that value proposition first becomes legible, so the two axes should be visible before load, not discovered during play.

Accessibility: the reference encodes level by bar colour alone. Per CMD-12 (colourblind-safe affiliation), pair the meter with a value or label.

- CMD-27.9 — Setting metadata. Location and Year — the reference shows Ukraine — 2016 and Nova Scotia / Eastern Seaboard — 1975. These are the fields players actually browse by, and they are the natural filter axes for CMD-27.5. - CMD-27.10 — Briefing is the primary selection content, and it is long. The reference runs several paragraphs of geopolitical background in a scrolling region. Aegis already treats briefings as first-class — scenario_export_brief is a shipped CLI verb — so the preview should render the same brief that verb produces, not a separately authored summary. One brief, two surfaces: the CLI/MCP parity principle applied to the library. - CMD-27.11 — Map preview showing force disposition. The reference renders a real tactical thumbnail — terrain, NATO unit symbols, and place labels (CFB GREENWOOD, HALIFAX, HMCS TERRA NOVA, HMCS ASSINIBOINE) — pannable within the preview. You can read the shape of the fight before committing to load.

Aegis can build this cheaply: MapPictureProjection and MapPlaceholderPanelHost are shipped (REQ-20 CMD-06, ADR-007 Phase A). A scenario preview map is the same projection over an unopened document rather than live sim state — reuse, not new rendering work.

- CMD-27.12 — Campaigns are an artifact class, not a folder. The Northern Inferno node expands to 15 numbered, dated scenarios running 1. Opening Moves 07 Aug 1975 through 15. Fail Safe 20 Oct 1975 — an ordered chain with narrative progression, not a bag of unrelated files. Chains Of War is another. The library must model campaign membership, sequence, and completion state; treating a campaign as a directory loses all three. ### Do not inherit - File extensions in the UI. .scen is an implementation detail; Aegis uses *.scenario.json. Show scenario titles, with paths secondary — the same demotion CMD-09 needs in the editor chrome. - Mixed hierarchy. The reference places expandable folders and flat files at the same level, so Tutorials ▸ and Rumble.scen are siblings with different affordances. - Ordering encoded in filenames. Campaign sequence is carried by a 1. … 15. prefix and the date embedded in each name (Needle in a Hay Stack 19 Oct 1975.scen). Sequence and in-fiction date are metadata, not naming convention — encoding them in filenames makes reordering a rename, breaks sorting the moment someone omits a leading zero, and forces the extension-hiding rule above to fight the ordering scheme. ### Dependency — this is not view-only work There is no scenario list/browse verb or projection. Under ADR-010 (headless-first, command-driven), a browse surface needs a read-only projection, and under the CLI/MCP parity principle it should have a headless equivalent — likely scenario_list alongside the existing scenario_* verbs. Confirm before estimating. ## CMD-28 — Menu system, map layers, and view tools \[P1\] Requirement. The client shall provide a menu system exposing view control, map layer selection, spatial tools, and window management — and it shall be the discovery surface for keyboard shortcuts. Reference evidence. The View menu carries, in one flat list: Toggle Full-screen / Windowed Alt+Enter, Zoom In Z, Zoom Out X, Pan Map ▸, Select Next Unit |, Select Previous Unit Backspace, Range / Bearing Tool Ctrl+D, Message Log in Separate Window, Map Lat/Lon Grid, then ten basemap layers (Sentinel-2, ✓BMNG, Relief, ✓Borders + Coastlines, Stamen — Terrain, Stamen — Roads + Cities, Land Cover, Custom Layers, Placenames, Day + Night Lighting), and 3D View. ### The gap REQ-20 specifies no menu bar at all. Keyboard shortcuts appear once in the parity table (§10.1, P1 — Open), custom overlays once (§10.2, P2 — Phase N). There is no mention of fullscreen, zoom controls, a measurement tool, a coordinate grid, a 3D toggle, or basemap layers. ### CMD-28.1 — The menu is how shortcuts become discoverable Every item in the reference displays its binding inline. REQ-20 already wants keyboard shortcuts (§10.1) and the editor reviews found zero :focus rules in the shipped USS — but a shortcut nobody can find is not a feature. The menu is the discovery mechanism, and specifying shortcuts without specifying where they are advertised leaves them unusable. Pairs with the ? shortcut sheet proposed in the [ME-W1 review](https://app.notion.com/p/3a9f7cb4e4df8151ae42d2b0a065683e) (UX-06). ### CMD-28.2 — Basemap layer stack — an architectural gap, not a menu item Ten independently toggleable layers with persisted checked state. Aegis has no layer model. ADR-007 phases map presentation (Phase A placeholder → Phase B Cesium → Phase C APP-6 LOD) but never mentions a layer stack; src/ has no MapLayer / Basemap / overlay-stack type. This needs a decision before it needs a menu: - Which layers exist, and are they fixed or extensible (Custom Layers implies extensible)? - Who owns visibility state? Under ADR-010 everything else is a projection from the headless core — but layer visibility is pure presentation with no sim meaning. It should almost certainly be UI-local, and that exception is worth stating explicitly rather than discovering later. - Do layers persist per user, per scenario, or not at all? ### CMD-28.3 — View-state actions are exempt from CLI/MCP parity; command actions are not This menu makes a boundary explicit that the project will otherwise settle ad hoc. - View state — zoom, pan, layers, grid, fullscreen, 3D toggle — changes only what this operator sees. It has no headless meaning and needs no CLI verb, no order-log row, and no determinism guarantee. - Commands — anything that mutates the scenario or issues orders — must keep CLI/MCP parity and produce logged intents (ADR-010). Stating the line prevents both failure modes: plumbing view toggles through the command bus, and quietly letting a mutating menu item bypass the order log. ### CMD-28.4 — Spatial tools - Range / bearing measurement with a binding. REQ-20 lists "measure" only as a map context-menu item (§4.2, Partial). In a genre where range is the primary spatial judgement — the same reasoning behind CMD-20 — measurement deserves to be a tool, not a buried context entry. - Lat/Lon grid as a toggleable overlay; a coordinate reference alongside CMD-20's distance scale. ### CMD-28.5 — Keyboard unit cycling Select Next Unit / Select Previous Unit. Complements CMD-07 (map ↔ OOB ↔ panel selection sync) by making selection reachable without pointing, which matters for dense pictures and for accessibility. ### CMD-28.6 — Single-panel detachment is much cheaper than the multitasker Message Log in Separate Window detaches one panel to one window. REQ-20's CMD-14 defers "multitasker bookmarks / multi-monitor detachable chrome" to Phase N — but that is the full product feature. Detaching a single panel is a fraction of the cost and delivers most of the multi-monitor value for a log you want visible continuously. Worth splitting from CMD-14 rather than inheriting its deferral. ### CMD-28.7 — Menu organisation The reference's View menu mixes roughly six concerns — window management, camera, selection, tools, panel spawning, overlays, basemap layers, render mode — in one flat list of nineteen items. Adopt the coverage, not the organisation: separate view control from layer selection from tools. ### Do not inherit — the fourth instance Quick Jump is greyed in the menu bar with no stated reason. That is now the fourth disabled-without-reason case catalogued in this series — after the editor's greyed actions, the Air Ops action bar, and the scenario library's padlocks. This should stop being four findings and become one house rule: every disabled control states why, at the control. --- ## CMD-29 — Contact detail panel \[P0\] Requirement. Selecting a contact shall present a panel distinct from the own-unit panel, showing classification and its confidence, detection provenance, engagement permission, and battle-damage assessment. ### The framing that matters The unit panel shows what is. The contact panel shows what we believe. Everything about a contact is inference from sensor returns and may be wrong — the identification, the classification, the position, whether it is still there at all. Collapsing both into one "selected object" panel silently asserts that hostile data is as trustworthy as own-force data, which in this genre is the central lie to avoid. This is the same epistemics as CMD-17 seen from the other side: CMD-17 is "I own this unit but cannot reach it"; CMD-29 is "I can see this thing but do not own it." Both are about the gap between the world and the picture. ### The gap REQ-20's Right-panel row specifies "Selected unit/group: status, sensors, weapons, fuel, doctrine" — own-unit data only. Contacts appear in the left drawer (contact list tab) and in map styling ("Contact styling distinct from friendly"), but selecting one has no specified panel. ### Unusually, the data mostly exists Most gaps in this series are UI over an absent model. This one is the reverse: | Capability | Status | | --- | --- | | ContactSummaryProjection, ContactPictureProjection, ContactPictureEntry | Shipped (src/ProjectAegis.Delegation/Projection/) | | BdaContactDamageStates | Shipped | | ContactChangeRecord — contact lifecycle in the order log | Shipped (doc 17) | | WRA in the engage path | Shipped (EngagementAbortReason, MvpEngagementResolver, AbortReasonCatalog) | | Contact detail panel spec | Absent | The gap is specification, not model. That makes this cheaper than its P0 suggests. ### Sub-requirements - CMD-29.1 — Identification with its confidence. The reference is quietly precise here: the header reads SAM Bn (SA-3b) while the resolved line reads SAM Bn (SA-3c Gon [S-125M1 Nevn-M]). Those disagree — a coarse initial classification alongside a more specific resolution. Classification specificity increases as sensor data accumulates, and the panel must show how well the contact is identified, not merely assert a name. An overconfident label on a poorly-resolved contact is how players shoot the wrong thing. - CMD-29.2 — Detection provenance. "Detected by: Automatic detection on \[Unknown\]" — which sensor, on which platform, and when. Likely the single highest-value element on the panel: it answers why do I think this exists, connects doc 15 (sensor/detection) to CMD-11's "why can't I fire?" explain surface, and makes stale or single-source tracks visible rather than implicit. - CMD-29.3 — WRA classification. The reference shows WRA: Land Structure - Soft - Building (Revetted) — the target classification that drives release authority under doc 13. This is the field that determines whether an engagement is permitted, so it belongs on the panel where the engagement decision is made, not only inside an abort reason after refusal. - CMD-29.4 — BDA as belief, not truth. Damage / BDA / Damage Ctrl — battle damage assessment is an estimate from observation. Rendering it identically to own-unit damage state would assert knowledge the player does not have. BdaContactDamageStates already models this. - CMD-29.5 — Contact report action. A Contact Report… affordance producing the fuller intelligence picture for the selected track. - CMD-29.6 — Staleness. A contact not currently held is a last-known position with an age, not a current one. Pairs with the CMD-17 question about whether last-known values carry an age stamp or are suppressed — the two should be answered together and consistently, since they are the same design question on own units and on hostiles. ## CMD-30 — Tactical overlay control \[P1\] Requirement. The client shall provide control over tactical overlay symbology — range envelopes, engagement vectors, connectivity, courses, and datablocks — separately from basemap layer selection. Reference evidence. A Map Settings menu carrying eight colour-chipped range toggles (Air / Surface / Underwater Sensors, Air / Surface / Land / Underwater Weapons, Aircraft Range, each stating (Current: ON)), plus Show Non-friendly Range-Symbols, Merge Range-symbols, Sonobuoy Visibility, Reference Point Visibility, Illumination Vectors, Targetting Vectors, Datablocks, Datalinks, Contact Emissions, Plotted Courses, Mission area/course, Track Selected Unit (T), LOS Tool, Minimaps, and Terrain Type Legend — the last rendering a 17-class land-cover legend on the map. ### The architectural point — two stacks, two owners This is not the same surface as CMD-28.2, and the difference matters under ADR-010: | Stack | Content | Ownership | | --- | --- | --- | | Basemap layers (CMD-28.2) | Imagery, relief, borders, land cover — what the world looks like | UI-local; no sim meaning | | Tactical overlays (CMD-30) | Range envelopes, vectors, datalinks, courses — what the sim state looks like | Projections from the headless core | Two menus in the reference, two different owners. Conflating them would either plumb basemap toggles through the command bus, or make sim-derived overlays UI-local state that replay cannot reproduce. ### Sub-requirements - CMD-30.1 — Range symbology is a taxonomy, not a toggle. Eight independent controls across \{Air, Surface, Underwater\} × \{Sensors, Weapons\} plus Land Weapons and Aircraft Range. CMD-21 is a subset of this, not a synonym — CMD-21 is the Phase A baseline for the selected unit; CMD-30.1 is the picture-wide taxonomy. - CMD-30.2 — Non-friendly range symbols are beliefs. Estimated hostile envelopes are a major tactical affordance, but they are inference (CMD-29 epistemics) and must not render identically to own-force envelopes, which are known. - CMD-30.3 — Merged range symbols are Phase A decluttering, not Phase N LOD. REQ-20 discusses decluttering only under APP-6 LOD and the 5k@60 north-star (CMD-13/15, Phase N). Merging overlapping envelopes into a hull is cheap, needs no LOD product, and becomes necessary long before 5,000 symbols. Same baseline-versus-deferred split as CMD-21 — do not let it ride along with the LOD work. - CMD-30.4 — State in text, not colour alone. The reference writes (Current: ON) beside each colour chip. Adopt it: satisfies CMD-12 by construction and makes the menu readable without decoding swatches. - CMD-30.5 — Engagement geometry overlays. Illumination and targeting vectors — who is illuminating or targeting whom (doc 14). Pairs with CMD-11 intent preview. - CMD-30.6 — Connectivity and emissions. Datalinks are modelled (9 datalink types in src/); EMCON is modelled (EmconState, CatalogEmcon, CatalogRadarEmconResolver) though emissions as a distinct concept are not. Links docs 15 and 19 to the map. - CMD-30.7 — Route and mission-area overlays. - CMD-30.8 — Datablocks. Configurable symbol labels — the density knob that decides whether a dense picture is readable. Not modelled. - CMD-30.9 — Camera and analysis tools. Track-selected-unit, LOS tool, minimaps. None modelled. - CMD-30.10 — Legends for data-driven colouring. The reference pairs its land-cover layer with a 17-class legend. Any layer whose colour encodes a taxonomy needs one — without it the colouring is decoration the player cannot decode. - CMD-30.11 — Group / Unit view toggle, complementing CMD-07 (§4.4). > ⚠️ Colour budget — worth an explicit audit. Eight range-symbol colours, plus affiliation colours (CMD-12, which must stay colourblind-safe), plus seventeen land-cover classes, plus severity and diff colours. The colour channel is heavily oversubscribed, and adding overlays without a palette audit will collide with the accessibility commitment REQ-20 has already made. --- # 🔍 Original observation — now filed as CMD-29 above The same screenshot shows a Contact Status panel that is structurally different from the Unit Status panel reviewed earlier — and REQ-20 does not distinguish them. For a detected hostile (SAM Bn (SA-3b)) it shows: classification (Building (Revetted)), WRA line (Land Structure - Soft - Building (Revetted)), side, course/speed, a Contact Report… action, Damage / BDA / Damage Ctrl, and a DETECTIONS section reading "Detected by: Automatic detection on \[Unknown\]". REQ-20's Right-panel row specifies only "Selected unit/group: status, sensors, weapons, fuel, doctrine" — own-unit data. Selecting a contact has no specified panel, yet a contact answers different questions: how do I know it is there, how confident am I, what is it classified as, and may I shoot it. Unlike most gaps in this series, the data largely exists: ContactSummaryProjection, ContactPictureProjection, ContactPictureEntry, and BdaContactDamageStates are all in src/ProjectAegis.Delegation/Projection/, and WRA appears in the engage path (EngagementAbortReason, MvpEngagementResolver). The gap is specification, not model. The "Detected by" line is the most interesting part for Aegis — detection provenance connects doc 15 (sensor/detection) to the "why can't I fire?" explain surface (CMD-11), and to the comms-staleness question in CMD-17. Say tentatively: this may be the single highest-value contact-panel element. Not filed as CMD-29 — it was not the request. Flagged so it is not lost. --- # Proposed amendments to existing requirements | Existing | Amendment | | --- | --- | | CMD-04 Top bar | Absorb CMD-22; state the time model (multiplier vs time-per-step) explicitly | | CMD-09 Delegation badges | Note per-axis granularity per CMD-19 — a unit-level tri-state badge cannot express "mixed" | | CMD-10 Context menus | Note toolbar parity per CMD-16; both paths, not one | | CMD-06 Map symbol picture | Clarify that CMD-20 and CMD-21 are Phase A baseline, not Phase N with the product globe | | Layout Zones table | Add a sixth zone for the order toolbar (CMD-16) | # Minor observations, not filed as requirements - Crew proficiency — the reference shows Regular on the unit panel. Aegis models agent traits and attention; whether crew quality is player-visible is a design question, not a UI gap. - Named map areas — the reference labels a "Designated Pirate Staging Area" directly on the map. REQ-20 says "mission areas / reference points as projection data permits," which is vague about labelling. - Disabled menu items — Quick Jump and Contacts are greyed with no stated reason, the same disabled-without-explanation pattern flagged in the editor reviews. Worth not inheriting. - Selection stated three times — top-left label, map ring, and right-panel header. Deliberate redundancy for a dense screen; worth keeping in mind when trimming. --- > OPEN QUESTION: Should these land as new CMD rows in REQ-20, or as a Phase-2 addendum? REQ-20 is Status: Draft — Template B (Wave 2 re-honesty) with a carefully maintained honesty column; adding eight P0/P1 rows shifts its completion picture and should be a deliberate edit, not a drive-by. > OPEN QUESTION: CMD-17 and CMD-19 both imply projection changes, not just view work — per-axis autonomy state and comms-staleness have to reach the panel from the headless core. Are those projections already shaped for it, or is this an ADR-010 contract change? > OPEN QUESTION: How much CMO parity is actually wanted? REQ-20 tracks parity area-by-area against the manual, but Aegis's differentiator is agent delegation — CMD-19 is the one proposal here that has no CMO equivalent worth copying, because CMO has no agents to delegate to.

wiki_pages.note: ## Linear delivery tracking | Item | Link | | --- | --- | | Milestone | H8 — Drone Swarm Platforms (cmano-clone) | | Epic | [DRG-83](https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-83) | | Next action | [DRG-86](https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-86) A1 Catalog/schema (Wave 2) — Todo | | Issue map | [Linear tracking — Drone Swarm Platforms (H8)](https://app.notion.com/p/3b7f7cb4e4df81ad90e9fff052fff79e) | Status, comments, and progress live in Linear. This page remains the requirements draft until landed in Git. --- ## Downloadable artifact Portable Markdown index of SWARM-01…SWARM-30 for offline / PR attachment. --- Type: Requirements proposal — draft corpus for a new requirements doc (or amendment set), not a replacement for existing REQ files Status: Landed / superseded for content — merged [PR #412](https://github.com/drgaciw/cmano-clone/pull/412) → Game-Requirements/requirements/22-Drone-Swarm-Platforms.md on main (commit 9b328dd). Date: 2026-08-09 Canonical home (landed path): Game-Requirements/requirements/22-Drone-Swarm-Platforms.md + amendment pointers on 01, 14–21 · PR [#412](https://github.com/drgaciw/cmano-clone/pull/412) Method: Research synthesis + Aegis architecture fit (see sibling research page) Related research: Drone Swarm Platforms — Research (2026-08-09) Related Linear Milestone: H8 — Drone Swarm Platforms · Epic [DRG-83](https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-83) ## Read this first — what this is not This is not a design page under the 8-section template, and not a claim that CMO already has swarm platforms. It is a proposed requirements delta so the project can decide whether swarms are in charter, which phase, and which existing docs they amend. Git is SoT. Landed: [PR #412](https://github.com/drgaciw/cmano-clone/pull/412) → Game-Requirements/requirements/22-Drone-Swarm-Platforms.md. This Notion page is superseded for content (keep for research history / attachments). Depends on research: [Drone Swarm Platforms — Research (2026-08-09)](https://app.notion.com/p/3b7f7cb4e4df81428f39e8423877957b) --- # Proposed requirement index | ID | Requirement | Priority | Phase | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | SWARM-01 | Swarm as first-class platform type | P0 | A | | SWARM-02 | Aggregate integrity state (droneCount) | P0 | A | | SWARM-03 | Intent orders: Move, Attack, Hold | P0 | A | | SWARM-04 | Combat DPS/ISR scale with living drones | P0 | A | | SWARM-05 | Single selection / OOB node | P0 | A | | SWARM-06 | Headless logged swarm intents | P0 | A | | SWARM-07 | Deterministic aggregate engagement SoT | P0 | A | | SWARM-08 | At least one hard counter interaction | P0 | A | | SWARM-09 | Map integrity + density readout | P0 | A | | SWARM-10 | Modes: Hold, Assault, Screen, Scatter, Rejoin | P1 | B | | SWARM-11 | Host / mothership link | P1 | B | | SWARM-12 | LinkState connected/degraded/lost | P1 | B | | SWARM-13 | Regen near host/base (logistics-gated) | P1 | B | | SWARM-14 | C2 mode + integrity panel fields | P1 | B | | SWARM-15 | Doctrine / WRA for expend and auto-engage | P1 | B | | SWARM-16 | Formations: cloud, wall, spear, orbit | P2 | C | | SWARM-17 | Multi-axis auto-split assault | P2 | C | | SWARM-18 | EMP / jam soft-kill effects | P2 | C | | SWARM-19 | Expend / kamikaze pulse (authorized) | P2 | C | | SWARM-20 | Mission types for swarm tasking | P2 | C | | SWARM-21 | Catalog + Platform Editor authoring | P1 | B/C | | SWARM-22 | Scenario editor place/configure swarm | P1 | B | | SWARM-23 | Agent delegation compatibility | P1 | B | | SWARM-24 | Replay: orders + integrity deltas | P0 | A | | SWARM-25 | Performance / render LOD caps | P0 | A | | SWARM-26 | Contact classification for swarms | P1 | B | | SWARM-27 | Split / merge swarm platforms | P3 | N | | SWARM-28 | Per-member full physics SoT | P3 | N / Won't for MVP | | SWARM-29 | True multi-static ISR mesh | P3 | N | | SWARM-30 | Full MUM-T package with manned flight leads | P3 | N | --- # Phase A — Must ship for MVP ## SWARM-01 — Swarm is a first-class platform type \[P0\] Requirement. The catalog and sim shall support a platform type (or type flag) representing a drone/UAS swarm that can be instantiated as a side-owned unit alongside ships, aircraft, and facilities. Why. Without a platform type, swarms are either fake groups of N aircraft (micro hell, wrong logistics) or pure VFX. Acceptance. A scenario can spawn at least one swarm unit; it appears in OOB and accepts selection. ## SWARM-02 — Aggregate integrity \[P0\] Requirement. A swarm unit shall expose droneCount / maxDrones (or equivalent pool HP that maps 1:1 to count). Destruction of the platform occurs when integrity reaches zero. Acceptance. Damage events reduce count; UI/projections show remaining integrity; at 0 the unit is destroyed/removed per normal unit death rules. ## SWARM-03 — Intent orders: Move, Attack, Hold \[P0\] Requirement. The unit shall accept at least Move (plot/course or mission point), Attack (engage target/auto), and Hold (loiter/station) without requiring selection of individual drones. Acceptance. Headless commands exist; C2 can issue them; swarm centroid follows / engages accordingly. ## SWARM-04 — Effects scale with living drones \[P0\] Requirement. Offensive output and sensor effectiveness shall scale with living drone count (monotonic; exact curve is a tuning knob). Acceptance. Full swarm detects/engages more effectively than a half-depleted swarm under identical geometry; golden or unit tests lock the curve. ## SWARM-05 — Single selection node \[P0\] Requirement. Selection, map symbol, and OOB entry treat the swarm as one unit. Per-drone selection is out of scope for Phase A. Acceptance. Clicking the swarm selects one unit id; multi-select behaves like any other unit. ## SWARM-06 — Headless logged intents \[P0\] Requirement. Per ADR-010 patterns, swarm orders shall be headless commands that produce order-log rows (or equivalent deterministic intents), not UI-only gestures. Acceptance. CLI/MCP or existing command path can move/attack a swarm; replay consumes the same intents. ## SWARM-07 — Deterministic aggregate engagement SoT \[P0\] Requirement. Detection, fire, and damage resolution shall use aggregate swarm state, not non-deterministic per-drone physics, as the source of truth. Acceptance. Same scenario + seed → same integrity timeline; cosmetic member layout may be seeded but must not drive outcomes. ## SWARM-08 — Hard counter interaction \[P0\] Requirement. At least one weapon/system class (e.g. area AA / flak / CIWS profile) shall be demonstrably effective at shredding swarm integrity faster than point-fire against a conventional airframe of similar cost band. Acceptance. Documented test scenario where swarm dies to area AA while surviving longer against single-target fire of equal nominal DPS. ## SWARM-09 — Map integrity + density readout \[P0\] Requirement. Map and/or unit panel shall show remaining integrity (count or bar) and a density/affiliation-safe symbol distinct from a single light aircraft where feasible. Acceptance. Player can read swarm health without opening a deep inspector; color alone is not the only channel (CMD-12 alignment). ## SWARM-24 — Replay integrity \[P0\] Requirement. Replay/fixtures shall reconstruct swarm orders and integrity-affecting events. Member cosmetics need not be bit-identical if seeded consistently. Acceptance. Golden replay or world-hash path includes swarm integrity deltas. ## SWARM-25 — Performance caps \[P0\] Requirement. Logical drone count and rendered member count shall be independently capped; Phase A combat must remain aggregate so large logical counts do not imply O(n) engagement work per pulse. Acceptance. Profiled scenario with design-max swarms meets project frame/pulse budgets (state numbers when landed in REQ NFR). --- # Phase B — Modes, host, C2, authoring ## SWARM-10 — Operational modes \[P1\] Requirement. Swarm shall support modes: Hold, Assault, Screen, Scatter, Rejoin. Mode changes are orders (logged). Acceptance. Mode is visible in projection; behavior differs in at least movement posture and engagement aggressiveness. ## SWARM-11 — Host / mothership \[P1\] Requirement. A swarm may designate a host unit (ship/vehicle/aircraft/base). Screen mode prefers orbiting the host. Host loss triggers doctrine last-order. Acceptance. Scenario can bind hostId; Screen keeps swarm near host; host death produces a defined autonomous reaction. ## SWARM-12 — LinkState \[P1\] Requirement. Swarm shall track linkState ∈ \{connected, degraded, lost\} driven by range, jam, and host/comms rules consistent with project comms degradation themes. Acceptance. Lost link blocks or delays new player orders per doctrine; panel shows cause (CMD-17 pattern: unknown-with-reason, not blank). ## SWARM-13 — Regeneration \[P1\] Requirement. Near a valid host/base with stores, swarm may regenerate drones over time up to maxDrones, subject to logistics rules. Acceptance. Without stores, regen does not occur; with stores, count climbs on a documented rate. ## SWARM-14 — C2 panel fields \[P1\] Requirement. Selected swarm unit panel shows: mode, integrity (count/max), energy/endurance if modelled, host, linkState, and primary sensor/weapon summary. Acceptance. Fields update live; missing telemetry uses explicit unknown reasons when link lost. ## SWARM-15 — Doctrine / WRA \[P1\] Requirement. Doctrine shall control auto-engage posture and whether expend (if present) is authorized. WRA classification for swarm munitions/target classes shall be expressible. Acceptance. Hold-fire prevents assault shots; authorized expend is the only path to SWARM-19 when that ships. ## SWARM-21 — Catalog + Platform Editor \[P1\] Requirement. Authors can define swarm catalog entries: maxDrones, sensors, weapons/munition class, speed/endurance bands, default mode, host constraints. Acceptance. Platform Editor / PDA path can create a valid swarm db entry consumed by sim. ## SWARM-22 — Scenario editor \[P1\] Requirement. Scenario editor can place swarms, set initial count ≤ max, assign side/host/mission. Acceptance. Round-trip save/load preserves swarm fields; validation catches count > max and missing catalog refs. ## SWARM-23 — Agent delegation \[P1\] Requirement. Delegated agents may issue the same intent orders as humans to swarm units; per-axis or unit-level delegation badges apply as for other units. Acceptance. Agent can task swarm assault/screen without UI; order log attributes actor correctly. ## SWARM-26 — Contact classification \[P1\] Requirement. Hostile swarms as contacts expose classification that can distinguish swarm/UAS cloud from single airframe when sensors allow, with confidence (CMD-29 alignment). Acceptance. Contact panel/projection can show swarm-class label when identified; misclassification possible at low quality. --- # Phase C — Depth ## SWARM-16 — Formations \[P2\] Cloud, wall/screen, spear, orbit as soft constraints on member layout and engagement geometry. ## SWARM-17 — Multi-axis auto-split \[P2\] Assault may split logical mass across approach axes against a single high-value target when doctrine allows. ## SWARM-18 — EMP / jam soft-kill \[P2\] EMP scatters/freezes mode switches temporarily; jam degrades linkState and order latency. ## SWARM-19 — Expend pulse \[P2\] Authorized order spends N drones for a burst strike; irreversible; logged. ## SWARM-20 — Mission integration \[P2\] Patrol / support / strike mission types can assign swarms with swarm-appropriate default modes. --- # Phase N / Won't for MVP ## SWARM-27 — Split / merge \[P3\] Split one swarm platform into two; merge compatible swarms. High UX and identity cost — defer. ## SWARM-28 — Per-member physics SoT \[P3 / Won't MVP\] Individual drone bodies as engagement authority. Conflicts with SWARM-07; only if product fantasy demands it and replay strategy is redesigned. ## SWARM-29 — Multi-static ISR mesh \[P3\] True distributed sensing geometry beyond scaled aggregate quality. ## SWARM-30 — Full MUM-T packages \[P3\] Manned flight leads with organic swarms as a package type — after host + air ops maturity. --- # Proposed amendments to existing requirements (if accepted) | Existing | Amendment | | --- | --- | | Entity / unit model (M2 / related REQ) | Add swarm platform flag, integrity fields, hostId, linkState, mode | | REQ-18 Combat Domains | Clarify Air vs new UAS-swarm aspect; damage model for integrity pools | | Sensors / doc 15 | Aggregate ISR scaling; contact class for swarms | | Weapons / doc 14 | Area-AA vs swarm; expend salvo; CIWS interaction notes | | Logistics / REQ-16 | Regen stores; host magazine coupling | | Comms / doc 19 | LinkState for swarm C2 | | REQ-20 C2 UI | Panel fields (SWARM-14); map density; no per-drone micro | | CMD-24 Air Ops | Decision: shared window vs Swarm Ops | | Replay / fixtures | Integrity deltas in golden paths | | Platform Editor / doc 21 | Authoring schema for swarm entries | | doc 01 Project Overview | Charter check: are swarms in scope for air/naval interaction? | --- # Suggested starter tuning (non-normative) | Knob | Starter | | --- | --- | | maxDrones | 40 logical | | renderMembers | 24 cap | | dpsPerDrone | tune vs soft targets | | regen | 1 drone / 1.5s near host if stores | | scatter cooldown | 8s | | armorClass | light-air | --- # Acceptance criteria — Phase A done when 1. Swarm platform spawns, selects, moves, attacks as one unit 2. Losing drones weakens sensors/weapons measurably 3. At least one hard counter shreds integrity faster than point fire 4. Orders are headless + logged; replay/hash stable 5. Map/panel show integrity without per-drone UI 6. Performance caps documented and met in a stress scenario --- # Owner triage (2026-08-09) — DECIDED Closed by: delegated decision (owner → Grok Build) · Linear [DRG-84](https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-84) · Workflow [H8](https://app.notion.com/p/3b7f7cb4e4df818fb428ff449ffe1cb3) | # | Question | Decision | | --- | --- | --- | | T1 | Charter — in scope under doc 01 air/naval now? | Yes — Phase A now. Core platform type under air/naval interaction; not deferred to Phase N fiction. | | T2 | Corpus shape | New Game-Requirements/requirements/NN-Drone-Swarm-Platforms.md (next free NN on land) plus amendment pointer bullets on entity model, weapons/14, sensors/15, logistics/16, combat domains/18, C2 UI/20. | | T3 | Air Ops vs Swarm Ops | Phase A: reuse existing unit panel / Air Ops surfaces. Phase B: dedicated Swarm Ops panel fields (SWARM-14). | | T4 | Phase A catalog | Abstract generic only — 1–2 generic swarm presets; national exemplars Phase B+. | | T5 | Boundary vs [DRG-47](https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-47) | Core air domain owns SWARM-01…26 delivery. Only SWARM-27…30 (split/merge, per-member SoT, multi-static mesh, full MUM-T) sit near REQ-09/10 speculative. | | Delivery | Who owns? | Epic [DRG-83](https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-83) · milestone H8 — Drone Swarm Platforms. | Land path: [DRG-85](https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-85) Done via [PR #412](https://github.com/drgaciw/cmano-clone/pull/412). Linear: DRG-84 Done → DRG-85 Done → DRG-86 Todo. ### Former open questions All five open questions above are resolved by this triage. Do not re-open without a new ADR / milestone note. --- # Provenance Research basis: sibling page Drone Swarm Platforms — Research (2026-08-09). Pattern modelled on Main Game Window — Proposed C2 UI Requirements (CMD-16…CMD-30).

wiki_pages.title: 🎯 Combat Interaction UX — Proposed Requirements and Vertical Slice
wiki_pages.note:
## Four-system delivery contract - Notion: requirements, slice framing, acceptance gates, and design decisions. - Linear: milestones, epics, stories, ownership, dependencies, and delivery status. - GitHub: code, pull-request review, CI evidence, merge history, and release provenance. - Graphite: atomic branch stacks and pull-request ordering; each layer remains independently reviewable. ### Required traceability Every Linear implementation story links to this requirements page. Every GitHub pull request names its Linear story, links the relevant Notion requirement, states acceptance criteria and test evidence, and records its Graphite stack position when applicable. On merge, the Linear story records the merged pull request and moves only when its acceptance criteria are verified. --- ## Delivery roadmap Linear is the execution system of record; this page is the requirements and design source. Each delivery epic and story links back here rather than duplicating its full specification. - Slice A — Sense and target: Find, Fix, Track, Target; contact-state projection, information quality, authority and ROE, sensor-to-shooter traceability, and a targetability scenario. - Slice B — Engage and assess: Target, Engage, Assess; event contract, missile/gun/laser rendering, explanation, contact combat card, replay, and accessibility. - Slice C — Command, learn, adapt: confidence-aware recommendations, after-action review, sensor/EW understanding, damage state, and formation coordination. - Cross-cutting readiness: performance and declutter budgets, usability scenarios, and kill-chain traceability. - Slice G - Unity UX/UI rebaseline and acceptance: Slice G - Unity UX/UI Rebaseline and Acceptance extends acceptance across C2 and Mission/Platform Editor surfaces, reusing existing A-C and cross-cutting stories. [DRG-233](https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-233) owns delivery; this addition does not close any existing acceptance gate. --- Delivery status (Linear 2026-09-04): Headless Combat UX stories DRG-206–230 are Done on main @ 6f80d226 (#610 docs W1-HUB). Wave 5 leftovers (#600–#603) remain on main. This page stays the requirements SoT. Update 2026-09-30: UI stories proceed under the authorized S122.0–S127 evidence rebaseline. DRG-180/181/182 are Done in live Linear; DRG-183/169/258/197 are In Progress. Owner Play Mode [DRG-208](https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-208) remains Todo and human-only at Linear-reported integration1902dc1299678ea17f75014406fd9c616e5576bd. It is an acceptance gate for the program. The current roadmap and mandatory QA plan separate delivery status, retained technical evidence and owner acceptance. Proposed VER-07.3–6 strengthens revision provenance under DRG-201/244. Do not treat this page as a second board. ## Slice framing ### Slice A — Sense and target Find → Fix → Track → Target. A player can trace a contact from detection to targetability, including provenance, confidence, freshness, comms state, classification, authority, and rules-of-engagement constraints. ### Slice B — Engage and assess Target → Engage → Assess. The existing vertical slice proves a missile, gun, and laser engagement from command through outcome, explanation, accessible symbology, replay, and assessment. ### Slice C — Command, learn, and adapt Observe → Orient → Decide → Act. The player reviews outcomes, receives clearly non-authoritative recommendations, commands formations within delegated authority, and updates intent using battle-damage assessment. ## Cross-cutting requirement lenses - Command and control: make authority to observe, recommend, approve, engage, abort, and delegate explicit. - Sensor-to-shooter: preserve traceability from detection through firing solution to engagement and assessment. - Rules of engagement and escalation: explain permitted, withheld, and approval-required actions. - Information quality: distinguish confidence, provenance, freshness, comms loss, and genuine unknowns. - Mission command and BDA: express intent and constraints, then support retasking, withdrawal, or re-attack from assessed results. --- Status: Accepted for headless delivery; UI/render in progress under S122–S127, owner acceptance via [DRG-208](https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-208).
Purpose: Requirements and slice framing. Linear holds story status.
Scope: Cross-domain C2 presentation only. The simulation remains the source of combat facts; the UI renders projections and submits commands through the approved boundary. --- ## Recommended requirement set ### CMB-UI-01 — Combat event grammar \\\[P0\\\] Every player-visible engagement shall have a consistent lifecycle: intent accepted, authorization or refusal, weapon launch or firing, in-flight or sustained effect where applicable, terminal outcome, and replay correlation. The event payload shall identify shooter, target, weapon family, outcome, and explanation reference. ### CMB-UI-02 — Weapon-family symbology \\\[P0\\\] The tactical map shall distinguish missile, gun, and laser engagements without depending on color alone. Each family shall have distinct iconography, line behavior, motion treatment, and accessible text or tooltip labels. The same semantics shall appear in the event log and replay. ### CMB-UI-03 — Engagement explanation \\\[P0\\\] For a selected engagement or blocked order, the player shall be able to see firing solution state, hard constraints, doctrine or policy constraints, sensor/contact confidence, selected weapon, and the actionable reason for refusal. ### CMB-UI-04 — Contact combat card \\\[P0\\\] A selected contact shall have a presentation distinct from an own-unit panel. It shall show identity confidence, detection provenance and freshness, posture, targetability, associated engagement status, and battle-damage assessment when known. ### CMB-UI-05 — Scale-aware declutter and accessibility \\\[P0\\\] At operational scale, salvos and gun bursts shall aggregate while selected or replay-inspected engagements remain explorable. Weapon family, affiliation, clearance, and outcome shall use redundant channels: shape, line style, label, and color. --- ## Vertical slice One deterministic scenario shall show one shooter and one target for each family: missile, gun, and laser. It shall prove command acceptance, permitted and refused engagement states, event ordering, map symbology, impact or miss, event-log correlation, replay determinism, and usable presentation at tactical and operational zoom. --- ## Story sequence 1. Combat event projection contract — headless projection with replay correlation; blocks all UI stories. 2. Missile, gun, and laser renderer — consumes only the event projection; validates the visual vocabulary. 3. Engagement explain surface — connects selected event to constraints and doctrine reasoning. 4. Contact combat card — provides provenance, confidence, targeting state, and BDA. 5. Declutter and accessibility pass — validates three zoom bands and non-color-only recognition. 6. Replay acceptance harness — asserts event-to-render outcomes across the vertical slice. --- ## Acceptance gates - A user can identify shooter, target, weapon family, and outcome without opening a detail panel. - A blocked shot states the reason and the next corrective action when one exists. - Replay emits the same combat event sequence and yields the same presentation state. - Weapon family and outcome remain distinguishable in a non-color-only mode. - No presentation code derives combat truth independently from the simulation projection. --- ## Dependencies and boundaries - Reuse existing sensor and weapon envelope overlays; do not rebuild them. - Keep the simulation and C2 command contracts headless-first. - Do not start implementation until this draft is accepted and placed in a newly authorized delivery scope. --- ## References - [Combat domains and damage](https://app.notion.com/p/3a7f7cb4e4df816995d5d02e5d5bd9ec) - [C2 UI requirements delta](https://app.notion.com/p/3aaf7cb4e4df816992cff848b5532378) - [Unity UI maturity plan](https://app.notion.com/p/3abf7cb4e4df812f8128c528ce3f3f7b) - [Command UI reference](https://command.matrixgames.com/?page_id=2697) Any Sensor, Best Shooter — Derived Requirements IBCS-Informed Combat C2 Framework — Derived Requirements Agentic Combat Capabilities — Proposed Requirements QA Gauntlet Architecture — Requirements and Delivery Sequence

wiki_pages.title: SYM-MIL-01 — Military Tactical Symbology (NTDS / APP-6 / MIL-STD-2525)
wiki_pages.note: ## Traceability Design requirement: SYM-MIL-01. Delivery: [DRG-231](https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-231). Linear owns delivery status; this page owns the draft design and acceptance criteria. Local draft mirror: Game-Requirements/drafts/2026-09-05-military-tactical-symbology.md (uncommitted working copy, not a landed Git source). Linked from REQ-20 and the local Game Requirements index. Paired profile: [SYM-CIV-01](https://app.notion.com/p/3d2f7cb4e4df81a68f32f174cabcd48d). ## Requirement — SYM-MIL-01 Project Aegis shall provide a selectable Military Tactical symbology profile for U.S. Navy surface ships and the other supported unit/contact domains. The profile shall use documented NTDS naval display conventions and an explicitly versioned mapping to NATO APP-6 and U.S. MIL-STD-2525, informed by the CMANO/CMO tactical-display reference experience. ## Standards and reference interpretation CMO's official UI addendum names its military symbol option NTDS + NATO APP-6, alongside a Stylized option. MIL-STD-2525 is the U.S. joint military symbology standard; APP-6 is the NATO standard family. These names must not be treated as interchangeable or as evidence that CMO implements every provision of MIL-STD-2525. The supplied NTIS link identifies the 2007 Common Navy Warfighting Display Symbology Implementation Guide (ADA484484), not the standard itself. Its abstract describes maritime implementation of MIL-STD-2525 and additional Navy modifiers from NTDS/SSDS. Use this as supporting naval guidance; document deviations from the selected standard. DLA lists MIL-STD-2525 Revision E Change 1, dated 2025-03-02. Proposed implementation baseline: that revision for the U.S. mapping; the exact APP-6 edition and NTDS subset must be pinned in the mapping specification before artwork implementation. This is a documented subset requirement, not a claim of formal standards certification. ## Acceptance criteria - MIL-AC-01: Map options expose a clearly named Military Tactical profile and an in-game legend identifying its selected standards editions and any custom deviations. - MIL-AC-02: A versioned symbol mapping manifest records semantic key, domain, affiliation, known platform category, frame/icon/modifiers, source edition or guide section, and fallback for every supported symbol. Missing entries use a documented generic unknown symbol. - MIL-AC-03: The naval test atlas covers at least carrier, destroyer, cruiser, frigate, amphibious, support/auxiliary, and unknown surface vessel categories when known to the observer. Any category unsupported by the chosen standard has an explicit generic fallback; symbols must not invent class-level identification. - MIL-AC-04: Friendly, hostile, neutral, and unknown tracks are distinguishable by shape/frame and text/legend, not color alone. A U.S. Navy platform's nationality does not automatically make it friendly; displayed affiliation follows the observer's projected knowledge. - MIL-AC-05: Domain, affiliation, heading when known, selection, and observed contact quality/status remain readable at supported zoom/UI scales. Selection and command/outcome overlays must not overwrite or contradict symbol identity. Unobserved damage and platform type stay undisclosed. - MIL-AC-06: Map, OOB, and detail views identify the same selected entity, including contact-to-unit selection transitions. Switching to/from the civilian profile preserves selection, camera position, simulation time, and active orders. - MIL-AC-07: Headless mapping/unknown-fallback tests plus a Unity visual atlas review prove conformance to the declared subset and document any deviations. Asset provenance is retained; CMANO/CMO are behavior references, not a source of copied proprietary artwork. ## Sources - [CMO official UI addendum — Map Symbols](https://command.matrixgames.com/?page_id=2697) - [DLA official MIL-STD-2525 record](https://quicksearch.dla.mil/qsDocDetails.aspx?ident_number=114934) - [NTIS / Naval Surface Warfare Center naval symbology guide, ADA484484](https://ntrl.ntis.gov/NTRL/dashboard/searchResults/titleDetail/ADA484484.xhtml) - [User-supplied NTDS discussion — contextual only, not a normative standard](https://forum.finescale.com/t/navy-command-symbols/132729) ## Boundaries and delivery Status: Draft requirement, recorded 2026-09-05 at the user's request. Implementation is not started or scheduled. This addition does not mark existing map symbology complete or reopen a release milestone. Related requirements: REQ-20 / CMD-06 (map picture), CMD-07 (selection sync), CMD-12 (accessibility), CMD-13 (APP-6/LOD), CMD-28 (map options), CMD-29 (contact knowledge), and CMD-30 (tactical overlays). Architecture: presentation reads existing observer-side projections and preserves ADR-010 §§2–3, ADR-007, and ADR-001. Changing a symbol profile must not change simulation state, orders, ROE, ownership, visibility, contact knowledge, or replay hashes. Missing or uncertain information must remain missing or uncertain. Verification: headless mapping/semantic tests first, then Unity Game view UAT and retained screenshots. Verify selection and contact provenance in both profiles, including unknown, stale/lost, and degraded-comms tracks.

This is an alternate visual vocabulary over the same tactical picture, not an easier simulation or a change to military/civilian affiliation. ## Scope assumption requiring review The user's phrase custom civilian symbology is provisionally interpreted as a simplified display profile for all supported units, not only icons for civilian vessels. A clarification question has been sent. If the intended scope is civilian vessel/traffic categories only, revise this requirement before implementation. The requirement is Draft and the Linear item remains Backlog. ## Acceptance criteria - CIV-AC-01: Map options expose Civilian-Friendly alongside Military Tactical, with a preview and plain-language legend. The chosen profile persists across application restarts; both profiles remain selectable. First-run default is a separate product decision, not changed by this requirement. - CIV-AC-02: Original, consistent silhouettes/pictograms cover surface vessels, submarines, aircraft/UAS, ground units, and unknown contacts already supported by the scenario. Civilian vessel categories may include merchant, tanker, fishing, passenger, and pleasure craft only when the observer knows that category; otherwise use a generic vessel/unknown contact. - CIV-AC-03: Affiliation uses redundant shape/badge and text cues as well as color. Unknown/stale/lost/degraded information remains explicit; heading is shown only when known. No recognizable silhouette may reveal an unclassified enemy platform. - CIV-AC-05: Switching profiles during paused or running gameplay preserves camera, selected entity, OOB/detail synchronization, command availability, orders, and replay outcomes. Record sample size, fixtures, answers, and screenshots; missing evidence is not a pass. - CIV-AC-08: Headless profile-parity/fallback tests and Unity mouse/keyboard UAT show all declared categories render without missing icons, selection drift, hidden-information leaks, or altered command behavior. ## Reference and originality - [CMO official UI addendum — military and stylized symbol choices](https://command.matrixgames.com/?page_id=2697) provides precedent for player-selectable profiles. - The artwork and style guide are original Project Aegis gameplay assets. No assertion of MIL-STD-2525/APP-6 compliance is made for the civilian-friendly glyphs. ## Boundaries and delivery Status: Draft requirement, recorded 2026-09-05 at the user's request.
