wiki_pages.title: Milsim Comparative Research & New Requirements — 2026-10-07
wiki_pages.note: Status: Draft / owner-review-pending. Clean-room: the features below are inspired by public descriptions only. No proprietary databases, scenarios, or code are reused. ## 1. Research summary (public sources) | Title | Relevant traits | Source | | --- | --- | --- | | Command: Modern Operations (CMO) | Joint air/naval/subsurface/ground/space/cyber; global 3D globe; EW and C4ISR | [https://store.steampowered.com/app/1076160/Command\_Modern\_Operations/](https://store.steampowered.com/app/1076160/Command_Modern_Operations/) | | CMO comms disruption (ex-"Chains of War") | Units cut off from the comms grid lose direct control; on rejoin, contact merges are reported and no-info merges omitted. Realistic sub comms: subs below 40 m go off-grid and show last-reported position; ELF "bell-ringer" recall | [https://command.matrixgames.com/?p=4990](https://command.matrixgames.com/?p=4990) | | CMO aircrew/EW | Frequency-agile and AESA radars resist noise jamming and Doppler notching; beaming vs pulse-Doppler radars depends on crew skill; G-strain; detailed aircraft damage instead of one-hit kills | [https://command.matrixgames.com/?p=4990](https://command.matrixgames.com/?p=4990) | | CMO environment/sensors | 11 cloud profiles, flying below/within/above clouds; sonar reverberation from shallow water and ice scales with sonar tech level and frequency; passive bearing gates (4°–20°); heavy seas hurt small ships' unguided fire; NCTR (JEM, NBILST) | [https://command.matrixgames.com/?page\_id=2711](https://command.matrixgames.com/?page_id=2711) | | CMO comms jamming | Comms jamming moved from Professional Edition into CMO in v1.08, along with drone autonomy levels | [https://steamdb.info/patchnotes/18808439/](https://steamdb.info/patchnotes/18808439/) | | Harpoon series | Real-time with time compression; one to thousands of platforms; scenario editor; Harpoon ANW (2006) added human-vs-human play | [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harpoon\_(series)]() | | Sea Power | Dynamic time of day and weather; ECM; mission editor and global map; branching campaign; theater dynamic campaign (beta mid-2026); AI scripting for mission makers | [https://store.steampowered.com/app/1286220](https://store.steampowered.com/app/1286220) | | Cold Waters / sub sims | Serious sub sims are built on the passive sonar equation | [https://signallockapp.com/guides/submarine-simulator-history](https://signallockapp.com/guides/submarine-simulator-history) | ## 2. Code-base review (drgaciw/cmano-clone @ main, 2026-10-07) Present: Sim/Engage (DLZ, magazine ledger, domain validators incl. Subsurface/Mine, Winchester/Bingo/Shotgun gates, hypersonic, CEC remote engage, BDA), Sim/Sensors (deterministic detection loop, IR/visual, PD contact sim, ScenarioJamResolver, datalink picture merger), Sim/Logistics (air/boat ops FSMs, FuelLedger, ScenarioSeaState), Delegation/Comms (CommsState, CommsOrderDelay, track staleness, spoof timeline), Delegation/EmconPosture, Mission Editor CLI, replay/save work (H6, DRG-325/329/349). Gaps found by code search (0 non-test hits): weather/cloud layers in sensors, thermocline/convergence zones/sonar propagation, decoys/chaff/flares/countermeasures, sonobuoys, terrain/radar-horizon LOS (1 hit only), torpedo modeling (1 hit), comms jamming tied to Sim authority, damage control/flooding (minimal), campaign layer, multiplayer/lockstep (only ADR stage). Linear search found no issues for weather, acoustic, sonar, countermeasure, torpedo, or terrain. ## 3. New requirements Each must stay inside Sim authority, be deterministic (seeded, same-build replayable), and expose facts to presentation via existing projections. Presentation never computes outcomes. ### ENV — Environment - ENV-01 Weather & cloud-layer model. Scenario weather (cloud layers with base/top altitude and density, precipitation, wind, visibility, time-of-day lighting) as authored scenario data. AC: IR/visual detection gets a deterministic modifier per layer; a unit's altitude relative to layers is queryable; the editor validates layer ordering. - ENV-02 Terrain & radar-horizon line of sight. Earth-curvature radar horizon plus DEM-based terrain masking for low-altitude and ground units. AC: the detection loop rejects a sensor-target pair blocked by the horizon or terrain, with a reason code; there is a performance budget per tick. - ENV-03 Sea-state effects. Extend ScenarioSeaState so it affects small-ship unguided fire accuracy, low-flyer radar clutter, and boat-ops launch/recovery. AC: effects are tabulated and covered by tests per sea state. ### ASW — Undersea warfare - ASW-01 Acoustic propagation model. Simplified passive/active sonar equation (source level, transmission loss, noise, DI, DT) with layer depth, surface duct, convergence zones, and bottom bounce. AC: deterministic SNR → detection probability; shallow-water/under-ice reverberation scaled by sonar generation and frequency. - ASW-02 Platform acoustic signatures. Speed-dependent radiated noise, cavitation, and own-ship noise penalty on hull sonar. AC: catalog fields plus validation rules; sprint-and-drift behavior emerges. - ASW-03 Sonobuoys & dipping sonar. Expendable sensor fields with lifetime, depth setting, and datalink to parent. AC: the sonobuoy inventory uses MagazineLedger; buoy contacts merge through the datalink picture. - ASW-04 Torpedo engagement model. Torpedo as a simulated weapon entity (wire-guided, acoustic homing, run-to-enable, seeker cone, evasion). AC: resolves through IEngagementResolver; abort codes are added to EngagementAbortReasonCodes. - ASW-05 Passive bearing-only tracking. Bearing gates by sonar generation; target masking; TMA solution quality grows over time. AC: contact projections show bearing-only vs fixed position with uncertainty. ### EW — Electronic warfare & countermeasures - EW-01 Radar ECCM attributes. Frequency-agile/PESA/AESA flags and tech generation in the catalog; jammer vs. radar generation matrix in ScenarioJamResolver. AC: table-driven tests. - EW-02 Expendable countermeasures. Chaff, flares, towed and expendable decoys as magazine items with seeker-specific seduction probability. AC: engagement results record a countermeasure outcome; the BDA explanation shows the cause. - EW-03 Beaming / notching maneuver. Doctrine-triggered evasion versus pulse-Doppler radars, scaled by crew proficiency; ineffective against pulse-only radars. AC: deterministic outcome, explained in the engagement explanation. - EW-04 NCTR classification. JEM (frontal 15° arc) and imaging-based classification affect contact ID confidence. AC: contact lifecycle transitions include classification source. ### C3 — Communications authority - C3-01 Off-grid units in Sim. Promote Delegation/Comms state into a Sim-authoritative comms-grid membership. Off-grid units execute their last orders or doctrine and do not accept new direct orders. AC: the command façade rejects orders with an OffGrid reason; the UI shows the last-reported position. - C3-02 Rejoin reconciliation. On rejoin, merge the unit's contact picture into the side picture and emit a summary of informative merges only. AC: reported in the AAR/order log. - C3-03 Submarine comms depth & ELF recall. Subs below the comms depth go off-grid; an ELF recall order makes the sub attempt to come shallow, with a delay if threatened. AC: scenario toggle; deterministic test. - C3-04 Comms jamming. Area comms jammers degrade datalinks and command links and feed CommsOrderDelay. AC: CEC/mandatory-datalink pre-fire checks abort with a reason when the link is jammed. ### DMG — Damage & attrition - DMG-01 Component damage for aircraft. Replace one-hit kills with damage points plus component hits (engine, sensor, fuel leak) that drive RTB/Bingo. AC: hooks into CatalogDamageWithdrawEngageGate. - DMG-02 Ship damage control & flooding. Fires and flooding progress over time and are mitigated by crew quality; list and speed penalties. AC: deterministic progression; replay-stable. ### HUM — Crew / human factors - HUM-01 Crew proficiency. Five-level proficiency modifies OODA intervals, evasion, and DLZ personality. AC: a scenario-authored side/unit attribute. - HUM-02 G-strain & fatigue. Sustained hard maneuvering accumulates strain that degrades performance. AC: bounded state with tests. ### OPS — Operational layer - OPS-01 Time compression with safe-stop events. Harpoon/CMO-style compression that auto-drops to 1x on configurable events (new contact, weapon launch). AC: deterministic regardless of compression step. - OPS-02 Branching campaign. Linked scenarios with carry-over of losses and magazines plus story branches (Sea Power-style). AC: campaign manifest schema validated by the Mission Editor CLI. - OPS-03 Mission-maker AI scripting surface. A sandboxed, deterministic event/action scripting API over the existing trigger/event system. AC: the event debugger trace covers scripted actions; no direct Sim mutation outside the command façade. - OPS-04 Human-vs-human play (post-H6). Lockstep multiplayer gated on DRG-349 save/resume determinism. AC: a desync detector based on DetectionWorldHash. Dependency: DRG-325/329. ## 4. Suggested sequencing 1. ENV-02, EW-01, C3-01 (low cost, existing hooks). 2. ASW-01/02/05 (new subsystem; spike first). 3. EW-02/03, DMG-01, HUM-01. 4. ASW-03/04, C3-02/03/04, ENV-01/03. 5. OPS-01..03; OPS-04 after H6. ## 5. wiki_pages.title: Core Simulation Design
wiki_pages.note: Status: Draft — source reconciliation authored; owner review pending. Owner: drg amtd Related Linear Milestone: M3 / Core — S122–S127 evidence rebaseline. Last updated: 2026-09-30. Design review task: [DRG-343](https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-343). Evidence identity: The 2026-09-30 refresh cited a local checkout at C:\Users\dgorn\cmano-clone\cmano-clone, HEAD 4190fb1b49cd15775b6b995b7c245d73828cd7a2, with uncommitted changes. As of 2026-11-20 that SHA is not on origin (absent from a fetched clone and from GitHub), and uncommitted working-tree changes cannot be pinned. Published main SHAs: last main tip at the time of the refresh, [1902dc12](https://github.com/drgaciw/cmano-clone/commit/1902dc1299678ea17f75014406fd9c616e5576bd) (2026-09-27, 2:40 PM CDT, #681), which this page already named as a separate target; current main [99a4d6e4](https://github.com/drgaciw/cmano-clone/commit/99a4d6e4be82dcf1bbce372caa47abef150f2b9b) (2026-11-17, 7:16 PM CT). Blob links that previously used 4190fb1b now point at the same paths on [1902dc12](https://github.com/drgaciw/cmano-clone/commit/1902dc1299678ea17f75014406fd9c616e5576bd). Refreshed against main 1902dc12 because 4190fb1b was never pushed (ruling: Decision, 2026-11-20). Planning completion does not grant product acceptance. --- ## Overview The headless simulation supplies authoritative execution; the player prepares the scenario, begins execution, delegates orders, and inspects outcomes. This page describes the implemented session/tick contract and distinguishes it from proposed session restoration. UI reads projections and submits intent through approved command seams; it does not own the simulation clock or world state. The main orchestration source is [src/ProjectAegis.Delegation/Orchestration/SimulationSession.cs](https://github.com/drgaciw/cmano-clone/blob/1902dc1299678ea17f75014406fd9c616e5576bd/src/ProjectAegis.Delegation/Orchestration/SimulationSession.cs); delegation is [src/ProjectAegis.Delegation/Orchestration/DelegationOrchestrator.cs](https://github.com/drgaciw/cmano-clone/blob/1902dc1299678ea17f75014406fd9c616e5576bd/src/ProjectAegis.Delegation/Orchestration/DelegationOrchestrator.cs). GitNexus path-qualified context calls against this exact checkout corroborated both classes, plus ReplayCheckpointStore and the delegation SeededRng. Same-name sibling indexes are not interchangeable; graph results corroborate source navigation, not runtime proof. ## Player Fantasy Command a theater at the pace needed to understand events: plan before execution, pause to inspect attention and constraints, accelerate quiet periods, then see why delegated or human orders executed or were withheld. Outcomes remain reproducible for a fixed build and input sequence. Pause freezes the interactive simulation clock; it must not be presented as a guarantee that all orchestration queues and logs stop changing. ## Detailed Rules 1. Planning versus execution. SimulationSession.Tick and TickHeadless return false in Planning before running the session. BeginExecution changes the orchestrator phase; its initial Planning-to-Executing transition appends a mode-change record. The session does not infer readiness from elapsed calendar time. 2. Outer delegation call. RunExecutingTick calls Orchestrator.Tick once with the supplied ObservedState. The orchestrator drains approved orders, evaluates active agents, and drains agent/human issued queues into ExecutedOrders. It derives its order tick from the observed SimTime; this is distinct from the pipeline clock. 3. Interactive pause. The pause check occurs after the orchestrator call. A paused executing session may therefore drain queues or emit decision/denial records while its simulation clock does not advance. Tick returns true for the executing call even when paused; that return value alone does not prove a new simulation tick. 4. Engagement and cadence. An unpaused call selects Engage orders, applies communications and salvo/deconfliction gates, enqueues requests, and calls Sim.TickOnce in RealTime mode. It logs the initial results and applies damage handling, then performs acceleration-factor-minus-one extra pipeline steps. Delegation, result logging/damage handling, and the final logistics FSM call are not repeated for every extra step by this method. Do not describe acceleration as a whole-session tick repeated uniformly. 5. Headless execution. TickHeadless selects HeadlessBatch, bypassing the pipeline pause gate while retaining the pause flag. In Planning it still returns false. Watch attention can require acknowledgement or explicit override through TryResumeSim; legacy ResumeSim bypasses that watch gate. 6. Verification checkpoints. [src/ProjectAegis.Delegation/Replay/ReplayCheckpointStore.cs](https://github.com/drgaciw/cmano-clone/blob/1902dc1299678ea17f75014406fd9c616e5576bd/src/ProjectAegis.Delegation/Replay/ReplayCheckpointStore.cs) appends strictly increasing checkpoint ticks and finds the latest at/before a requested tick. [src/ProjectAegis.Delegation/Replay/ReplayCheckpoint.cs](https://github.com/drgaciw/cmano-clone/blob/1902dc1299678ea17f75014406fd9c616e5576bd/src/ProjectAegis.Delegation/Replay/ReplayCheckpoint.cs) contains SimTick, WorldHash, LogFingerprint, and LastSequenceId. These are verification metadata, not a serialized restorable session. ## Formulas - Clock time is SimClock.SimTime = SimTick * FixedDeltaSeconds; default delta is 1/60 second. Acceleration changes the number of fixed steps, not the delta. See [src/ProjectAegis.Sim/Time/SimClock.cs](https://github.com/drgaciw/cmano-clone/blob/1902dc1299678ea17f75014406fd9c616e5576bd/src/ProjectAegis.Sim/Time/SimClock.cs). - For an executing, unpaused session call with factor F, the pipeline advances 1 + max(0, F - 1) steps. F is clamped to 1–256. The session owns this outer acceleration loop; direct pipeline Accelerated mode separately uses F steps. See [src/ProjectAegis.Sim/Core/SimTickPipeline.cs](https://github.com/drgaciw/cmano-clone/blob/1902dc1299678ea17f75014406fd9c616e5576bd/src/ProjectAegis.Sim/Core/SimTickPipeline.cs). - Delegation [src/ProjectAegis.Delegation/Decision/SeededRng.cs](https://github.com/drgaciw/cmano-clone/blob/1902dc1299678ea17f75014406fd9c616e5576bd/src/ProjectAegis.Delegation/Decision/SeededRng.cs) initializes state from global seed XOR salted agent identity, substitutes 1 for zero, applies xorshift updates (13, 7, 17), then returns (state & 0xFFFFFF) / 0x1000000. Reproducibility requires the same seed, salt, and draw order. - The separate [src/ProjectAegis.Sim/Core/SeededRng.cs](https://github.com/drgaciw/cmano-clone/blob/1902dc1299678ea17f75014406fd9c616e5576bd/src/ProjectAegis.Sim/Core/SeededRng.cs) uses seed/domain/entity/tick/draw-index hashing. Its masked uint division can include the endpoint 1.0; the two RNG contracts must not be conflated. ## Edge Cases - Calling Tick during Planning is rejected even when headless execution was requested. - Paused execution is not queue immutability; distinguish observed order time, orchestration effects, and pipeline tick progression in diagnostics. - Repeating a checkpoint tick or recording an earlier tick is ignored; an empty/before-first lookup returns no checkpoint. - A hash checkpoint cannot reconstruct pending events, RNG state, engagements, resources, or authority-bearing mission state. - Proposed RPL-29–31 require same-build/scenario/catalog/policy uninterrupted-versus-restored equality and non-mutating corrupt/incompatible-load failure. These contracts, [DRG-348](https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-348) and [DRG-349](https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-349), are gated backlog work; save/resume and multiplayer are not established by replay goldens. ## Dependencies The [cmano-clone project](https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/project/cmano-clone-7f6a00e4c1c9) links requirements 03/08/17, ADR-001 simulation boundary, ADR-003 order log, ADR-004 tick pipeline, and presentation ADR-010 sections 2–3 plus ADR-007. DelegationBridge remains zero-touch. Scenario policy, catalog, seed and ordered input identities are required context for deterministic comparisons. S122–S127 delivery follows evidence gates; [DRG-208](https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-208) remains owner Play Mode acceptance. ## Tuning Knobs Fixed delta and clock factor are existing implementation settings; factor bounds 1–256 are code constraints, not newly accepted product performance targets. Scenario-policy values govern gameplay tuning. Checkpoint frequency is chosen by the harness/caller, not persisted as a save/resume contract. Any cadence or performance change needs profiling, criterion-specific evidence and current upstream impact analysis before symbol edits; no parameter changes are authorized by this page. ## Acceptance Criteria These are review/verification criteria, not fresh execution results or owner signoff. - CS-01: verify Planning calls do not advance the pipeline; BeginExecution exposes the documented phase/log transition. Candidate source tests: SimulationSessionPhaseTests. - CS-02: verify paused interactive clock remains unchanged while separately inspecting approved/human queue and log behavior; do not accept only the Tick boolean. Candidate source tests: SimulationSessionClockControlsTests; queue/log coverage must be checked explicitly. - CS-03: compare factors 1 and greater than 1 against the documented outer/inner cadence; confirm fixed delta does not stretch. Existing clock tests are candidate mappings, not proof of uniform subsystem acceleration. - CS-04: verify headless pause override and watch acknowledgement/override behavior. Candidate source tests: SimulationSessionWatchAttentionTests. - CS-05: repeat identical build/input/seed runs and compare state/order fingerprints; retain Baltic v2 hash 17144800277401907079. Use [AGENTS.md](http://AGENTS.md) standing gates and the six canonical replay cases; recorded counts must identify revision and local delta. - CS-06: review checkpoint metadata honesty and keep RPL-29–31 proposed until schema/feasibility/ADR and differential restore tests exist. - CS-07: collect criterion-level SHA/build/local delta/scenario/catalog/policy/test-layer/result evidence and an explicit owner decision under proposed VER-07.3–6. This draft and source inspection satisfy neither Editor coverage nor owner acceptance.

wiki_pages.title: Weapons & Engagement Resolution
wiki_pages.note:
Status: Draft — source-backed design, owner review pending.

Owner: drg amtd

Related Linear Milestone: Combat Interaction UX M1 — Engage and assess; historical cmano-clone M4 context retained.

Last updated: 2026-09-30

Delivery: [DRG-344](https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-344)

--- ## Overview This draft describes the implemented headless engagement path and its presentation boundary; owner design review and product acceptance are pending. Scope covers launch permission, magazine consumption and deterministic Hit/Miss → Intercept → Kill assessment. It does not claim physical missile flight, a universal damage equation or completion of every combat-domain requirement. Evidence identity: The 2026-09-30 review cited local checkout 4190fb1b49cd15775b6b995b7c245d73828cd7a2 with uncommitted changes. As of 2026-11-20 that SHA is not on origin (absent from a fetched clone and from GitHub), and uncommitted working-tree changes cannot be pinned. Published main SHAs: last main tip at the time of the review, [1902dc12](https://github.com/drgaciw/cmano-clone/commit/1902dc1299678ea17f75014406fd9c616e5576bd) (2026-09-27, 2:40 PM CDT, #681), already named here as a distinct remote reference; current main [99a4d6e4](https://github.com/drgaciw/cmano-clone/commit/99a4d6e4be82dcf1bbce372caa47abef150f2b9b) (2026-11-17, 7:16 PM CT). The source map below was not GitHub blob or commit links, so those paths were left as-is after confirming they exist at [1902dc12](https://github.com/drgaciw/cmano-clone/commit/1902dc1299678ea17f75014406fd9c616e5576bd). Refreshed against main 1902dc12 because 4190fb1b was never pushed (ruling: Decision, 2026-11-20). Source observations below are not an owner acceptance of either revision. Source map: src/ProjectAegis.Sim/Engage/MvpEngagementResolver.cs, CombatOutcomeResolver.cs, MagazineLedger.cs, SwarmOffensiveEffect.cs, WeaponEnvelope.cs, DlzEngageGate.cs and DlzEvaluator.cs in the same Engage directory. Presentation sources are src/ProjectAegis.Delegation/CombatEvents/CombatEventLogProjection.cs, CombatEventProjection.cs and src/ProjectAegis.Delegation.UnityAdapter/Presentation/CombatMapPresentation.cs. ## Player Fantasy The commander decides whether to commit scarce weapons under ROE, fire-control, readiness and range constraints. A denied shot provides its actual refusal reason; an accepted shot consumes the real magazine ledger and yields a deterministic outcome suitable for replay and after-action review. Map effects communicate logged events without becoming combat authority. ## Detailed Rules 1. MvpEngagementResolver.Resolve checks killed shooter, killed target and context availability first. Zero unit identifiers skip their respective killed-registry check. The first failing gate returns its explicit abort result; later gates do not replace that reason. 2. Remaining prelaunch checks follow source order: speculative settings; optional policy evaluator; optional domain validator registry; air readiness; damage withdrawal; Bingo; Shotgun; spoofed track; radar EMCON; remote CEC/fire-control eligibility; usable fire-control; Winchester/magazine; combat-domain validation; hypersonic gate; inclusive weapon envelope; DLZ. Some validators are optional/configured, so do not describe every domain registry as active in every run. 3. Live rounds use tracked ledger state when present, including tracked zero; an unseeded mount falls back to context rounds for gate assessment. Launch still requires an actual seeded ledger entry with enough rounds in TryConsumeSalvo. 4. All abort paths in this resolver precede successful consumption. Failed TryConsumeSalvo leaves rounds unchanged. On success it consumes the complete normalized salvo, allocates the next engagement ID and resolves outcomes in the same invocation using the request's simulation tick. 5. Outcome order is CombatOutcomeResolver.Apply (Hit/Miss), then ApplyInterceptOnHit, then ApplyKillOnHit. Miss bypasses both later stages. Successful intercept replaces Hit with Intercept and therefore bypasses kill. Remaining Hit can become Kill. This path does not schedule a later physical flight/impact time. 6. For swarm shooters the resolver scales offensive base probability by living integrity. For a swarm target, final Hit/Kill can apply integrity damage through the injected authorized sink when target swarm metadata is present. 7. CombatEventLogProjection derives presentation phases from authoritative log rows, with sequence IDs as correlation IDs. It shows InFlight for a missile launch with no matching outcome yet; matching outcome produces TerminalOutcome. CombatEventProjection also projects InFlight when an assessed launched leg has no outcome row. These labels are visual lifecycle state, not evidence of simulated weapon kinematics. The current checkout did not contain a BattleGraphicsPresentationBridge declaration; no behavior is attributed to that unavailable source. ## Formulas Implemented formulas, verified directly in source: - Normalized salvo: n = max(1, SalvoSize). Successful ledger consumption: remaining' = remaining - n only when the mount is tracked and remaining >= n; otherwise return false without mutation. - Hit: pHit = clamp(pkBase, 0, 1); u0 = SeededRng.UnitFloat(seed, Combat, engagementId, simTick, 0); Hit iff u0 < pHit, otherwise Miss. Hit draw occurs only for a launched result. - Intercept: only when incoming outcome is Hit and clamp(pkIntercept,0,1) > 0, draw salt 1 and replace Hit with Intercept iff u1 < clamp(pkIntercept,0,1). Zero intercept probability skips the draw. - Kill: only when the remaining outcome is Hit, draw salt 2 and replace Hit with Kill iff u2 < clamp(pkKill,0,1). The kill draw is still evaluated for zero kill probability on a remaining Hit. - Swarm scale: for positive base effect, living count and maximum, effectivePkBase = pkBase * clamp(living/max,0,1); otherwise SwarmOffensiveEffect.Scale returns zero. This scaling is used only when the resolver has positive shooter maximum metadata. - Envelope: minRange <= range <= maxRange. DLZ evaluates OutOfZone below 0.9*minRange or above maxRange; Approaching above 0.85*maxRange; otherwise InZone. Early accepts InZone/Approaching, Normal accepts InZone, Late additionally requires range <= 0.7*maxRange. Resolver envelope approval precedes DLZ, so DLZ's lower tolerance does not permit a launch below the weapon minimum. These are per-engagement implementation rules, not a multiplied salvo probability, a continuous trajectory model or a general damage formula. Numerical validity and tuning changes require their own validated input contract. ## Edge Cases - Dead shooter/target and denied policy consume no rounds; competing failures expose the first source-ordered gate. - A tracked-empty mount must not be mistaken for an unseeded mount. Context ammunition alone cannot make an unseeded ledger consume successfully. - Nonpositive salvo sizes normalize to one; insufficient rounds reject the whole salvo rather than partially consume it. - Probabilities zero/one and repeated identical inputs are boundary cases. Draws are conditional, so code must not add extra random calls or use wall-clock/shared RNG. - Intercept is a terminal nonlethal outcome on this path; it must not subsequently become Kill. - Missing victim/weapon enrichment appears as explicit unknown facts in presentation. Missing outcome data may produce an InFlight label; do not invent travel time, physical position or a delayed authoritative kill from it. - Different optional gate configuration, catalog/policy inputs or local deltas require separate evidence identity. ## Dependencies Requirements: Game-Requirements/requirements/14-Engagement-And-Fire-Control.md, 18-Combat-Domains.md, and 17-Replay-AAR-And-Order-Log.md. Simulation contracts: IEngageWorldQuery, EngageContext, MagazineLedger, KilledTargetRegistry, IPolicyEvaluator, configured domain/speculative gates, SimSeed and SeededRng. Presentation follows ADR-010 §2–3, ADR-007 and ADR-001: read snapshots/projections and submit intent through approved commands. No UI/content asset becomes simulation authority. DelegationBridge remains zero-touch; existing CatalogWriteGate paths remain extend-only; Baltic v2 replay hash 17144800277401907079 remains pinned. Documentation delivery/review is [DRG-344](https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-344), with native reconciliation context Requirements, backlog and roadmap reconciliation — 2026-09-30. GitNexus evidence is qualified by exact path and source inspection because DRG-323/324 track overload/index defects and DRG-197 graph recovery. No new graph-count certainty or code-edit authorization follows from this page. ## Tuning Knobs Scenario/catalog/context inputs include weapon envelope, salvo size, effective ROE/WRA, DLZ personality, PkBase, PkIntercept, PkKill, readiness/track/EMCON state, configured speculative/domain gates and swarm integrity metadata. Gameplay configuration stays data-driven and revisioned with replay inputs. The current source contains DLZ thresholds 0.9/0.85/0.7 and a linear living-integrity scale; these are observed implementation constants, not newly approved balancing targets. A proposed nonlinear curve, new flight model, per-round salvo resolution or revised damage model needs an explicit design decision, backlog scope and deterministic regression evidence. ## Acceptance Criteria - [ ] Named owner reviews this complete eight-section draft and records approved/rejected design scope; document completion alone does not satisfy product acceptance. - [ ] Headless gate fixtures prove first-refusal reason, dead shooter/target, ROE/WRA, readiness/EMCON/fire-control, envelope/DLZ and insufficient-ammo behavior; every abort preserves rounds. - [ ] Successful normalized salvo consumes exactly its size; repeated identical seed/request/configuration produces equal outcome and recorded hit draw. - [ ] Probability boundaries and Hit → Intercept → Kill precedence are tested, including conditional intercept draw and remaining-Hit kill behavior. - [ ] Swarm scaling and authorized integrity updates are verified against the source-defined positive/zero bounds. - [ ] Presentation fixtures prove refusal visibility, explicit unknown enrichment, correlation and InFlight/TerminalOutcome projection without world/order/RNG mutation or a physical-kinematics claim. Candidate tests: src/ProjectAegis.Sim.Tests/Engage/MvpEngagementResolverTests.cs, CombatOutcomeResolverTests.cs, SwarmOffensiveEffectTests.cs; src/ProjectAegis.Delegation.Tests/CombatEvents/CombatEventLogProjectionTests.cs, CombatEventProjectionTests.cs; src/ProjectAegis.Delegation.UnityAdapter.Tests/Presentation/CombatMapPresenterTests.cs. Fresh coordinating local regression results on 2026-09-30 were 3,352 solution tests, 26 proxy smoke and six canonical replay tests, with zero failures; build zero warnings/errors using SDK 8.0.425. These broad results do not independently prove each criterion above, exact SDK 8.0.400, live Editor visuals, owner design approval or DRG-208 acceptance at 1902dc12. Record per-criterion revision/input identity and named owner decision before checking these boxes. ## Linked Linear Project: [cmano-clone](https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/project/cmano-clone-7f6a00e4c1c9) · Historical milestone: M4 — Weapons & Engagement Resolution

wiki_pages.title: Map / Rendering / UI
wiki_pages.note:
Status: Draft

Owner: drg amtd — draft review owner; owner review pending

Related Linear Milestone: Combat UX M0 / S122–S127 — source-backed design reconciliation; H5 remains gated

Last updated: 2026-09-30

--- ## Overview The tactical map is a presentation client over the headless simulation. It renders registered friendly units, log-derived contacts, alive/dead state, optional kinematic poses, and plotted courses through MapPictureBridge and immutable projection rows. Presentation boundaries are ADR-010 §2–3, ADR-007, and ADR-001. Evidence scope: The 2026-09-30 source inspection cited a local checkout at HEAD 4190fb1b49cd15775b6b995b7c245d73828cd7a2, with existing working-tree changes. As of 2026-11-20 that SHA is not on origin (absent from a fetched clone and from GitHub), and uncommitted working-tree changes cannot be pinned. Published main SHAs: last main tip at the time of the inspection, [1902dc12](https://github.com/drgaciw/cmano-clone/commit/1902dc1299678ea17f75014406fd9c616e5576bd) (2026-09-27, 2:40 PM CDT, #681); current main [99a4d6e4](https://github.com/drgaciw/cmano-clone/commit/99a4d6e4be82dcf1bbce372caa47abef150f2b9b) (2026-11-17, 7:16 PM CT). The source contracts below were not GitHub blob or commit links, so those paths were left as-is after confirming they exist at [1902dc12](https://github.com/drgaciw/cmano-clone/commit/1902dc1299678ea17f75014406fd9c616e5576bd). Refreshed against main 1902dc12 because 4190fb1b was never pushed (ruling: Decision, 2026-11-20). This is not a claim about current main or owner Play Mode acceptance. GitNexus was queried with the absolute repository path and corroborated against source because DRG-323/324 record index/overload limitations. Existing delivery includes the placeholder map host, map bridge/binder, selection controller, course projection, glyph/atlas fallback seams, and globe status host code. Full globe interaction, complete tactical symbology, and H5 content loading remain separately scoped delivery or design work; host presence does not establish product completeness. ## Player Fantasy The player reads a theater picture, selects a friendly force or contact, inspects why events occurred, and issues deliberate commands. The map must make unavailable positional evidence distinguishable from a real tracked position. Selecting or inspecting an item changes presentation context without changing authoritative simulation state. ## Detailed Rules 1. MapPictureBridge collects OOB membership from the target registry, alive state and optional kinematic poses from ISimWorldSnapshot, and contact rows from the decision-log contact projection. Rendering does not write the world or decision log. 2. Placement precedence is exact: a complete normalized X/Y pair wins; otherwise a complete latitude/longitude pair projects onto the Baltic canvas; otherwise use deterministic hash placement and set HasAuthoritativePose to false. With normalized coordinates, supplied geographic coordinates are retained when both exist; otherwise derive Baltic geographic coordinates. Normalized coordinates are not clamped by this projection. 3. Friendly and contact rows are sorted by affiliation and then symbol ID using ordinal comparison. The current basic contact path renders contacts as Hostile; it does not implement the full future affiliation/classification symbology matrix. 4. MapPanelBinder marks non-authoritative placements as unknown-pose, applies selection styling, adds stale/ghost presentation for degraded hostile contacts, and frozen styling for denied comms. These styles are presentation effects, not additional sensor truth. 5. Selecting a friendly unit clears contact selection. Selecting a hostile contact clears the friendly selection and graph highlights from the previous unit. CombatInspection is separate from the unit selection used for player commands. 6. Plotted courses omit destroyed units, absent waypoint lists, and paths with fewer than two vertices. The current pose or hash fallback is prepended unless it already matches the first waypoint. 7. Interpolation only blends matching, non-destroyed symbols with authoritative previous and current poses. New, unknown-pose, or destroyed symbols use the current row. Frame interpolation never enters authoritative clocks or order logs. 8. MapPlaceholderPanelHost binds the projected picture and routes symbol clicks through its presentation feed. Its existing atlas choice is: unavailable catalog when frames are disabled; successfully loaded local manifest catalog when preferred; otherwise the default atlas catalog. This bounded fallback does not prove the broader H5 loader or LIB-05 failure-isolation requirement is implemented. 9. Authority-changing map actions use the approved command façade under ADR-010. Camera, layout, selection, and inspection are presentation actions. Full military/civilian symbology profiles remain proposed in the two 2026-09-05 requirement drafts. ## Formulas Baltic canvas projection (existing code): ```txt x = clamp01((longitude - 24.0) / 1.5) y = clamp01((latitude - 59.5) / 1.0) latitude = 59.5 + normalizedY * 1.0 longitude = 24.0 + normalizedX * 1.5 ``` Only the latitude/longitude-to-canvas path clamps. The inverse and normalized-pose path do not add a clamp. Placeholder placement (existing code): hash the string seed:ID with DeterministicHash.OrdinalHash. For friendly units use layoutSeed; for contacts use layoutSeed + 17. Take the low 16 bits for hx and the next 16 bits for hy. ```txt x = (hx / 65535) * 0.75 + 0.1 y = (hy / 65535) * 0.75 + 0.1 ``` This places fallback markers in the interior of the canvas; it is a layout convention, not estimated geography. Presentation interpolation: for 0 ≤ t \< 1, blend each eligible coordinate as a + (b - a) \* t; negative t becomes zero, and t ≥ 1 returns current rows. Geographic values blend only when both endpoints provide them. Course first-vertex equality uses absolute X and Y differences below 1e-5. ## Edge Cases - Missing or incomplete coordinate pairs fall through the precedence rule rather than fabricating a partial authoritative pose. - Out-of-box geographic coordinates clamp to the Baltic canvas edge while retaining the original geographic values. Out-of-range normalized values are retained by MapPictureProjection; upstream validation is a separate responsibility. - Missing atlas frames must resolve through the existing glyph fallback seam. H5 will define asset delay, corruption, version mismatch, timeout/cancellation, visible diagnostics, and measured budgets for its chosen local pilot before delivery. - Ghost rows are unselected and carry ghost IDs; they must not masquerade as new authoritative contacts. - Destroyed units retain destroyed-symbol presentation and do not emit plotted courses or interpolate motion. - Inspection history may lack pose evidence. Display unavailable evidence explicitly instead of substituting a later/current pose. - Empty OOB/contact inputs produce an empty picture. Null required bridge inputs are rejected. Finite-coordinate validation is not introduced by this design refresh. ## Dependencies Current source contracts: - src/ProjectAegis.Delegation.UnityAdapter/Bridge/MapPictureBridge.cs - src/ProjectAegis.Delegation/Projection/MapPictureProjection.cs - src/ProjectAegis.Delegation/Projection/MapPanelBinder.cs - src/ProjectAegis.Delegation/Projection/MapSymbolPresentationLerp.cs - src/ProjectAegis.Delegation.UnityAdapter/Presentation/C2PresentationController.cs - unity/ProjectAegis/Assets/Scripts/Runtime/MapPlaceholderPanelHost.cs - unity/ProjectAegis/Assets/Scripts/Runtime/GlobeMapProductHost.cs — present in the pre-existing dirty working tree; no integrated-main equivalence claimed. Normative architecture: docs/architecture/adr-010-headless-first-command-driven-ui.md, docs/architecture/adr-007-c2-map-presentation.md, docs/architecture/adr-001-sim-assembly-boundary.md. Requirements: Game-Requirements/requirements/20-Command-And-Control-UI.md; Game-Requirements/drafts/2026-09-05-military-tactical-symbology.md; Game-Requirements/drafts/2026-09-05-civilian-gameplay-symbology.md; proposed LIB-05 in Game-Requirements/drafts/27-Scenario-Library-Campaigns.md. Delivery: [DRG-275 design reconciliation](https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-275), [DRG-208 owner acceptance](https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-208), [DRG-332 H5 inventory](https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-332), [DRG-331 H5 ADR](https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-331), and [DRG-347 local presentation pilot](https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-347). Related design: Core Simulation Design and Weapons & Engagement Resolution. ## Tuning Knobs layoutSeed controls placeholder layout only. ScenarioCommsDisplaySettings supplies ghost offsets and lag labels. The host frame-enable flag, manifest preference, and manifest path select the current atlas availability path. Presentation interpolation t belongs to the frame clock. Baltic box constants describe the current demo projection; making arbitrary theater bounds data-driven is a future design decision. H5 compatibility versions, timeout/cancellation policy, content class, diagnostic wording, and performance budgets remain explicit pilot decisions. Neither a 5k-symbol/60 FPS product target nor full globe fidelity is asserted by this page. ## Acceptance Criteria Existing contracts to preserve, validated here by source inspection rather than a new test run: - Same seed and IDs give stable fallback placement and ordering; a complete pose replaces fallback and sets the authoritative flag. Evidence: src/ProjectAegis.Delegation.Tests/Projection/MapPictureProjectionTests.cs and src/ProjectAegis.Delegation.UnityAdapter.Tests/Bridge/MapPictureBridgeTests.cs. - Unknown pose, selection, comms ghost/frozen styling, and atlas fallback remain observable. Evidence: src/ProjectAegis.Delegation.Tests/Projection/MapPanelBinderTests.cs. - Friendly/contact selection and previous graph highlights remain coordinated. Evidence: src/ProjectAegis.Delegation.UnityAdapter.Tests/Presentation/C2PresentationControllerTests.cs. - Combat effects resolve contact identity without changing the underlying map picture. Evidence: src/ProjectAegis.Delegation.UnityAdapter.Tests/Presentation/CombatMapIntegrationTests.cs. - Interpolation remains presentation-only and courses exclude destroyed units. Evidence: src/ProjectAegis.Delegation.Tests/Projection/MapSymbolPresentationLerpTests.cs and MapPictureProjectionTests. Pending owner/product acceptance: DRG-208 records the revision-specific Play Mode walk and individual criteria; headless proxy passes do not substitute for it. DRG-275 owns review of this draft and any corrections to the current/proposed boundary. Proposed H5 acceptance: after inventory and ADR gates, inject missing, delayed, corrupt, and version-mismatched presentation assets; show the agreed fallback/diagnostic; compare authoritative state and order-log fingerprints at identical simulation ticks. Record revision, build/catalog/scenario identity, commands, expected/actual results, and evidence links. Pilot budgets are agreed before execution; no measured pass is claimed here. ## Linked Linear Project: [cmano-clone](https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/project/cmano-clone-7f6a00e4c1c9) · Current design review: DRG-275 / Combat UX M0 / S122–S127. Original stub milestone: M5 — Map/UI Rendering (historical).

wiki_pages.title: Scenario Editor Spec
wiki_pages.note: Status: DRAFT — generated from implementation, needs owner review Owner: (unassigned) Related Linear Milestone: M6 — Scenario Editor Last updated: 2026-07-26 Provenance: Reverse-engineered from repo HEAD by automated audit; NOT an authored design doc. Verify before treating as authoritative. ## Overview The Project Aegis Scenario Editor is a headless-first authoring system over a canonical *.scenario.json document, with interchangeable front-ends. The engine-free core (src/ProjectAegis.Data/Scenario/Authoring/) owns the document DTO, loader/writer, mutation editor, disk-backed undo stack, and the deterministic Validation Engine; the one-shot verb surface is src/ProjectAegis.MissionEditor.Cli/; the long-lived in-process host is ScenarioAuthoringSession + ScenarioEditCommandBus, bound by engine-free presenters in src/ProjectAegis.Delegation.UnityAdapter/Authoring/ and rendered by a Unity EditorWindow at unity/ProjectAegis/Assets/Editor/ScenarioMapAuthoringWindow.cs. Per ADR-017 the core is the system of record and every UI is a thin front-end; per ADR-008 validation is pure, deterministic, LLM-free, and gates export/play/sample but never save. ## Player Fantasy Per design/gdd/agentic-mission-editor.md §2, the v1 fantasy is theater designer: you place the ORBAT, draw patrol zones, and lay missions and triggers on a map-first surface. The differentiator stated in the GDD is that the tool never lets you ship something broken silently — the moment a strike cannot reach its target on fuel, a patrol zone is empty, or a ferry has no destination, the editor names what, where, and how to fix it before play. The scenario is a plain, diffable artifact that replays identically. The GDD explicitly scopes the "AI staff drafts your scenario" experience to Phase 2/3 as a north star, not a v1 promise. ## Detailed Rules Authoring surfaces that exist. Three, over one contract: 1. CLI/MCP one-shot verbs (src/ProjectAegis.MissionEditor.Cli/Program.cs): scenario_create, scenario_validate, scenario_export, scenario_export_brief, scenario_publish, scenario_simulate_sample, scenario_undo, scenario_ai_scaffold, scenario_diff_summary, scenario_event_trace, plus mission_*, orbat_*, event_*, side_*, timeline_*, reference_point_upsert. 2. In-process host — ScenarioAuthoringSession.Open(path) → session.Bus verbs (PlaceUnit, MoveUnit, CloneUnit, UpsertReferencePoint, Attach{Patrol,Strike,Ferry,Support}FromSelection, CloneMission, AddFromTemplate, DeleteMission, UpsertEvent, UpsertSide, UpsertTimelineEntry, RefreshFindings), documented in docs/engineering/scenario-authoring-host.md. 3. Unity Editor window — menu Project Aegis/Scenario Map Authoring, UI in unity/ProjectAegis/Assets/UI/ScenarioEditor/ScenarioMapAuthoringPanel.uxml/.uss: sticky path/Open/Save/Rebuild/Refresh-Findings bar, ORBAT/RP/findings-code lists, a PLACE UNIT form, and a 3-vertex RP polygon upsert. Lifecycle. Place/edit → mutate → validate → export/publish. Every mutation goes through one pipeline: RequireEditVersion → CaptureUndoSnapshot → action → persist snapshot → CommitMutation (bumps editVersion by 1) → optional save → live validate. Undo is disk-backed at .undo-stack.json and cross-process. Reading is tolerant (case-insensitive, comments, trailing commas); writing is canonical camelCase with DefaultIgnoreCondition = Never. Gestures are two-phase: Begin* stages a tentative DTO, Commit* pushes through the bus, CancelGesture() discards. Save is never gated; export/publish/sample are. ScenarioPublishCommand refuses with VALIDATION_BLOCKED when ScenarioExportCommand.Prepare(...).Allowed is false, and emits a manifest with provenance tags and the embedded ReportHash. Host policy (ScenarioMapAuthoringHostPolicy.cs): catalog/domain/form chrome is always enabled; session write actions require an open session; the no-session message is "Open a scenario.json first (Browse… then Open).". Chrome rebuilds and any domain/form change call CancelGesture() so Commit can never write a stale invisible payload. Default UI-dev seed candidates, first-existing-wins: assets/data/scenarios/authoring/russia-vs-nato-baltic-ui-dev.json, then assets/data/scenarios/validation/golden_clean.json. Domain catalog constraints (ScenarioPlatformDomainCatalog.cs): four stable domains — aircraft, ships, subs, ground — with a hard-coded preset list per domain, each carrying a DefaultSideId of blue/red. GetPresets accepts aliases (air, naval, land); unknown domains return empty. SuggestUnitId emits u-{platform-slug≤24}-{n}. This is a UI preset list, not the authoritative catalog — ids resolve at validation time against the bound dbRef catalog. Agent-authored transparency. Per docs/engineering/scenario-ai-authoring-and-adjudication.md, the v1 "no-LLM contract" holds: AiAuthoringServices are deterministic heuristic stubs, enforced by NoDynamicExecutionGateTests which bans Lua packages and Reflection.Emit/Roslyn/CSharpScript/Process.Start from the authoring path. Every output carries ManifestBuilder.ProvenanceTag(Tag, Source, AgentId?, Evidence?, Hash?) with Source ∈ {user, ai, import}, surviving into the published manifest. ADR-015 (Proposed, decision due 2026-09-01) would derive an "agent-assisted / agent-authored" label from provenance — not implemented. ## Formulas Strike/ferry reachability (GDD §4.1, ADR-008), haversine in nm. combat_radius_nm is a round-trip budget and must not be doubled: ```javascript range_to_target_nm = haversine(launch_base, target) + ingress_egress_pad_nm available_radius_nm = combat_radius_nm * fuel_fraction reachable = available_radius_nm >= range_to_target_nm ``` Event-graph complexity (ADR-016): ```javascript complexity = E + sum(conditions_per_event) + C * cross_refs warn if > WARN_THRESHOLD peak_tick_density = max over ticks of (events with trigger_time_resolved == tick) warn if > DENSITY_THRESHOLD ``` Both are soft warnings and never block export. The single hard cap is 32 conditions per event → EVENT_CONDITION_CAP_EXCEEDED (Error). Live defaults in assets/data/editor/validation-config.json: pad 50 nm, fuel fraction 0.85, floor error, complexity 400, density 20, cross-ref weight 2, max conditions 32. Determinism: findings sort (Severity DESC, Code ASC, MissionId, UnitId, TargetId, Message) with a SHA-256 ReportHash (ADR-008). Seed default 42 (metadata.seed); scenario_simulate_sample defaults to 32 ticks and emits SEED=… HASH=… plus a world-state SHA-256 excluding editorState. Authoring-time fire order (EventFireOrderCalculator.cs): Time triggers rank 0, all others int.MaxValue, ties broken by event id ordinal. > OPEN QUESTION: GDD §4.2 specifies sort_key = (trigger_time_resolved, event.priority, event.id) with a designer priority field (0–1000, default 100). ScenarioEventDto has no priority field and EventFireOrderCalculator ignores it. Is the GDD formula aspirational, or is the implementation under-built? ## Edge Cases - Invalid placement / geometry. Invalid reference-point geometry still commits by design — MapAuthoringSurface + ScenarioGeometryValidity mark it IsGeometryValid=false with an InvalidReason map hint, not a Validation Engine finding. A Patrol with fewer than 3 waypoints is PATROL_ZONE_DEGENERATE (Error). - ID resolution failures. DB_MISMATCH when dbRef/dbSnapshotId resolves to no snapshot; BROKEN_REF for a ref:-prefixed id resolving to nothing; unresolved ids are skipped by reachability rather than falsely flagged. ScenarioValidateCommand.ResolveCatalog falls back to InMemoryCatalogReader.BalticPatrolFixture() when SQLite or the binding fails. - Policy / gate violations. Export, brief, publish, and sample are refused while any Error finding stands; save always succeeds. TL branch errors: TL_BRANCH_MISSING/INVALID/SNAPSHOT_MISMATCH, TL_RELEASE_TRAIN_NOT_FOUND/MISMATCH. Strike readiness: AIR_NOT_READY, STRIKE_INVALID_PLATFORM (combat_radius_nm ≤ 0). - Round-trip failures. A stale --edit-version raises ScenarioEditConflictException, code: "CONFLICT", exit 3, carrying currentEditVersion + fileHash; the guard throws before any write, so no partial state. Bus verbs return ScenarioMutationResult with CONFLICT or INVALID_OPERATION instead of throwing. save: false batches in memory — un-flushed edits are lost without session.Save(). DeleteSide does not cascade ORBAT units. - Event graph. EVENT_DEAD_TRIGGER, EVENT_UNREACHABLE_ACTION, EVENT_CONTRADICTORY, and EVENT_CIRCULAR (Tarjan SCC over ActivateMission → MissionComplete) are all Warnings. scenario_event_trace reports fired: false for nearly everything because there is no live sim state. - Agent-authored content. Reproducible stub output only; scenario_ai_scaffold refuses a blank brief (MISSING_BRIEF) and an existing --out (FILE_EXISTS). > OPEN QUESTION: GDD §5 specifies edge behaviors not found in the implemented finding catalog — the TeleportUnit export transform, the "time trigger before scenario start" warning, and the zero-distance-strike STRIKE_COLOCATED_WARNING (explicitly listed non-v1 in ADR-008). Current status was not determinable from the code read. ## Dependencies | Kind | Path | | --- | --- | | Core assembly | src/ProjectAegis.Data/Scenario/Authoring/, src/ProjectAegis.Data/Validation/ | | Presenters | src/ProjectAegis.Delegation.UnityAdapter/Authoring/ (8 files) | | CLI | src/ProjectAegis.MissionEditor.Cli/ (Program.cs, Scenario*Command.cs, Mission*Command.cs, EventCommands.cs) | | Sim policy | src/ProjectAegis.Sim/Scenario/ (ScenarioPolicyRepository, ScenarioPolicyJsonLoader, ScenarioPolicyCatalog) | | Unity host | unity/ProjectAegis/Assets/Editor/ScenarioMapAuthoringWindow.cs, Assets/UI/ScenarioEditor/ScenarioMapAuthoringPanel.uxml/.uss | | Data files | data/scenarios/scenario-document.schema.json, data/scenarios/examples/*.scenario.json, assets/data/editor/validation-config.json, assets/data/scenarios/authoring/russia-vs-nato-baltic-ui-dev.json | | ADRs | 008 (Accepted), 014 (Accepted), 016 (Accepted), 015 (Proposed), 017 (Proposed); ADR-008 depends on ADR-001/004/006 | | Docs | docs/engineering/scenario-{document-authoring,authoring-host,event-system,policy-authoring,ai-authoring-and-adjudication,mission-editor-cli}.md | ## Tuning Knobs assets/data/editor/validation-config.json — ingressEgressPadNm (20–150, default 50), fuelFraction (0.70–0.95, default 0.85), exportBlockSeverityFloor (error/warning, default error), complexityWarnThreshold (200–1000, default 400), densityWarnThreshold (10–50, default 20), crossRefWeight (1–4, default 2), maxConditionsPerEvent (fixed 32). CLI — --edit-version (required on every mutating verb); --seed / --db-ref / --policy-id on scenario_create (defaults 42 / baltic_patrol / baltic-patrol-catalog); --ticks (default 32) and --policy-dir on scenario_simulate_sample; --policy / --policy-dir / --profile ladder|ci on gauntlet_oracle_eval; --event on scenario_event_trace. Document-level — metadata.seed, metadata.tlBranch (TL-0…TL-5), metadata.maxTechnologyLevel (default 2), features.maxTimeCompression (default 256), LiveFindingsPresenter(debounceMs) (default 300, reserved/inert). ## Acceptance Criteria 1. scenario_validate --path emits passed, canExport, reportHash, findings[]; exit 1 on any blocking finding, 0 otherwise. 2. Save succeeds on a document with blocking errors; scenario_export, scenario_export_brief, scenario_publish, and scenario_simulate_sample on the same file are rejected with the same finding list. 3. Two scenario_simulate_sample runs at fixed seed and knobs produce byte-identical fire_order and identical world-state SHA-256, both emitting SEED=… HASH=…. 4. A stale --edit-version returns CONFLICT with currentEditVersion + fileHash, exit 3, with no partial write. 5. Each of the six ADR-008 v1 rules has a dedicated test asserting its code; STRIKE_UNREACHABLE carries Data["excess_nm"]. Baltic-scale validation completes in under 100 ms. 6. An event with more than 32 conditions blocks export; complexity and density breaches warn and still export; warnings are byte-identical run-to-run. 7. Committed examples in data/scenarios/examples/ and live ScenarioDocumentEditor output both conform to scenario-document.schema.json. 8. Host/presenter contracts are green headless: ScenarioEditCommandBusTests, MissionBoardPresenterTests, MapAuthoringSurfaceTests, EditModeControllerTests, LiveFindingsPresenterTests, EventGraphPresenterTests. 9. Unity panel contract: ScenarioMapAuthoringPanelUiTests pins stable UXML element names, USS token imports, and that CreateGUI loads the shipped UXML path. 10. NoDynamicExecutionGateTests fails the build on any Lua/eval/reflection-emit reference in the authoring path (ADR-014). 11. Repo gates: dotnet test ProjectAegis.sln --filter "PlayModeSmokeHarnessTests|ReplayGolden" and the /scenario-audit skill's per-scenario PASS/FAIL. > OPEN QUESTION: ADR-008 declares "exactly six v1 rules", but the shipped catalog in docs/engineering/scenario-document-authoring.md has roughly 20 codes (TL branch, fuel variants, BROKEN_REF, INCOMPATIBLE_HOST, DOCTRINE_RESOLVED, event codes). The ADR has not been amended to reflect the delivered rule set. > OPEN QUESTION: event_validate exists as EventValidateCommand but is not wired into CLI dispatch. Dead code, or an unfinished verb? --- ## Linked Linear Project: [cmano-clone](https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/project/cmano-clone-7f6a00e4c1c9) · Milestone: M6 — Scenario Editor

wiki_pages.title: 🤖 Platform Design Assistant — Spec (2026-08-04)
wiki_pages.note: Type: Design / product artifact Status: Active — companion to PE-UX productization Date: 2026-08-04 Related: [Platform Editor — UX/UI Review](https://app.notion.com/p/3aaf7cb4e4df81d2adf9cc55c4dd9dbb) · ADR-011 · doc 21 Platform Editor --- ## Decision Ship a Platform Design Assistant (proposal agent), not a second Platform Editor. | Surface | Role | | --- | --- | | Catalog | Read-only browse | | Design Assistant (Propose) | Draft future/hypothetical archetypes relative to peers | | Import | Propose → Acknowledge → Approve via CatalogWriteGate | Excel remains the write workbench (ADR-011). Assistant never commits catalog rows. --- ## Why New platforms must sit on the existing distribution (collision radius, HP, mounts, sensors, latency). wiki_pages.title: 📋 Platform Design Assistant — Skill Pack
wiki_pages.note: Parent: Platform Design Assistant — Spec (2026-08-04) Audience: Engineering + curator UX ## Skills ### 1. catalog-grounding - Input: domain, side, concept tokens - Output: ranked peers with scores/reasons - Fail closed if catalog empty ### 2. archetype-schema Allowed fields: id, name, domain, side, collisionRadiusNm, speedKn, damage.\{hp,maxHp,resilience,withdraw\}, mounts, sensors, comms\[\], links\[\] ### 3. relative-scaling - Role weights: light 0.25 · standard 0.5 · heavy 0.75 - Method: weightedToward(min, median, max) of peer set - Cite peer ids per field ### 4. provenance - docId: assistant - docTitle: Platform Design Assistant · peers {ids} ### 5. gate-policy - New ids only (plt-* unique) - Mutate-existing → out of scope; tell user to use Excel + approval path ### 6. workbook-emit - Emit DiffRow kinds: added (archetype sheets), info (basis line) - Destination: Import staging, not live tables ### 7. what-if - Flag on draft + staging chrome - Catalog preview allowed; not canonical until ApproveBatch ## Test vectors | Case | Expect | | --- | --- | | Light Surface Blue OPV | Peers include skiff/corvette/patrol; HP between min and mid | | Explicit peer pick | Uses only selected peers | | Id collision | Suffix -2, -3… | | Domain HP outlier | Warning banner |

It is consumed by MapPlaceholderPanelHost with a Unicode fallback (S27-07). - The roadmap says "Addressables / remote content design undesigned". SimulationSession (src/ProjectAegis.Delegation/Orchestration/SimulationSession.cs) has Pause, Resume, SetTimeAccelerationFactor and Tick, but no save or restore. ReplayCheckpointStore records only simTick, worldHash, logFingerprint and lastSequenceId, which is verification data, not restorable state. - The GDD already describes the target: design/gdd/simulation-core-time.md edge case "Save/load restores simTick, scenarioSeed, RNG stream counters (checkpoint + log tail)". The determinism contract is in docs/engineering/determinism-and-replay.md. - Multiplayer is out of v1: design/gdd/game-concept.md, production/stage.txt, production/release/launch/faq-draft.md. MultiplayerManager.asset is only the Unity default. - ZERO-touch wording: AGENTS.md "DelegationBridge.cs — Zero-touch through Release v1 — no hotpath changes". production/agentic/local-cloud-agent-routing.md "Zero-touch: DelegationBridge hotpath / SimulationSession unless product waiver". - Blocking: no product confirmation (save-load only vs multiplayer), no ADR, and no waiver decision. ### Standing rules (unchanged) The suite floor follows production/test-floor.json (≥1638, 0 failed). Formulas None defined in the current implementation. ## 5. Edge Cases — risks and hard-no exposure ### Top risks - H6 vs the DelegationBridge hotpath hard-no. Multiplayer order injection goes through DelegationBridge.TryEnqueueHumanOrder / TryIssuePlayerCommand, and the tick is DelegationBridge.Tick(ISimWorldSnapshot, IOrderSink). A full state snapshot would have to reach inside SimulationSession (a frozen hub). Only a replay-to-tick save driven through existing public APIs has a chance of being zero-touch. DRG-330 checks that. - H6 vs deterministic replay. Any change to order-log or checkpoint schema (ADR-003) or to tick order can move the Baltic hash. Re-blessing ReplayGolden silently is forbidden; a re-bless needs its own ADR. - H5 vs the presentation wall. Addressables APIs must stay in Unity presentation assemblies. ProjectAegis.Sim, ProjectAegis.Data and ProjectAegis.Delegation keep headless resolvers only. Sim-relevant data (catalog, scenario policy) must not load through Addressables, or the hash can drift. - H5 vs map hosts. The only Addressables consumer is MapPlaceholderPanelHost, and globe tiles live behind GlobeMapProductHost. Bulk loading needs a new loader seam, not growth in those hosts. - H4 vs CatalogWriteGate. Folding the WYSIWYG platform editor into H4 collides with ADR-011 (Excel-primary) and the extend-only gate. - Tracker drift resolved for planning. cmano-clone H4–H6 milestones now describe the September30 planning direction and retain implementation gates. wiki_pages.title: Command experience — delivery plan and acceptance package (2026-10-30)
wiki_pages.note:
Status: Implementation plan; runtime delivery blocked by unavailable development tooling. User authorized proceeding with the recommendations in this conversation. This is not product acceptance or a waiver of frozen runtime boundaries.
Review date:
Source baseline: [main 570a7f84](https://github.com/drgaciw/cmano-clone/commit/570a7f843ebffaa0ec9f2a3d9a7871d0354adc51).
Delivery system: Linear; existing story ownership and completed work are retained. ## Outcome and scope A player can notice a consequential event during accelerated play, inspect the evidence and doctrine behind a blocked action, take or return control, and understand what is known when communications degrade. One integrated scenario demonstrates the complete workflow. The same-build save/resume contract proceeds as a separate workstream. Requirements: Combat Interaction UX — Proposed Requirements and Vertical Slice and Slice G - Unity UX/UI Rebaseline and Acceptance. Later mechanics derive from Milsim Comparative Research & New Requirements — 2026-10-07. ## Source findings that change implementation scope 1. Basic doctrine provenance already exists in [DoctrineInheritanceProjection.cs](https://github.com/drgaciw/cmano-clone/blob/570a7f843ebffaa0ec9f2a3d9a7871d0354adc51/src/ProjectAegis.Delegation/Projection/DoctrineInheritanceProjection.cs). It returns a single source label, effective ROE/max-salvo labels, EMCON and an override marker. Extend this implementation; do not create a competing projection. 2. [ScenarioPolicyProfile.ResolveUnitPolicy](https://github.com/drgaciw/cmano-clone/blob/570a7f843ebffaa0ec9f2a3d9a7871d0354adc51/src/ProjectAegis.Sim/Scenario/ScenarioPolicyProfile.cs) resolves unit override, then mission, then friendly/opposing default. This read does not establish a complete per-field Side/Mission/Group/Unit cascade. Unsupported source levels must not be fabricated. 3. [ContactProvenanceState](https://github.com/drgaciw/cmano-clone/blob/570a7f843ebffaa0ec9f2a3d9a7871d0354adc51/src/ProjectAegis.Delegation/Projection/ContactProvenance.cs) contains identification confidence, freshness, age, source and comms-quality flags. It contains no downrange/cross-range uncertainty or weapon-tolerance dimensions. DRG-411 first needs source-contract verification; identity confidence is not positional uncertainty. 4. [MessageLogBridge.ProjectLive](https://github.com/drgaciw/cmano-clone/blob/570a7f843ebffaa0ec9f2a3d9a7871d0354adc51/src/ProjectAegis.Delegation.UnityAdapter/Bridge/MessageLogBridge.cs) uses the player-info-filtered view. New live notifications must consume the same permitted information; a hidden event must not leak through a balloon, sound, counter or pause. 5. The source tree already contains AttentionAssignmentForecastProjection and tests. The proposed attention-management enhancement is a reuse/UX-verification task, not evidence that a forecast subsystem is absent. 6. ADR-029 is Accepted. Its historical “Proposed” paragraphs and unmarked decision checkboxes need documentary reconciliation; the accepted header and explicit owner decisions govern H6 direction. ## Delivery sequence and traceability | Order | Existing item | Deliverable | Exit evidence | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 1 | [DRG-408](https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-408), [DRG-398](https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-398), [DRG-269](https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-269) | Shared notification/attention policy and time-command integration; approval-specific countdown is layered onto it | Category mapping, duplicate-event handling, fog filtering, replay read-only behavior, deterministic safe-stop tests | | 2 | [DRG-247](https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-247) | Take/return control and pause/resume-agent workflow | Exactly one active controller; preserved tasking; group detach/rejoin; repeat-command behavior; replay refusal | | 3 | [DRG-409](https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-409) | Extend existing doctrine provenance; command-based reset where a supported command exists | Source/effective value agree with policy resolver; unavailable source levels explicit; reset recorded and replayable | | 4 | [DRG-271](https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-271), [DRG-411](https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-411) | Stale/datalink/queued-order badges; separately gated positional-uncertainty details | Unknown differs from zero; age uses simulation time; stale selection cannot borrow another shooter/contact's facts | | 5 | [DRG-235](https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-235) | Integrated degraded-comms scenario and owner-walk evidence | Live source → projection → visible UI → command → outcome, with keyboard/pointer evidence | | Alongside | [DRG-348](https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-348) → [DRG-349](https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-349) | Save/resume contract, then implementation and differential proof | Whole candidate-world restore; journal completeness; uninterrupted/resumed equality; non-mutating failure | DRG-408 owns shared category policy; DRG-398 owns accelerated-time safe-stop integration/proof; DRG-269 owns pending-approval/DLZ behavior. This avoids three independent alert systems. No new epic duplicates Slice G or Combat UX. ## Bounded implementation contracts ### Alerts - Input is the permitted live message/event projection plus a data-driven category policy. Output is presentation state and an attention intent routed through the existing command façade. - The coordinator consumes each event identity once. Repeated panel refresh, reopening a panel or replay scrubbing must not issue duplicate pause/1x commands. - For simultaneous attention requests, proposed deterministic precedence is Pause above DropTo1x; preserve event identity and display all relevant reasons. Dismissing one alert must not clear another unresolved pause reason. - Routine duplicate grouping may reduce visual noise; it must retain occurrence counts and never suppress a newly actionable approval. - Live policy changes take effect for subsequent events; historical events do not retrigger implicitly. - At every supported acceleration, verify where the stop is observed relative to extra pipeline steps. A display-only next-frame notification is not proof that intermediate critical events are actionable. - Replay/AAR can inspect notifications but cannot mutate the recorded run. Observer commands stay disabled. - Hold prior DLZ countdown semantics until authoritative remaining-window facts are available; do not derive a firing deadline from animation. ### Control handoff - Use the existing public direct-control APIs. Preserve the exactly-one-controller invariant. - Treat agent pause independently from simulation pause and from group detachment. Do not implement “pause agent” by freezing the world or silently seizing the unit. - First demonstrate the supported suspension/resume seam and task-retention behavior. If absent, record a domain dependency rather than storing authority in a UI widget. - Repeated take/release and rejected commands must not duplicate queue entries or controller-change records. - Current badges and initial assignment are delivered dependencies to reuse. ### Doctrine and uncertainty - Keep the domain resolver as the only policy authority. Expose the source that actually resolved each supported value. - Do not claim Group inheritance or per-field inheritance merely because the proposed UI enumerates those levels. - Reset requires a real command and authoritative resulting policy; no mutation of scenario dictionaries from a host. - Identification confidence, positional uncertainty, track freshness and communications quality remain separate fields. - Unknown numeric precision or tolerance stays Unknown. Do not translate High/Medium/Low identity confidence into an ellipse. - Any later ambiguity thresholds must be domain-owned, versioned, and covered by boundary tests. Reference-product multipliers are not proof that Aegis supports them. - Live last-reported positions depend on [DRG-417](https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-417); production targetability evidence depends on [DRG-414](https://linear.app/drgamtd-workspace/issue/DRG-414). Mock providers must be labeled as fixtures. ## Candidate files for impact analysis These are discovered candidate paths, not a CMANO Surface stamp or permission to change protected hubs. | Lane | Existing anchors | Proposed additions / required investigation | | --- | --- | --- | | Alerts | src/ProjectAegis.Delegation/Projection/MessageLogProjection.cs; inspect supported time-command façade; thin host integration only after impact | | Handoff | src/ProjectAegis.Delegation/Controllers/ControllerSlot.cs; src/ProjectAegis.Delegation/Orchestration/DelegationOrchestrator.cs; unity/ProjectAegis/Assets/Scripts/Runtime/RightUnitPanelHost.cs | Read existing take/release APIs and suspension semantics; scope any missing domain command separately | | Doctrine | src/ProjectAegis.Delegation/Projection/DoctrineInheritanceProjection.cs; DoctrineInheritancePanelBinder.cs in the same folder; unity/ProjectAegis/Assets/Scripts/Runtime/DoctrineInheritancePanelHost.cs | Extend current contract and tests; verify reset command; ScenarioPolicyProfile.cs is the resolver reference | | Information quality | src/ProjectAegis.Delegation/Projection/ContactProvenance.cs; ContactProvenanceProjection.cs in the same folder | Reuse provenance for badges; discover authoritative uncertainty/tolerance sources before DRG-411 numeric presentation | | Save | src/ProjectAegis.Delegation.UnityAdapter/Baltic/BalticReplayHarness.cs | ADR-029 proposed Save/ DTO/journal/driver and shared stepper; no bridge/session edits | ## Integrated acceptance scenario Use a new isolated scenario/fixture identifier; do not alter Baltic v2 fixtures. | Step | Player observation / action | Required proof | | --- | --- | --- | | Plan | Assign an agent to a group, inspect doctrine and control ownership | Actual current source labels and controller badges | | Accelerate | Run at 1x and supported higher rates; countdown only when supported | | Intervene | Take control, pause/resume agent as supported, issue order, return | Single controller, correct tasking/group semantics, logged outcome | | Lose link | Degrade then deny communications | Stale/unknown states; queued versus rejected command distinctions; last report only from a live source | | Recover | Restore communications and review | Updated information with explicit provenance; no claim that DRG-391 reconciliation is already delivered | | Replay | Revisit the same events and attempt a command | Stable explanation; observer input rejected; no log mutation | Record build SHA, scenario/catalog/policy identity, seed, input steps, expected/actual outcomes, screenshots and failures. Keep headless tests, proxy tests, Editor evidence and owner acceptance separate. DRG-208's historical Done state is not acceptance of this new package. ## ADR and requirement reconciliation - REQ-04 contains per-phase lethal-autonomy opt-in language while ADR-023 remains Proposed. Package decision: retain existing runtime behavior, explicitly track the unmet requirement and proposed deferral; do not silently accept ADR-023 or claim opt-in is implemented. - ADR-021 accepts headless/CI-scoped mission timeline execution.
