wiki_pages.title: 🔗 Any Sensor, Best Shooter — Derived Requirements
wiki_pages.note:
Status: Draft requirements for Slice A and Slice C
Purpose: Model the separation between the source of a trusted track and the platform best able and authorized to act. --- ## Research conclusion The concept is not “every sensor can command every weapon.” It is a common C2 and fire-control network that combines compatible sensor evidence, evaluates candidate shooters, applies authority and policy, and selects or recommends the best feasible option. Public Army IAMD material describes connecting sensors, shooters, and mission command through a common network, with attention to interoperability, operational load, and resilient communications.[\[1\]](https://www.lineofdeparture.army.mil/Journals/Air-Defense-Artillery/ADA-Archive/2024-Edition/IBCS-Any-Sensor-Best-Shooter/) The Army’s fires concept also emphasizes near-real-time convergence with human decision makers overseeing AI-enabled support.[\[2\]](https://api.army.mil/e2/c/downloads/2021/10/06/869ca62b/afc-concept-for-fires-2028-oct21.pdf) --- ## Derived requirements ### ASBS-01 — Composite track and provenance The system shall construct a targetable contact from one or more compatible sensor contributions while retaining each contribution’s source, confidence, freshness, domain, and link state. ### ASBS-02 — Sensor-to-shooter eligibility The system shall evaluate candidate shooters against hard constraints: track quality, weapon compatibility, range and geometry, sensor or fire-control support, communications path, platform readiness, and current availability. ### ASBS-03 — Best-shooter recommendation The system shall rank eligible shooters using transparent mission trade-offs, including time to effect, probability of success, weapon availability, defended-asset priority, exposure, and mission commitments. It shall state why the recommended shooter is preferred and why alternatives are excluded. ### ASBS-04 — Authority and policy gate No recommendation or cross-platform pairing shall imply authorization. The system shall evaluate delegated authority, rules of engagement, escalation state, and required human approval separately from technical feasibility. ### ASBS-05 — Graceful degradation When a contribution, track, communications route, or shooter becomes stale or unavailable, the system shall identify the affected link, downgrade confidence or eligibility, and avoid presenting a false firing solution. ### ASBS-06 — Allocation and conflict management The system shall prevent incompatible or competing commitments, expose resource reservation and magazine effects, and explain a shooter’s unavailability due to a prior assignment. ### ASBS-07 — Determinism and auditability Every recommendation and final pairing shall record the input evidence, eligibility decisions, authority state, selected trade-offs, and outcome so it can be reproduced in replay and reviewed after action. --- ## Slice mapping - Slice A: ASBS-01, 02, 04, and 05 establish trusted, authorized targetability. - Slice B: consumes the selected pairing for engagement and assessment. - Slice C: ASBS-03, 06, and 07 provide recommendation, allocation, after-action review, and retasking. --- ## Acceptance scenario A contact is produced by multiple sensors. One shooter is technically feasible but lacks authority, one is unavailable due to a committed mission, and one is selected as the best authorized option. The player can inspect each decision and see the system change its recommendation when a link becomes stale. --- ## Sources - [Army IBCS overview](https://www.lineofdeparture.army.mil/Journals/Air-Defense-Artillery/ADA-Archive/2024-Edition/IBCS-Any-Sensor-Best-Shooter/) - [Army concept for fires](https://api.army.mil/e2/c/downloads/2021/10/06/869ca62b/afc-concept-for-fires-2028-oct21.pdf) - [Air Force test perspective](https://www.505ccw.acc.af.mil/News/Article/2355284/605-tes-testing-effort-crucial-to-ensure-abms-real-time-to-any-shooter-and-any/)

wiki_pages.title: 🛡️ IBCS-Informed Combat C2 Framework — Derived Requirements
wiki_pages.note:
Status: Draft requirements
Purpose: Use public IBCS principles as an architectural lens for the game’s combat command-and-control experience; this is not a simulation of a real operational system. --- ## Architectural interpretation Public Army material characterizes IBCS as a common mission-command and fire-control capability that integrates sensors and effectors over a network, develops composite tracks, supports flexible task organization, and maintains resilience rather than binding a crew, sensor, and shooter into a single platform. It is therefore a strong frame for a game C2 layer: common picture, composable forces, positive control, explainable pairing, and graceful degradation.[\[1\]](https://www.army.mil/article/290087/ibcs_and_the_future_of_offensive_and_defensive_integrated_fires) [\[2\]](https://asc.army.mil/web/access-st-from-concept-to-reality/) [\[3\]](https://rdl.train.army.mil/catalog-ws/view/100.ATSC/C01CC9C1-DA1C-4D5E-A6EB-5FCFAE218DCD-1398170439966/FM_3_01wc1.pdf) --- ## Derived requirements ### IBCS-01 — Common integrated picture The C2 layer shall present a coherent contact picture composed from compatible sensor contributions while preserving provenance, confidence, freshness, and disagreement. ### IBCS-02 — Decoupled, composable force elements Sensors, shooters, relays, and C2 nodes shall be independently modeled and dynamically grouped into a mission package; the UI shall show the current package and each member’s role. ### IBCS-03 — Fire-control quality and compatibility The system shall distinguish general awareness from the evidence quality required for a specific engagement. A proposed pairing must state its sensor, weapon, guidance, and communications compatibility. ### IBCS-04 — Best-resource allocation The system shall rank eligible shooters and available weapons by transparent mission criteria, while conserving scarce resources and respecting existing commitments. ### IBCS-05 — Positive control and delegated authority Technical feasibility shall never be treated as authority. The UI shall separately display command relationship, delegation, ROE, required approval, and abort authority. ### IBCS-06 — Network health and graceful degradation The C2 picture shall expose links, relays, latency or staleness, partitioning, and rerouting where modeled. A degraded network shall reduce confidence or availability rather than silently presenting a complete picture. ### IBCS-07 — Resilient operations If a sensor, shooter, or C2 node is lost, the system shall re-evaluate the mission package, preserve auditable last-known state, and surface alternatives without fabricating capability. ### IBCS-08 — Mission-tailored task organization The player shall be able to compose or inspect layered, cross-domain defense or mission groups and see coverage, gaps, commitments, and the effect of moving an element. ### IBCS-09 — Explainable automation and human oversight Automation may fuse, rank, and recommend; it shall identify evidence, assumptions, confidence, and policy gates. Human approval points must be visible where required. ### IBCS-10 — Mission-thread verification Deterministic scenarios shall verify normal, degraded-link, lost-node, conflicting-allocation, and authority-withheld cases from contact formation through assessment and retasking. --- ## Slice mapping - Slice A: IBCS-01, 03, 05, 06, and 07 establish a trusted and governed targeting picture. - Slice B: IBCS-03 and 04 feed engagement selection and assess actual effect. - Slice C: IBCS-02, 04, 08, and 09 support mission packages, recommendations, and retasking. - Cross-cutting verification: IBCS-10 provides the scenario matrix. --- ## Sources - [Army IBCS and integrated fires overview](https://www.army.mil/article/290087/ibcs_and_the_future_of_offensive_and_defensive_integrated_fires) - [Army IBCS architecture overview](https://asc.army.mil/web/access-st-from-concept-to-reality/) - [Army doctrine on composite tracks and preferred shooters](https://rdl.train.army.mil/catalog-ws/view/100.ATSC/C01CC9C1-DA1C-4D5E-A6EB-5FCFAE218DCD-1398170439966/FM_3_01wc1.pdf)

wiki_pages.title: 🤖 Agentic Combat Capabilities — Proposed Requirements
wiki_pages.note:
Status: Draft — architecture alignment in progress
Purpose: Make agentic skills a first-class gameplay capability while preserving deterministic simulation, authority controls, and replay. --- ## Requirements ### AGC-01 — Agent-callable tactical skills Tactical assessment, recommendation, coordination, information routing, emissions management, and explanation shall be exposed as named, discoverable, capability-scoped skills invocable by authorized AI models. ### AGC-02 — Deterministic boundary The simulation shall remain authoritative for world state, sensor and data-link facts, policy gates, engagement authority, and replay. Agentic skills consume projections and submit bounded proposals or commands through approved interfaces. ### AGC-03 — Authority and override Every agentic proposal shall identify its authority basis, required approval, and player override path. A recommendation shall never imply engagement authorization. ### AGC-04 — Evidence and explanation Each skill invocation shall record its skill identity, inputs, evidence, assumptions, rationale, output, and relevant simulation time so its decision can be inspected and replayed. ### AGC-05 — Degraded-mode disclosure If an agent, model, or required skill is unavailable, the UI shall disclose the condition and apply an explicit fallback policy. The game shall not silently substitute undisclosed decision behavior. ### AGC-06 — Data-link and IBCS skills The data-link and integrated-fire-control layers shall expose skills for track assessment, sensor-to-shooter pairing, best-resource recommendation, network-health reasoning, mission-package coordination, and human-readable explanation. ### AGC-07 — Verification Deterministic scenarios shall test normal, stale-data, network-partition, authority-withheld, resource-conflict, and model-unavailable cases. --- ## Slice mapping - Slice A: track assessment, authority, data-link health, and pairing proposals. - Slice B: bounded engagement recommendation and explanation. - Slice C: coordination, allocation, after-action learning, and retasking. --- ## Architecture alignment The repository ADR will define the authoritative simulation boundary, the skill contract, provenance and replay requirements, player control, and degraded-mode behavior. This page remains the design and acceptance source.

wiki_pages.title: 🧪 QA Gauntlet Architecture — Requirements and Delivery Sequence
wiki_pages.note: ## Purpose Evolve the QA Gauntlet into a traceable combat-quality system that verifies deterministic simulation truth, command-and-control decisions, player-facing presentation, and agentic resilience across all three delivery slices. ## Architectural principles - The deterministic simulation remains authoritative for world state and replay. - Executable scripts and formal oracles own pass or fail; agents may plan, generate, diagnose, and propose remediation but cannot override a hard gate. - Test contracts must consume simulation projections and typed evidence, never recreate tactical decision logic. - Every requirement must trace to a specialist, test layer, scenario, oracle, and evidence artifact. ## Requirements ### GNT-01 — Specialist capability routing The Gauntlet coordinator shall route work to mission-thread, agentic-resilience, and combat-UI/replay specialists based on changed capability and delivery slice. ### GNT-02 — Versioned test-capability manifest A machine-readable manifest shall map each combat requirement to test owner, assurance layer, scenario, oracle, evidence, and delivery status. Validation shall detect orphaned required capabilities. ### GNT-03 — Typed mission-thread evidence The system shall publish versioned, typed evidence for contact state, provenance, authority, data-link state, recommendation, engagement, and assessment. Existing fingerprint gates remain during migration. ### GNT-04 — Three-layer oracle model The Gauntlet shall independently assess simulation truth and replay, decision and authority correctness, and player-presentation correctness. ### GNT-05 — Agentic resilience and regression resistance Deterministic test campaigns shall cover stale or conflicting data, partitioned links, lost nodes, withheld authority, resource conflict, and unavailable skills or models. They shall include relevant property and mutation tests. ### GNT-06 — Impact-aware execution Focused pull-request checks shall be selected from GitNexus impact plus manifest mappings, with conservative fallbacks. Full baseline and release regression remain separate evidence paths. ### GNT-07 — Combat presentation release gates Replay, accessibility, declutter, and usability checks shall be explicit release gates. They must validate weapon-family recognition, non-color accessibility, event-to-render correspondence, zoom behavior, and player comprehension. ### GNT-08 — Unified evidence ledger A run shall correlate requirement, scenario, replay, oracle outcome, CI result, and defect follow-up in a retained, inspectable record. ## Delivery sequence 1. Active foundation: integrate the three Gauntlet specialist skills. 2. Next enabling work: capability manifest. 3. Then: typed mission-thread evidence and evidence ledger. 4. Then: three-layer oracle contracts. 5. Later hardening: resilience, property and mutation campaigns; impact-aware selection; presentation release gates. ## Linear delivery record - Gauntlet architecture and combat-quality evidence is the parent epic. - The active specialist integration is first; the remaining work stays in the backlog in dependency order. - GitNexus reindexing remains a post-integration closeout activity, rather than a prerequisite for current implementation. ## Success condition A combat change can be traced from requirement through deterministic scenario and authority reasoning to player presentation, replay, CI evidence, and any resulting defect work.
